* * *
_**" The contractors who are willing to change with us will prosper and grow. Those who don't -- and resist it -- will be gone."**_
That quote is the Deputy Secretary of Defense talking to a room full of defense company executives.
Not a hedge fund manager addressing his portfolio companies -- anymore. Not a private equity partner at an investor day. _The second-highest official at the United States Department of Defense, with almost a trillion dollars in taxpayer money behind him, talking like a mob boss._
The distinction should matter more than it apparently does, because the man who said it built his entire career erasing that distinction, and he is now doing the same thing to the Pentagon.
## **Who is talking**
**Stephen Feinberg** co-founded Cerberus Capital Management in 1992 and ran it for over three decades, growing it into a roughly $65-70 billion alternative investment firm with deep holdings across credit, real estate, and private equity. Bloomberg puts his net worth at about $5.3 billion. During the first Trump administration, he chaired the President's Intelligence Advisory Board from 2018 to 2021 -- while still leading Cerberus.
He contributed over $2 million to organizations aligned with the President. Then got nominated for this position. (Hmm.) He was confirmed by the Senate 59-40 on March 14, 2025, and sworn in three days later as the 36th Deputy Secretary of Defense.
He did not arrive alone. **Four former Cerberus partners and managing directors followed him into the building** now unofficially rebranded, by executive order, the Department of War. One of them, Tomas Rakusan, previously ran the CIA's clandestine service before becoming a Cerberus managing director. As of recent reporting, at least two had not filed the ethics disclosures required by the Office of Government Ethics.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3260111&post_id=209082532&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA5MDgyNTMyLCJpYXQiOjE3ODU1MDcyODgsImV4cCI6MTc4ODA5OTI4OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTMyNjAxMTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.g1zRInehXB8nOtbBeURQl8OIHWI3JZfcXnDUFEHFOHQ)
## **What "reform" looks like**
Feinberg has built an Economic Defense Unit inside the Pentagon, reporting directly to him, tasked with accelerating weapons production and reorganizing the defense industrial base to compete with China. He has centralized authority under designated program managers. He has pushed contractors toward loans, equity stakes, and investment-style financing tools instead of traditional procurement. This is not vague "business experience" brought into government. It is a private equity operating model, transplanted whole, complete with the vocabulary: deal teams, portfolio thinking, and a public ultimatum to the vendors -- change with us and prosper, resist and disappear.
Some of that pressure is deserved. Major defense contractors have spent decades delivering programs late, over budget, and under-tested, while pouring money into Congressional races to ensure little oversight, facing virtually no consequence. A push for performance is not the problem.
But this isn't pressure applied in the _public_ 's interests - but in private ones.
## **The case that makes it concrete**
Since 2023, Ligado Networks -- a satellite and telecom company backed by Cerberus -- has been suing the Department of Defense for $40 billion, one of the largest lawsuits ever filed against the federal government.
The dispute goes back to a 2020 decision by the FCC to let Ligado repurpose a wireless spectrum license, over the objection of the Defense Department, the Department of Transportation, and the Department of Commerce, all of which warned it could interfere with military satellite systems and GPS. A National Academies of Sciences study, ordered by Congress, later confirmed the risk was real. _Somehow_ , the FCC approved it anyway -- but the Pentagon didn't let it end there.
The DOD went to Congress and got language written into the must-pass defense authorization bill, which that year (2021) Congress passed _over Trump 's veto_, that effectively barred Ligado from ever doing business with the federal government again. That legislative blacklist made the license worthless no matter what the FCC had approved.
Ligado went bankrupt. It sued, claiming the government had gone further still, using or depending on spectrum adjacent to Ligado's without ever paying for it. A federal appeals court allowed the case to proceed.
Now, Feinberg is no longer running Cerberus. _He is running the Pentagon, which Ligado, backed by Cerberus, is suing for $40 billion_. And recent court filings suggest the two sides may be nearing a settlement.
If the government settles or loses, Cerberus stands to collect a share of the proceeds -- by Feinberg's own written admission to the Senate. Those proceeds would flow into irrevocable trusts that hold **his** Cerberus assets. The trusts are controlled **by his adult children.** They are managed, in part, by a senior Cerberus managing director and by Cerberus's own outside counsel.
This is not a hypothetical conflict of interest. It is a pending multibillion-dollar payout, sitting on the desk of the man whose Pentagon is negotiating it.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9tZWxpc3NhNGNvbmdyZXNzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.395nUkIjQQ2BehSsrlo2-GPCArZVVMxMEIk8N2YzOps?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=209082532)
## **And it isn 't isolated**
Cerberus-backed companies have also been winning contracts tied to Golden Dome, the missile defense program the Congressional Budget Office estimates will cost more than $1 trillion over the next two decades -- and which falls squarely under Feinberg's purview. Just this month, the Missile Defense Agency awarded a contract to Cerberus-backed _Eos Energy Enterprises_ for battery storage systems.
Earlier this year, Cerberus acquired an aerospace manufacturer specifically, in the company's own words, "to support its national security and space portfolio." This is a live, ongoing pattern of the _same firm 's holdings intersecting the same official's authority,_ not a one-time legacy entanglement left over from a previous life.
## **The letter of the ethics agreement, and the spirit of it**
When he was nominated, Feinberg pledged in writing to divest all of his interests in Cerberus -- equity, carried interest, incentive fees, capital commitments, all of it. What actually happened was narrower: **those interests moved into trusts for his children, run in part by his former colleagues**.
In January 2026, he amended his ethics agreement - again. The amendment explicitly acknowledges that he intends to keep contracting with Cerberus for "administrative services" -- tax compliance, accounting. It lists, by name, the funds and boards he's resigning from. It does not mention the Ligado lawsuit at all.
Senator Elizabeth Warren has pressed him on exactly this gap, in writing, more than once -- before his confirmation vote and again this spring -- asking him to sever his financial ties entirely, extend his recusal for the length of his Pentagon service, and reject any ethics waivers. The Pentagon's position is that Feinberg follows the law and has no conflicts. Both things can be true only if the law's definition of "conflict" is much narrower than most people's.
## **It is -- and here's the standard that actually applies**
There is a real, binding federal rule that speaks directly to this: **executive branch employees must avoid not just actual violations of ethics law, but the** _**appearance**_**of one, judged by whether a reasonable, informed person would question their impartiality.** A related regulation specifically addresses relationships with a former employer.
But there's a legal seam here, and it's the seam this whole arrangement is built to fit through. The narrower criminal conflict-of-interest statute generally does not automatically treat an adult child's financial interest as the parent's own. So a transfer to a trust for one's children can clear the highest bar -- actual criminal liability -- while still failing the lower, older, plainer-English bar: would a reasonable person, looking at all of this, think something's off?
The regulations acknowledge that second question exists. They also give agency ethics officials the power to decide the appearance problem is outweighed by the government's interest in keeping the person anyway.
The appearance standard is real. Its enforcement is discretionary. That combination is, itself, the story.
[Melissa Chaudhry for Congress](https://substack.com/redirect/9b4f59d9-a666-4a40-bb96-8a39a50ccdcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
## **What this actually is**
Strip away the legal vocabulary and there are three separate conflicts stacked on top of each other.
A **financial** one: Pentagon decisions can increase the value of assets held in trust for his own children.
An **informational** one: divestment doesn't erase three decades of knowledge about Cerberus's holdings, strategies, and vulnerabilities -- that knowledge doesn't sit in a brokerage account, it sits in his head.
And an **institutional** one, which is the one that should worry every taxpayer regardless of party: a private equity fund exists to generate returns for its investors. The Department of Defense -- or the Department of War, if you prefer the sign on the building -- exists to protect the country, answer to the Constitution and Congress, and responsibly spend the public's money. (Right?)
**Those are not the same job,** and the habits of one do not transfer safely into the other.
A department tasked with responsible national defense shouldn't be run like a Wall Street hedge fund behind the scenes.
## **Who 's supposed to be watching**
Congressional oversight of exactly this kind of arrangement runs through the House Armed Services Committee. Its ranking Democrat is **Adam Smith** -- my opponent in this race, and the incumbent for WA-09 since 1997. _I 'd genuinely like to know what oversight has actually happened here, because from where I sit, the silence has been loud._
And this is personal to me. My father and my husband are both disabled US Military veterans. When they signed up to serve in uniform, they did so honorably, under the _**reasonable impression**_ that they were signing up to support and protect the Constitution of the United States and defend the country they loved. To have a Wall Street billionaire now hijacking and redirecting taxpayer money intended to further _that_ mission, for his own family's enrichment? _Just when I thought this regime couldn 't go any lower._
I'm running on no corporate PACs, no foreign interests, [no defense contractors](https://substack.com/redirect/840d4675-52b0-4c0d-821b-e69d27bd3ef6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). This is **exactly** the kind of story that slogan is meant to prevent: a system where the people writing the rules and the people profiting from them are close enough that "appearance of impartiality" stops being a hypothetical and starts being a live, trillion-dollar question.
Before we hand this arrangement more of the public's money, we're owed full disclosure, real recusal, and someone in Congress willing to ask the plain question instead of the polite one: **who, exactly, stands to profit?
**

Can we spell "conflict of interest" - with our servicemembers' lives on the line? | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? A Wall Street billionaire is now running procurement for the DOD...over the industry in which he made his fortune. Can we spell "conflict of interest" - with our servicemembers' lives on the line? | | | Jul 31 | | | | | | | | | | | | Folks, I 'm launching a new layer of "It's a Matter of Integrity." This is a place for deeper dives, more unsparing looks, and insight into what I really think. It's called "Melissa Unfiltered." All posts there will be paywalled. I do this work intensively, I care about it deeply, and I bring over 20 years ' experience to bear to provide maximum value to you. If you 're already a paid subscriber, thank you! You'll have automatic access to this. Everyone else - here 's our Election Week special. 20% off annual plans forever, for access into this deeper layer of my work. I 'd love to see you there. " The contractors who are willing to change with us will prosper and grow. Those who don't -- and resist it -- will be gone." That quote is the Deputy Secretary of Defense talking to a room full of defense company executives. Not a hedge fund manager addressing his portfolio companies -- anymore. Not a private equity partner at an investor day. The second-highest official at the United States Department of Defense, with almost a trillion dollars in taxpayer money behind him, talking like a mob boss. The distinction should matter more than it apparently does, because the man who said it built his entire career erasing that distinction, and he is now doing the same thing to the Pentagon. Who is talking Stephen Feinberg co-founded Cerberus Capital Management in 1992 and ran it for over three decades, growing it into a roughly $65-70 billion alternative investment firm with deep holdings across credit, real estate, and private equity. Bloomberg puts his net worth at about $5.3 billion. During the first Trump administration, he chaired the President's Intelligence Advisory Board from 2018 to 2021 -- while still leading Cerberus. He contributed over $2 million to organizations aligned with the President. Then got nominated for this position. (Hmm.) He was confirmed by the Senate 59-40 on March 14, 2025, and sworn in three days later as the 36th Deputy Secretary of Defense. He did not arrive alone. Four former Cerberus partners and managing directors followed him into the building now unofficially rebranded, by executive order, the Department of War. One of them, Tomas Rakusan, previously ran the CIA's clandestine service before becoming a Cerberus managing director. As of recent reporting, at least two had not filed the ethics disclosures required by the Office of Government Ethics. What "reform" looks like Feinberg has built an Economic Defense Unit inside the Pentagon, reporting directly to him, tasked with accelerating weapons production and reorganizing the defense industrial base to compete with China. He has centralized authority under designated program managers. He has pushed contractors toward loans, equity stakes, and investment-style financing tools instead of traditional procurement. This is not vague "business experience" brought into government. It is a private equity operating model, transplanted whole, complete with the vocabulary: deal teams, portfolio thinking, and a public ultimatum to the vendors -- change with us and prosper, resist and disappear. Some of that pressure is deserved. Major defense contractors have spent decades delivering programs late, over budget, and under-tested, while pouring money into Congressional races to ensure little oversight, facing virtually no consequence. A push for performance is not the problem. But this isn't pressure applied in the public 's interests - but in private ones. The case that makes it concrete Since 2023, Ligado Networks -- a satellite and telecom company backed by Cerberus -- has been suing the Department of Defense for $40 billion, one of the largest lawsuits ever filed against the federal government. The dispute goes back to a 2020 decision by the FCC to let Ligado repurpose a wireless spectrum license, over the objection of the Defense Department, the Department of Transportation, and the Department of Commerce, all of which warned it could interfere with military satellite systems and GPS. A National Academies of Sciences study, ordered by Congress, later confirmed the risk was real. Somehow , the FCC approved it anyway -- but the Pentagon didn't let it end there. The DOD went to Congress and got language written into the must-pass defense authorization bill, which that year (2021) Congress passed over Trump 's veto, that effectively barred Ligado from ever doing business with the federal government again. That legislative blacklist made the license worthless no matter what the FCC had approved. Ligado went bankrupt. It sued, claiming the government had gone further still, using or depending on spectrum adjacent to Ligado's without ever paying for it. A federal appeals court allowed the case to proceed. Now, Feinberg is no longer running Cerberus. He is running the Pentagon, which Ligado, backed by Cerberus, is suing for $40 billion. And recent court filings suggest the two sides may be nearing a settlement. If the government settles or loses, Cerberus stands to collect a share of the proceeds -- by Feinberg's own written admission to the Senate. Those proceeds would flow into irrevocable trusts that hold his Cerberus assets. The trusts are controlled by his adult children. They are managed, in part, by a senior Cerberus managing director and by Cerberus's own outside counsel. This is not a hypothetical conflict of interest. It is a pending multibillion-dollar payout, sitting on the desk of the man whose Pentagon is negotiating it. And it isn 't isolated Cerberus-backed companies have also been winning contracts tied to Golden Dome, the missile defense program the Congressional Budget Office estimates will cost more than $1 trillion over the next two decades -- and which falls squarely under Feinberg's purview. Just this month, the Missile Defense Agency awarded a contract to Cerberus-backed Eos Energy Enterprises for battery storage systems. Earlier this year, Cerberus acquired an aerospace manufacturer specifically, in the company's own words, "to support its national security and space portfolio." This is a live, ongoing pattern of the same firm 's holdings intersecting the same official's authority, not a one-time legacy entanglement left over from a previous life. The letter of the ethics agreement, and the spirit of it When he was nominated, Feinberg pledged in writing to divest all of his interests in Cerberus -- equity, carried interest, incentive fees, capital commitments, all of it. What actually happened was narrower: those interests moved into trusts for his children, run in part by his former colleagues. In January 2026, he amended his ethics agreement - again. The amendment explicitly acknowledges that he intends to keep contracting with Cerberus for "administrative services" -- tax compliance, accounting. It lists, by name, the funds and boards he's resigning from. It does not mention the Ligado lawsuit at all. Senator Elizabeth Warren has pressed him on exactly this gap, in writing, more than once -- before his confirmation vote and again this spring -- asking him to sever his financial ties entirely, extend his recusal for the length of his Pentagon service, and reject any ethics waivers. The Pentagon's position is that Feinberg follows the law and has no conflicts. Both things can be true only if the law's definition of "conflict" is much narrower than most people's. It is -- and here's the standard that actually applies There is a real, binding federal rule that speaks directly to this: executive branch employees must avoid not just actual violations of ethics law, but the appearanceof one, judged by whether a reasonable, informed person would question their impartiality. A related regulation specifically addresses relationships with a former employer. But there's a legal seam here, and it's the seam this whole arrangement is built to fit through. The narrower criminal conflict-of-interest statute generally does not automatically treat an adult child's financial interest as the parent's own. So a transfer to a trust for one's children can clear the highest bar -- actual criminal liability -- while still failing the lower, older, plainer-English bar: would a reasonable person, looking at all of this, think something's off? The regulations acknowledge that second question exists. They also give agency ethics officials the power to decide the appearance problem is outweighed by the government's interest in keeping the person anyway. The appearance standard is real. Its enforcement is discretionary. That combination is, itself, the story. What this actually is Strip away the legal vocabulary and there are three separate conflicts stacked on top of each other. A financial one: Pentagon decisions can increase the value of assets held in trust for his own children. An informational one: divestment doesn't erase three decades of knowledge about Cerberus's holdings, strategies, and vulnerabilities -- that knowledge doesn't sit in a brokerage account, it sits in his head. And an institutional one, which is the one that should worry every taxpayer regardless of party: a private equity fund exists to generate returns for its investors. The Department of Defense -- or the Department of War, if you prefer the sign on the building -- exists to protect the country, answer to the Constitution and Congress, and responsibly spend the public's money. (Right?) Those are not the same job, and the habits of one do not transfer safely into the other. A department tasked with responsible national defense shouldn't be run like a Wall Street hedge fund behind the scenes. Who 's supposed to be watching Congressional oversight of exactly this kind of arrangement runs through the House Armed Services Committee. Its ranking Democrat is Adam Smith -- my opponent in this race, and the incumbent for WA-09 since 1997. I 'd genuinely like to know what oversight has actually happened here, because from where I sit, the silence has been loud. And this is personal to me. My father and my husband are both disabled US Military veterans. When they signed up to serve in uniform, they did so honorably, under the reasonable impression that they were signing up to support and protect the Constitution of the United States and defend the country they loved. To have a Wall Street billionaire now hijacking and redirecting taxpayer money intended to further that mission, for his own family's enrichment? Just when I thought this regime couldn 't go any lower. I'm running on no corporate PACs, no foreign interests, . This is exactly the kind of story that slogan is meant to prevent: a system where the people writing the rules and the people profiting from them are close enough that "appearance of impartiality" stops being a hypothetical and starts being a live, trillion-dollar question. Before we hand this arrangement more of the public's money, we're owed full disclosure, real recusal, and someone in Congress willing to ask the plain question instead of the polite one: who, exactly, stands to profit? Care. Courage. clean_body: In just one week of organizing, we've moved within 8 signatures of forcing a vote on the Dream & Promise Act. | | | Peter, One week ago, we told you about the discharge petition moving through the House of Representatives to force a vote on the Dream & Promise Act — the bill that would ensure citizenship for DACA recipients, immigrant youth, TPS holders, and those with Deferred Enforced Departure (DED). Today, we have big news: 210 Members of Congress have signed. We are just 8 signatures away from the 218 we need. Our momentum didn't come from nowhere. Every call, every letter, and every person is moving us closer to a vote. When we come together, we make the impossible possible — and this week proved it. This is only the beginning. Next comes the vote on the Dream & Promise Act in the House. Then we move to the Senate. We won't get tired, get quiet, or stop building towards a future where all working people can thrive. Our communities have come too far and built too much to slow down now. That is the amount of money Elon Musk plans to spend in order to help Republicans win in the midterm elections this November. That includes Michigan - where control of the House and Senate runs through Michigan — with what will be some of the closest and most expensive campaigns in the country.
**$0**
That is how much money the Democratic nominees for House and Senate in several critical races will have in the bank after spending down to virtually nothing in order to win their primary elections on Tuesday.

That is the contribution I am asking you to make to the Michigan Democratic Party today. The Party can and will be ready to defend our Democratic nominees on DAY ONE, but only if they have the resources to get it done.

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. clean_body: With less than a week until Michigan’s primary elections, AIPAC and corporate PACs are spending over $50 million to buy a Senate seat. | | | Friend, With less than a week until Michigan’s primary elections, AIPAC and corporate PACs are spending over $50 million to buy a Senate seat because they’re scared of Abdul El-Sayed winning. Abdul is pushing to end Big Money in politics, stop investing our taxpayer dollars into bombing kids abroad, and instead invest in our kids here. Like me, Abdul has never and will never take money from corporate PACs. That’s also true of our friend Donavan McKinney, who’s running for the House of Representatives in the district next to mine. Like Abdul, Donavan’s also running against a genocide-enabling candidate — incumbent Shri Thanedar, who’s gotten millions from AIPAC and corporate PACs. Abdul literally wrote the book on Medicare for All, and all three of us are leading the fight for guaranteed healthcare. We’re all long-time activists and champions for economic and environmental justice. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately, split evenly between Rashida Tlaib, Abdul El-Sayed, and Donavan McKinney | | | | | | | | | | AIPAC’s funders have spent over $30 million to prop up their genocide-supporting Senate candidate Haley Stevens, who’s running against Abdul. This is the most AIPAC has ever spent on an electoral race , and it’s an all-time record for a single organization in one congressional primary election.** AIPAC hides behind front groups to flood voters with lies and Islamophobic ads that don’t mention Israel — so most voters don’t even know these ads come from AIPAC. Haley has also voted to fund and thank ICE, and so has Donavan’s opponent Shri Thanedar. Shri even takes money from ICE contractors. Meanwhile, Donavan and Abdul want to abolish ICE, as do I. Haley and Shri’s other corporate backers include private healthcare and polluters such as our greedy utility monopoly DTE. Haley’s backed by banks, weapons corporations, and BlackRock — a major funder of the fossil fuel industry. Shri has millions of dollars in crypto stock and takes money from crypto PACs, even though he’s on a congressional committee that’s supposed to regulate crypto corporations. He’s spent about $30 million of his own wealth on his electoral races, and he doesn’t show up for his constituents, who often call my office for support instead. Meanwhile, Donavan has been showing up for the people as a union organizer and a state legislator. In the State House, he has funded universal pre-K and secured $600 million to get lead out of our water. And as a public health director, Abdul has also removed lead from schools, in addition to spearheading a program that will cancel up to $700 million in medical debt, providing thousands of free glasses for kids, and supporting Black maternal and infant health. What happens on Tuesday matters for the next six years, the length of a Senate term. Thank you for acting to save lives now and for the future. Together we’ll keep fighting to get corporate money out of politics and build a democracy and economy that work for working people. name: Lizzie Fletcher
subject: July Is Almost Over
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS
body:
ELIZABETH PANNILL FLETCHER FOR CONGRESS [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP10/1/82676/images/Non-Re-Elect%20Logo.png]
As a Houstonian, I am not sure I have ever before said that I am “so ready for August.” But I am. July has been a hard month. More senseless and heartbreaking violence—including ICE killing one of our neighbors here at home in Houston and another person in Maine the following week. The war in Iran rages on without the consent of the people, and more American servicemembers have died. The President of the United States has continued his attack on our voting rights, delivering another rambling, incoherent speech full of lies. And every day, piece by piece, systems that should be working for the American people are being dismantled before our eyes. It's a sobering reminder of what's at stake—and of why this work matters.
August is usually the hardest month of the year in Houston. It’s just too darn hot. But we are starting August with an incredible reminder of what we can accomplish when we work together: our Democracy Summer fellows are kicking off the month with a big Day of Action [https://www.mobilize.us/fletcherforcongress/event/991411/] . And a ton of people have signed up.
For me, it is a reminder of all the good people who are working to make a difference for people in our community and across our country, even if it means going out in Houston in August to knock on doors and give people the information they need to vote.
That's what we've been doing on this team for nearly a decade. We've organized, listened, knocked doors, made calls, built coalitions, and stood up for our neighbors—even when the odds were long. And we're not stopping now.
We've always done this work together. And even if you can’t volunteer tomorrow, you can help us start August strong by making a contribution today to help us keep going. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe260731?refcode=lpfe260731]
This year's elections will play a critical role in determining the direction of our country. The choices we make now will shape what comes next—not just in 2026, but in 2028 and beyond.
Any contribution you're able to make will go directly toward winning this race in TX-07, electing Democrats in Harris and Fort Bend counties, and helping Democrats in Texas and across the country take back the House and start to turn things around. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lpfe260731?refcode=lpfe260731]
I know we can do it. Together, we can do anything.

# **Graham Planter 's replacement reportedly has children with cousin**
Troy Jackson, Maine's Democratic Senate nominee replacing rape-accused Graham Platner, has two adult children with his longtime partner Lana Pelletier, who **[genealogical records show is his second cousin](https://substack.com/redirect/8d303371-16ae-4fda-9d80-d60d5c73d9eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) , **the Maine Wire reports. The couple, who have been together since high school, share the same great-grandparents, making them second cousins and their sons third cousins to both parents simultaneously.
[| | | | | The Maine Wire
---
@TheMaineWire
RELATIVE ATTRACTION: We can confirm that Troy Jackson and his longtime partner are second cousins. They have two children together
| 7:47 PM * Jul 30, 2026 * 2.27M Views742 Replies * 722 Reposts * 2.91K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/fe7cc214-c6d0-4d1a-8f40-9feff967afc3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **The relationship is entirely legal under Maine law,** which only restricts first-cousin marriages under certain conditions and places no limitations on second-cousin relationships. Genetic experts generally consider second-cousin pairings to present no meaningful elevated risk of inherited disorders compared to the general population.
* **Jackson now faces incumbent Republican Sen. Susan Collins** in one of the nation's most closely watched Senate races, viewed as a key opportunity for Democrats to flip a seat in their bid to regain Senate control. Jackson has generally referred to Pelletier as his "partner" throughout his political career, though some older biographies listed her as his wife.

# **49,000 muslim migrants flood Spanish enclave, military deployed amid crisis**
Spain's Interior Ministry estimated roughly 49,000 people -- nearly 60% of Ceuta's total population of 85,000 -- **[crossed from Morocco into the North African enclave](https://substack.com/redirect/664ce6d9-6057-48a4-8c4f-4352809d2331?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** within a single 24-hour period Thursday into Friday.

Bodies were seen in the water as rescue operations continued. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez and Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska are traveling to Ceuta as Madrid scrambles to restore order.

* **Spanish authorities said Morocco is cooperating to regain control of the border,** with Moroccan police intercepting migrants and both governments working to return those who entered illegally. Officials have not pinpointed a single cause for the surge, though Ceuta authorities cited a recent Supreme Court ruling limiting immediate sea returns. Migration advocates questioned whether that ruling alone could explain the dramatic escalation.

**Stephen Feinberg** -- $5B private equity billionaire, $2M+ to groups affiliated with the president -- is now the second-most powerful person at the Pentagon. He brought four former partners at his private-equity firm with him. One ran the CIA's clandestine service.

His old firm, Cerberus, backs a company currently suing the Pentagon for $40 billion. Feinberg oversees how the Pentagon handles that case. When he "divested," his stake moved to a trust for his adult children, managed by his old Cerberus colleagues.

Federal law says officials must avoid even the appearance of a conflict of interest. Putting your shares in a trust for your kids might clear the narrow legal bar. It does not protect the public's trust.

A private equity firm exists to make money. The Department of Defense exists to protect this country and answer to the Constitution, to Congress, and to us. Those are not the same job. You cannot run one like the other.

Congressional oversight runs through the House Armed Services Committee. Its top Democrat is Adam Smith -- my opponent, the incumbent since 1997 -- whose campaign runs on defense contractor money. Check it yourself at OpenSecrets.org.

Before we hand this arrangement one more dollar of public money, we're owed a straight answer to a simple question: Who exactly is set to profit?

I'm running on no corporate PACs, no foreign interests, and no defense contractors. This is exactly what that promise is meant to prevent.

Care. Courage. The Constitution.

Hey Peter,

Have you ever watched a race and noticed that all of the drivers, the race
cars, even the track are peppered with corporate sponsors? It’s hard to
miss!

I've been thinking about what these jackets would look like if politicians
had to wear them.

Mine would honestly be pretty bare at first. Since I’ve never taken
corporate PAC money, and never will, there are no oil company logos or
health insurance slogans to stitch on.

Instead, I'd patch it with unions and people who've actually backed this
campaign: National Nurses United. United Auto Workers. Bernie Sanders.
AOC. And a few hundred thousand of you, [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260731-1-ak.nLAuJQ&amount=10&refcode=em20260731-2780&t=1004&akid=2791%2E251025%2Eo_PEHX ]chipping in $10, $25, whatever
you could spare.

Now, picture my opponent's jacket.

It's crowded. Utility companies. Big Tech. Big Pharma. Health insurance
corporations. The list goes on. Not to mention, AIPAC’s Super PACs — which
have spent a record-breaking $59 million in Michigan to prop up her

body:
I have not lost my voice.
#

Friends --
Fifteen years ago, a gunman shot me in the head while I was meeting with constituents in front of a grocery store in Tucson.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260731-1-b&t=1&akid=11682%2E3935704%2EMdB7zT)
Because of the damage the bullet caused to the left hemisphere of my brain, where the language function sits, I have aphasia. This means that even though the words are in my head, I have a hard time getting them out.
**Aphasia may make it harder for me to speak. But I have not lost my voice.**
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giff-em-q32026.gsDos-&refcode=em260731-1-b&t=2&akid=11682%2E3935704%2EMdB7zT)
The road to recovery hasn’t been easy for me, but I’ve never given up. In addition to speech therapy and physical therapy, I dedicate much of my time to riding my bike, playing my French horn, and practicing yoga. These activities have helped me so much in my recovery journey.

name: Jenny Beth Martin, Tea Party Patriots Action
subject: She was sixteen. Danbury was burning.
body:
Episode 3: the women who defied a king
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org%2Ffoundation/1/0100019fb8a676c2-4c8b9d6c-978d-4057-b0e9-6e92e5b5cc49-000000/kVrjD5mn9JXwZr9_en8ukHyCNNmcigQLGCeyv9cMDQc=452)Patriot–On the night of April 26, 1777, British troops put the town of Danbury, Connecticut to the torch.They had come for what was stored there: the provisions, the tents, the barrels of supply that kept the Continental Army standing. What they could not carry off, they burned.Word of it had to travel fast, and it had to travel at night. Across the New York line, in what is now Putnam County, a militia colonel named Henry Ludington had four hundred men under his command. Every one of them was scattered across the countryside, home on furlough for spring planting.The story handed down in the Ludington family is that the rider who went out to gather those men was the colonel's sixteen-year-old daughter, Sybil.As her family told it, she rode close to forty miles that night, in the rain and the dark, through country thick with loyalists who would have been glad to come across the daughter of Henry Ludington alone on a road after sundown. She knocked at farmhouse doors and called out that Danbury was burning and to muster at her father's house. By morning, the regiment had come in.I want to be straight with you about one thing, because you would rather hear it from me than come across it later and wonder why we left it out. Historians have argued for a long time about how much of that night can be proven. There is no militia record of the ride and no letter from 1777 describing it. The account came down through Sybil's family and did not reach print until a century afterward. Her defenders answer that a girl carrying muster orders for a man with a bounty on his head had every reason not to advertise what she had done, and that a great many true things in 1777 were never written down by anybody.Here is what is not in dispute. Danbury burned. Those four hundred men were scattered across the hills. Somebody had to go out into the dark and bring them in. And a family remembered, and kept remembering for generations, that the one who went was their teenage daughter.Episode 5 of Defiant Ones tells her story, and it is available right now.**Here is how to listen:**[_**Visit the episode page and start Episode 5.**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.washingtontimes.com%2Fdefiant-ones%2Fsybil-ludington%2F/1/0100019fb8a676c2-4c8b9d6c-978d-4057-b0e9-6e92e5b5cc49-000000/rf0uop_QFUcB6Yx_Nvw8RZSg4CyRkiKWZJRowcdfb1g=452) While you are there, request our free activity pack. It is built for children, to give the young ones in your family something to do with these stories once the episode ends. It costs nothing.Tea Party Patriots Foundation is honored to help bring this series to you, alongside the team that created it, as our country marks 250 years of independence.A great deal of what was done for this country was done by people nobody thought to write down. That is not a reason to stop asking hard questions about the record. It is a reason to go looking.In liberty,Jenny Beth MartinCo-Founder, Tea Party PatriotsTea Party Patriots FoundationP.S. If you have children or grandchildren, listen to this one with them, and request the free activity pack so they have something to do with it afterward. For an older child, Sybil Ludington is a rare teaching opportunity: her ride is honored on a postage stamp and cast in bronze.[CONTRIBUTE](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org%2Ffoundation%2Fdonate/1/0100019fb8a676c2-4c8b9d6c-978d-4057-b0e9-6e92e5b5cc49-000000/ifezLvsLF0KvzW8-Y-6P-ZpOb33BjyS6_T8VQLaJZQM=452) _This email list is a joint venture of the following separate organizations: Tea Party Patriots Action, Inc., Tea Party Patriots Foundation, and Tea Party Patriots Citizens Fund. | | | I've faced a lot of hatred in my time in public life. I want to tell you about some of it — not for sympathy, but because I think it says something important about this moment.
When I first ran for Congress, there were people who tried to paint me as un-American simply because of where I was born. There were questions about whether someone with a name like mine could really represent this country.
More recently, a sitting Republican elected official publicly called for the mass deportation of Indians and labeled me a "foreign occupier" with an "unpronounceable name."
And just weeks ago, in Frisco, Texas, a demonstrator tore an Indian flag to pieces while a crowd around them chanted anti-India hatred.
This comes from anyone who has decided that people like me — immigrants, people with hard-to-pronounce names, people who don't fit some narrow idea of who belongs — don't have a right to be here, let alone lead.
_**Every single time, I've made the same choice: Keep going.**_
Because I know exactly what they're trying to do. They want to make people like me feel small, afraid, and unwelcome enough to quit. To go quiet. To let someone else do the fighting.
I refuse.
That's exactly why I started Equal Opportunity Now — to find and support leaders who have faced this same hatred and refused to be intimidated by it. Leaders who understand that extremism, wherever it comes from, only wins if we let it stop us.

clean_body: | | | | = | | | I've faced a lot of hatred in my time in public life. I want to tell you about some of it — not for sympathy, but because I think it says something important about this moment. When I first ran for Congress, there were people who tried to paint me as un-American simply because of where I was born. There were questions about whether someone with a name like mine could really represent this country. More recently, a sitting Republican elected official publicly called for the mass deportation of Indians and labeled me a "foreign occupier" with an "unpronounceable name." And just weeks ago, in Frisco, Texas, a demonstrator tore an Indian flag to pieces while a crowd around them chanted anti-India hatred. This comes from anyone who has decided that people like me — immigrants, people with hard-to-pronounce names, people who don't fit some narrow idea of who belongs — don't have a right to be here, let alone lead. Every single time, I've made the same choice: Keep going. Because I know exactly what they're trying to do. They want to make people like me feel small, afraid, and unwelcome enough to quit. To go quiet. To let someone else do the fighting. I refuse. That's exactly why I started Equal Opportunity Now — to find and support leaders who have faced this same hatred and refused to be intimidated by it. | | Hey Patriot,
---
Look – I’m not gonna sugarcoat this one.
**We _cannot_ run out of money** to fund and train ballot chasers at the worst possible time in this election cycle.
You’re one of Turning Point’s most dedicated supporters. When the rest of the list goes quiet, folks like you step up. That’s why I’m reaching out to you directly here.
Charlie Kirk built this movement from the ground up. He **_believed_** in the power of everyday patriots showing up, knocking on doors, and changing the direction of this country one conversation at a time.
We lost him, but we are **_still_** carrying his torch.
We need to train at least **[500 new ballot chasers next month](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NTR9AAwAAAAAAhLnPg9jcmAXa4V1IIeLmgyK6leP5Pk0fsEYEbYwdmndZtwE6AYXIzbenebQv69iDEKJXRyg8OB0VAXCeCX1Geuyn-Tn1tEgTW00jc6keQ)** and put them in key districts across the country.
If we hit that number, we have a real fighting chance at winning the midterms. We can keep “**democratic socialists** ” _AKA_ **_communists_** OUT of Congress.
But if we fail... we lose the majority. President Trump becomes a lame duck president. We get more of the same disastrous Biden-era policies. And for all practical purposes, the fight is over.
This is NOT theoretical. This is the crossroads.
We need patriots on the pavement right now. We need the funding to train them, equip them, and send them out before early voting begins.
**Help us keep Charlie’s mission alive.**
**[Every dollar makes a difference in training ballot chasers.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NTR9AAwAAAAAAhLnPg9kvDqnABBOtsfbPAnjIRvJUZQjY7cgG5p5S8nAp_9O0qsCjWPUlN7r_YBUPq0JNSJKo9_t8fr9IAtwjTNmjwVgiHbVyo4XLF200Q)**

[KEEP THE TORCH BURNING](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NTR9AAwAAAAAAhLnPg9llyrwapsDWg2gdav90Du-eXGY6iF1ad55bI_E6yffRP2LVdZos6f_fsDzGIZkc4yVuHQjW0Hy0ujDBdmsfDRMqXzLn_12r7r6jA)

We are running out of time to get the resources we urgently need to scale this operation. The only thing standing between us and a radical socialist takeover is the ground game Charlie so deeply believed in – **[and the patriots willing to fund it.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5NTR9AAwAAAAAAhLnPg9mVIkeBlZZ1zVvbwKDiVMO_dHhwpKhheHFZRQfvNz9kVyT6AYr57MrOP_OTrUhUciKpsk3Hs_8wV28132dZhzlxeKluVf0cYnAMw)**
Please please please don’t sit this one out.
For Charlie. For Our Country. For the America we still believe in.

Tyler Bowyer
Executive Director, Turning Point PAC

name: Kalliana @ Team AnderBois
subject: No one works harder than Sue
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of AnderBois
body:
| |
---
Hi friend, With less than six weeks until the primary, and three weeks before the start of early voting, our team is working hard to get Sue’s message out there. We’re knocking doors, making calls, attending community events, delivering yard signs, and so the list could go on.

Through all of this, I am continually reminded of one thing:
---
**Sue is the real deal**.
---
She has a clear vision, she knows how to make things happen, and she leads with infectious positivity and gratitude. To be honest, if this weren’t the case, I would probably be spending my summer in true Rhode Island fashion: relaxing on the beach. But doing that wouldn’t ease my frustration with how our government is (or really, isn’t) working. It wouldn’t give me hope for what my future looks like.
---
**Being a part of this team, and believing we can have people like Sue in office gives me that kind of hope.**
---
I want every Rhode Islander to know that the “real” Sue is the same one that you all have heard from at house parties, on social media, or through these emails. The TV ads that we just filmed will help make that possible – but we need your help getting this message out. We’re still **$6,550 short** of our goal to get Sue’s ad out to the voters we need to reach and tonight at midnight is our **last****fundraising deadline** before early voting starts. [**Can you chip in today?**](https://sue4ri.com/l/s6wyI9qUi9Z9)
---
[ **Contribute today to get Sue’s message out across Rhode Island >>** ](https://sue4ri.com/l/sMlFOIeDLXOU)
---
Thank you for joining us in this fight. \- Kalliana
---

name: Rick | Bennett for Governor
subject: My jersey says Maine
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Bennett for Governor · P
body:
Before midnight, help us keep this independent campaign moving.

| | |
---
---
---
---
Peter, **We can feel the momentum building.** Everywhere I go, Mainers are joining our campaign because they are fed up with politics as usual. They are fed up with a politics that is more focused on political point scoring than solving the challenges that working families are facing every day. I am running for Governor because Maine families cannot afford more of the same. The bills keep going up, housing is out of reach, child care costs too much, and the people in power keep serving the insiders instead of you. We cannot continue with the corrupt system that puts political parties ahead of results. Mainers are doing their part, but Augusta isn’t doing its job. Some people wear an R on their jersey. Some people wear a D on their jersey. **My jersey says MAINE.** That means I don’t answer to party bosses. I don’t answer to insiders. I answer to you, and to the people of this state. And because of people like you, this campaign is growing. More Mainers are stepping forward. More people are showing up. More people are deciding they want a governor who will fight for them instead of performing for a party. But we need your help to keep this momentum growing. The other campaigns have their machines. Their donor networks. Their insiders. **We have something stronger – people who still believe Maine comes first.** [So I’m asking you directly: before midnight tonight, will you chip in $10, $25, or $50 to help us keep building this independent campaign?](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/donate?e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=motivational_end_of_night&n=1) Your donation helps us reach more voters, grow this movement, and prove that this race belongs to the people of Maine – not the political class. I believe Maine is worth fighting for. I believe the people of this state are ready for something better. And if you believe that too, I’m asking you to stand with us tonight.

name: Kelly Morrison
subject: A doctor’s take on the Cyclosporiasis outbreak
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Morrison for Congress
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26]
You probably hadn’t heard of Cyclospora before this summer.
It’s a microscopic parasite that causes gastrointestinal illness, and it’s spreading across the country right now, spiking Cyclosporiasis cases and making people sick in 41 states and counting — and making 2026 its worst year on record.
As a doctor, I know that catching an outbreak early is a critical part of protecting the public’s health. But when you strip away the public health programs designed to keep people safe, your ability to do that is severely limited. Case in point:
A year ago, RFK Jr. gutted the CDC programs responsible for tracking foodborne illness outbreaks just like this one. He decided to make surveillance of Cyclospora optional.
Ten months later, an outbreak began. And instead of being quickly identified and contained, we found ourselves in this situation:
https://secure.ngpvan.com/Kqz1a2h3Q0ObJSaY-VqcCQ2?contactdata=Ph/LPIJLs4Vc8jrVkYm9yCvVbmQiYNyDoHoXRnuJGdossYQ6TSRUSe24jIvcvZbQ3qcjOvU0JZ9eDYyqdhHE8lNnJD4eCpw+9ExvM8WduaQwHcUfL2WzgTUR0FQjECpx7/GNlthUXWfB+Zsf+NKSdw== [https://secure.ngpvan.com/Kqz1a2h3Q0ObJSaY-VqcCQ2?contactdata=Ph/LPIJLs4Vc8jrVkYm9yCvVbmQiYNyDoHoXRnuJGdossYQ6TSRUSe24jIvcvZbQ3qcjOvU0JZ9eDYyqdhHE8lNnJD4eCpw+9ExvM8WduaQwHcUfL2WzgTUR0FQjECpx7/GNlthUXWfB+Zsf+NKSdw==]
But “just eat healthy and you’ll be fine” ... right? That’s what Donald Trump and RFK Jr. keep saying, but that is not how outbreaks work.
You can buy organic foods, wash every fruit and vegetable, and still get sick — because contamination prevention IS NOT and CANNOT be your personal responsibility.
It is a public health job, one that was formerly held by dozens of scientists at the FDA and CDC, until those jobs were drastically scaled back: The national advisory committee that used to advise our federal agencies on how to prevent food contamination has been completely disbanded. The CDC used to have 11 scientists tracking food parasites, but now it’s down to three.
The Trump administration is choosing to ignore the science and fire the experts, and this is the result.
RFK Jr. should be fired.
If you agree that this administration cannot be trusted with our public health, add your name to my petition calling for RFK Jr.’s firing today. clean_body: [] You probably hadn’t heard of Cyclospora before this summer. It’s a microscopic parasite that causes gastrointestinal illness, and it’s spreading across the country right now, spiking Cyclosporiasis cases and making people sick in 41 states and counting — and making 2026 its worst year on record. As a doctor, I know that catching an outbreak early is a critical part of protecting the public’s health. But when you strip away the public health programs designed to keep people safe, your ability to do that is severely limited. Case in point: A year ago, RFK Jr. gutted the CDC programs responsible for tracking foodborne illness outbreaks just like this one. He decided to make surveillance of Cyclospora optional. Ten months later, an outbreak began. And instead of being quickly identified and contained, we found ourselves in this situation: == [==] But “just eat healthy and you’ll be fine” ... right? That’s what Donald Trump and RFK Jr. keep saying, but that is not how outbreaks work. You can buy organic foods, wash every fruit and vegetable, and still get sick — because contamination prevention IS NOT and CANNOT be your personal responsibility. It is a public health job, one that was formerly held by dozens of scientists at the FDA and CDC, until those jobs were drastically scaled back: The national advisory committee that used to advise our federal agencies on how to prevent food contamination has been completely disbanded. The CDC used to have 11 scientists tracking food parasites, but now it’s down to three. The Trump administration is choosing to ignore the science and fire the experts, and this is the result. RFK Jr. should be fired. If you agree that this administration cannot be trusted with our public health, add your name to my petition calling for RFK Jr.’s firing today. body:
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Voter registration is a core part of how we fight back against suppression, folks. And we need your help, since we're behind our targets.
How does our program run? We maximize your impact by focusing on the under-served and ignored portions of potential voters. Unregistered, eligible citizens. Previous voters who let their registration lapse. Anyone who feels disregarded and disconnected from the political process.
Why them? Candidates and their political campaigns target those most likely to turn out. They hyper-focus on "persuadables" and "reliable partisans." Rather than trying to compete with their resources, we maximize your impact by speaking directly to Americans who feel left behind as they lose their fundamental rights.
We drive these eligible citizens to participation by helping them understand the stakes and showing how their vote matters . That's why our voter registration efforts are so important: Everyone should vote and feel invested in the outcome.
Just $3 can help us register a new voter. We need your help to catch up to our goals, will you step up with $30 or more today to help register 10 new voters? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=073126_1&amount=30]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=073126_1&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=073126_1&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=073126_1&amount=50]

Unfortunately, we don't have anywhere near the resources to blanket the country with our efforts. Each election cycle, we target specific states where our efforts will make the greatest difference, like Nevada, North Carolina, or Michigan.
We set our lofty goals for a reason . The key is getting these disenfranchised people -- always the first target of opponents of voting rights across the country -- to see the importance of voting now more than ever.
Voting quickly becomes a habit -- a habit our democracy sorely needs to fulfill the promise of the American dream. Overwhelming key states with new voter registrations can help turn the tide against the voter suppression laws we've seen passed over the last few years.
We've got to catch back up so new voter registration -- at a cost to us of just about $3 per new voter -- can help turn the tide. Can you pitch in with $30 or however much you can to help us register new voters ahead of registration deadlines? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=073126_1&amount=30]
Thank you,
Voter Action Project's Registration Team

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

Unsurprisingly, when they try to build these massive, noisy, polluting server farms in regular neighborhoods, local communities revolt. In just the first quarter of this year alone, at least 75 of these mega-projects were blocked by residents who refuse to watch their electricity bills spike and their resources drain. So, the administration found a loophole for their billionaire donors: **stop asking local communities and just hand over federal public lands instead.** On Wednesday, the Department of Energy announced a massive $100 billion project to allow private corporations to build a sprawling AI server campus and a 2-gigawatt natural gas power plant directly on federal land in Kentucky. That is enough gas to power 750,000 homes, dedicated entirely to a corporate server farm. [**This is a five-alarm fire for our public lands, and we need to fight back immediately. They know that if the public realizes they are handing over our deserts and federal lands to build giant, gas-powered server farms, there will be hell to pay at the ballot box. We are building the rapid-response infrastructure to expose these backroom deals and turn this corporate land grab into a political death sentence for the politicians cheering it on. We just need the volume to get our message directly into their home districts. They think they can quietly turn our public lands into their own private, taxpayer-subsidized power grid. Let's make sure the people rubber-stamping this are out of a job. You take our land—we take your seat. body:
Adam here,

Campaign Manager for Nate Powell.

We're in the home stretch.

You’ve seen the ads, mailers, and texts. Baumgartner, in a last-ditch effort, is spending heavily against Nate to box him out of the primary so he doesn't have to face him in November. Our movement is on the cusp of winning, and he knows it.

With Election Day approaching (August 4th), we've been building out two teams to combat Baumgartner’s attacks and drive this win home:
> **1.) **Get Out The Vote (GOTV) – knock doors and phone bank with fellow volunteers to make sure likely voters support Nate. Check our events page below to see which shifts Nate is joining us for.
>
>
> **2.)** Outreach Team – join our daily virtual phonebank (5-7pm) calling volunteers to schedule them for canvassing and phone banking shifts. Every call you make helps fill 100 more doors knocked or calls made.

I am personally asking you to do just one of these before Election Day. Pick GOTV or Outreach, whichever fits your schedule. Anything matters.
**
**
> **1.) Sign up for Get Out the Vote –** browse our events page and pick the canvassing or phone bank shift(s) that work for you: [https://natepowellforcongress.com/events/](https://natepowellforcongress-dot-yamm-track.appspot.com/2i3DxRbyELT3axV2_2Z9En7FoGm8D0PQEu8a4b6qjIg13EVS6nwESwc4hcI8xDfeggYcssEE7xbqQ7g0D1Bau3eRhnQJELtiCDW8kiu-YkY4Wkig8eQfGa8pA6nFdk9T6Ac0K9C7hsp5OtPOD7lDfjtkRZurhgEUphTjHsnI3rrugRogNCe1bPmv26BJ67v164fnst-k)
**
**
> **2.) Sign up to join our Outreach Team** by responding to this email.

Victory is within reach. We will win this primary, but only if each of us does our part. Getting this far wouldn’t have been possible without you.

Let's finish this fight.

Adam Sherrill
Campaign Manager

Growing up in Allagash and spending years working 80-hour weeks in the woods to make ends meet, I know firsthand what working Mainers need from our government.
And for 30 years, Susan Collins has failed us. Time and again, she has sold us out to Donald Trump and his MAGA agenda while pretending we’re too dumb to notice. And I’m sick of it.
My name is Troy Jackson. I’m a proud Mainer, father, and fifth-generation logger.
This weekend, I officially earned the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate. Now it’s time to defeat Susan Collins and her billionaire backers. So I’m asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to become a Founding Donor to my campaign right now and help us win the most important Senate race in the country. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson]
DONATE TO DEFEAT SUSAN COLLINS AND FLIP THE SENATE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson]
Let me tell you a bit about what this race means to me.
When I was growing up, I was a poor kid in a town full of poor kids. My family relied on food assistance at times. I distinctly remember when I was 13 years old, we didn’t have heat or running water, and I heard my mother quietly crying to herself, wishing she could do more for us.
After high school, I became a logger like my dad, and his dad, and his dad before him. When a greedy landowner tried to screw my fellow loggers and me out of fair wages, I fought back. A whole bunch of politicians, including then-first-term Senator Susan Collins, promised to listen, but they left us high and dry — and I realized that nothing would change unless there were working-class voices in power.
So I ran for the Maine legislature, where I served 20 years, including six years as the President of the Maine Senate. It’s been the honor of my life to fight for working people.
I drove hours each way between the North Woods and the State Capitol, because that's what the job required. I won those elections in a district that went for Trump by 20 points, because up here, people care less about a label and more about whether you give a damn about their family.
I’m building this campaign the right way. With grassroots support from folks like you. I’m not running to impress the billionaires or the corporate class. I’m running for the mom who’s worried about how she’ll fill her gas tank this week. I’m running for the kid whose whole life will be determined by the quality of his education. I’m running to ensure every working family in Maine has the government they deserve.
If you believe in this fight and our movement, I’m humbly asking you to split a donation between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild today to help us reach our fundraising goal and take on the GOP’s millions. * * *
# Iran
* **U.S. resumes strikes on Iran:** The U.S. restarted its campaign of strikes against Iran Thursday following an Iranian missile attack on a U.S. base in Jordan on Wednesday, with strikes reported across Iran's south and southwest.
* U.S. strikes on Qeshm Island on Thursday killed a taxi driver, his wife, and their 2-year-old child, Iranian media reported.
* Three members of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps were killed in U.S. strikes on Thursday, the group announced.
* Footage circulating online appeared to show missiles being [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/6e6c60e1-f487-47c6-b76f-8edaeadf2d9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from Kuwait, despite the insistence of the government to the Wall Street Journal earlier this week that it had not allowed missiles to be launched from its territory.
* Separately, CENTCOM [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/3b410051-4e6c-477e-b747-d71bd36e43e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday evening that U.S. forces had redirected 24 commercial vessels, disabled two, and boarded two, as part of their naval blockade on Iranian ports that began mid-July.
* **Iran hits U.S. bases in Jordan, Kuwait:**
* Iran responded by attacking bases in Jordan, Kuwait, and Bahrain, with Friday attacks reportedly [targeting](https://substack.com/redirect/73710279-4e6f-49b1-86e4-f6021c8cfae3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) aircraft shelters, satellite communication systems, and equipment storage facilities at the Ahmed Al-Jaber base in Kuwait and the Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain. Kuwait's Defense Ministry [said](https://substack.com/redirect/0544c50c-94cc-4633-bfda-5d03e3b48c13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it detected and destroyed Iranian drones in Kuwaiti airspace.
* The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/974e6163-a130-4536-a53e-2c8d0aac8335?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a missile strike on the Al-Azraq air base in Jordan on Thursday "completely destroyed" three U.S. F-35 fighter jets and badly damaged three others, according to a statement carried by Iranian state media.
* The IRGC also [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/21f26e26-4fc6-470f-add4-8e5f48788fb2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that its strikes on Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait destroyed two drone hangars and a fuel depot for military aircraft and helicopters, according to Tasnim. U.S. CENTCOM [denied](https://substack.com/redirect/b5e6be0e-dcab-4f5f-8d3c-532137c65867?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this, though satellite imagery appeared to show damage to a hangar.
* The Chinese embassy in Kuwait [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/febc75e1-c21c-464b-b35e-726cec5e871b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that a vehicle working for a Chinese company was struck during Iran's Thursday strikes on the country, killing its Nepalese driver, though it did not identify Iran as the party responsible for the strike in its statement.
* In the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Friday it targeted two oil tankers attempting to pass with U.S. military "air support." The IRGC claimed the two tankers were "targeted and stopped," while four other oil tankers quickly changed course and turned back.
* **Over 4,000 children killed or injured in Iran war:** More than 4,000 children have been killed or injured across six countries since the Iran war began five months ago, according to UNICEF. In Iran, 386 children have reportedly been killed and 2,117 children injured. "As war reverberates in Iran and neighboring countries, children continue to be killed and maimed in the places where they should be safest - their homes, schools and communities," Abdul Fofana, UNICEF Acting Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa, said in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/22e79b14-655f-49b2-9e4b-28ce9daec68f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). "Parties to the conflict should not normalize the suffering of children, who remain at the sharpest end of conflicts they did not start and have no power to stop."
* **Pakistan trying to broker more negotiations, FM says:** Tahir Andrabi, a spokesman for Pakistan's Foreign Ministry, [told](https://substack.com/redirect/06b41d62-8c9e-4d4d-9e4a-c1fd0ded36c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) reporters Pakistan is making "every effort to bring all parties back to the Islamabad memorandum," and has urged them to fully honor their commitment to hold technical talks under the deal, according to BBC Persian.

* **Egypt, Iran respond to Wednesday attack on Egyptian port:** Egypt's government confirmed that a U.S.-owned Floating Storage Regasification Unit, the Energos Winter, sustained significant damage from a drone attack at Egypt's Damietta port on Wednesday. Fire also engulfed a separate vessel, the Gaslog Salem.
* The government [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3f450616-e464-4aee-80ff-a401e5f6e409?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its security committee was assessing the situation and reviewing potential responses.
* The Winter is a floating terminal that receives super-chilled liquefied natural gas from transport tankers and converts it back into its gaseous form to feed national energy grids. FSRUs like the Winter play a critical role in supplementing Egypt's national power grid and managing domestic energy demand.
* Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi [responded](https://substack.com/redirect/1249c721-1046-4dc3-ad89-e6845a8b2f02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Wednesday's drone attack by warning that it may be an Israeli "false flag" operation.

* **Iraqi government denies it approved U.S.-Saudi strikes:** Iraqi government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi [said](https://substack.com/redirect/2f0971c4-286f-46c8-a3d5-b18cb1555f5f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that Baghdad had no prior knowledge of the joint U.S.-Saudi attacks on Iraqi territory, directly contradicting President Donald Trump's earlier claim. The strikes killed at least 20 members of the Iran-backed Popular Mobilization Forces. Prime Minister Mohammed al-Zaidi subsequently [postponed](https://substack.com/redirect/f5872f8c-f008-4415-8f06-21fb310c3839?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a planned trip to Saudi Arabia.

* **Iran thanks Jordan for "cooperation" after public letter calling for U.S. to leave:** An open letter demanding the immediate withdrawal of U.S. forces was signed by more than 200 prominent Jordanians. The letter said the roughly 4,000 U.S. troops in Jordan expose the country to "security, political, and economic risks that serve no national interest," according to the New York Times.
* Iran's armed forces publicly [thanked](https://substack.com/redirect/c77cc017-167b-43d1-904b-18c691c5d719?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "the people of Jordan" on Thursday for their "cooperation" and for providing useful information from inside U.S. bases on Jordanian soil.
* Iran has previously claimed that it has operational support within Jordan.
* **U.S. tags more Iranian firms with sanctions:** The U.S. Treasury Department [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/21911f73-84eb-4b16-a6b5-b31c8435325b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that it would be sanctioning Mahan Air, one of Iran's largest airlines, along with individuals and companies in China, India, Russia, and Iran accused of keeping the carrier flying.
* The Treasury accused Mahan of "enabling" the IRGC while "presenting itself as a civilian carrier," and alleged that it facilitated the movement of drones and weapons for the group.

* **Tanker traffic through Hormuz is increasing, Bloomberg reports:** A Thursday report from Bloomberg [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/de6d977b-62b6-49b5-bf68-11d263f829c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that oil-tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is picking up again after slowing earlier this month, despite this week's intensification of strikes.
* The report outlines a "transfer system" involving smaller or regional vessels, often sailing with transponders off, which work to move crude out of the Persian Gulf and which bring that crude to larger ships for international transport.
* Over the past seven days, the maritime tracking firm Kpler [recorded](https://substack.com/redirect/e05a5245-2983-4e27-b851-e207ec750b16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 18 tankers exiting the Strait of Hormuz, five of which were linked to Iran, carrying an average 1.86 million barrels per day.

* **Britain arrests British-Azerbaijani man on suspicion of spying for Iran in Cyprus:** Rashad Sultanov, a 44-year-old dual British-Azerbaijani national from Islington, north London, was [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/73f87946-f9e7-4b90-8be9-a7d434d3089e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Cyprus on July 17 on suspicion of surveilling Britain's RAF Akrotiri base and passing information to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, London's Metropolitan Police announced.
* The IRGC threatened earlier this month to strike British bases used by U.S. forces against Iran, and an Iranian-type Shahed drone caused slight damage at Akrotiri on March 2, after which Britain excluded the base from its defensive agreement with Washington.

# Yemen
* **Report: Saudi Arabia prepares offensive against Ansarallah:** Saudi Arabia is reportedly [preparing](https://substack.com/redirect/0905e345-1d5a-493c-8205-001c8733fcea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for a major military offensive against Yemen's Ansarallah by sea and possibly by land, in an effort to break their pressure on Saudi oil exports through the southern Red Sea, according to The Guardian.
* Saudi forces have reportedly begun withdrawing from eastern Yemen and concentrating troops for a possible assault on Ansarallah-controlled Al-Bayda governorate in central Yemen.
* **Fourteen countries back Saudi-led Red Sea naval coalition:** Fourteen countries, including Egypt, Turkey, and Pakistan, [backed](https://substack.com/redirect/834877c3-31e0-4ff2-b359-f579e8df2e42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Saudi-led maritime coalition aimed at countering Ansarallah's blockade of regional shipping routes. Saudi Arabia's Defense Ministry said the coalition would expand military coordination across the Bab Al-Mandab Strait, Red Sea, and Gulf of Aden. The United States, whose participation analysts call essential, is not among them.

* **Chinese-linked ships transit Bab Al-Mandab openly as most vessels go dark:** Two Chinese-linked cargo vessels [passed](https://substack.com/redirect/059e5b97-7069-4053-8941-5d3038eec71f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) through Bab Al-Mandab on July 30 without evasive maneuvers, GPS manipulation, or disabling their AIS signals, according to maritime intelligence firm Windward.
* Windward said the movements support reports of a case-by-case safe-passage arrangement between China and Ansarallah, with Iran informed.
* Twelve vessels traveled "dark" during the same period amid Ansarallah threats to target Saudi-linked tankers and export infrastructure.

* **Lloyd 's underwriters restrict war-risk cover for Saudi-linked ships:** Leading Lloyd's underwriters, including Ascot and Navium, [told](https://substack.com/redirect/85930177-e897-4fda-945a-7221e6382621?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) brokers they would cancel or restrict war-risk and cargo coverage for vessels with Saudi links, following Ansarallah's July 20 maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia, the Financial Times reported.
* The squeeze leaves Saudi Arabia caught between disruption in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea embargo, with Yanbu, currently its main outlet for crude exports.

# Palestine
* **Israel kills six in Gaza:** Israeli strikes on Gaza Thursday [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/9503a2f0-25b9-4ede-b03c-f646da5d7fde?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) six Palestinians, including two children, and wounded several others.
* An Israeli strike on Gaza City Thursday morning [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/0bc92a5f-248f-4172-b71d-4788e1dac7f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two Palestinians and wounded at least 10 others, WAFA reported.
* A separate drone strike in Jabaliya, north of Gaza, killed another Palestinian and wounded several more.
* Israeli warplanes [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/db3cd28f-5ac5-4825-9c04-c45419cac4b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a tent sheltering displaced people in the Al-Mawasi area west of Khan Younis, killing two Palestinians, including a child.
