* **Hamas agrees to second phase of Gaza ceasefire, says implementation hinges on Israel:**
* The Board of Peace and mediator countries announced Thursday that Hamas had agreed to a detailed roadmap for implementing the next phases of the Gaza ceasefire. The mediators said Hamas had, "for the first time," formally committed to "an actionable plan for relinquishing all its weapons," followed by an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza.
* In a Truth Social post, President Donald Trump hailed what he called a "HISTORIC agreement for the COMPLETE DISARMAMENT of Hamas."
* Hamas said Friday that it and other Palestinian factions had engaged "responsibly and positively" with mediators' proposals for the second phase of the ceasefire but stressed that implementation cannot proceed unless Israel fulfills all of its obligations under the first phase of the October 2025 agreement.
* The group said discussions over its heavy weapons are conditional on a permanent end to Israeli attacks, a full Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, early recovery and reconstruction, the entry of the National Committee and international forces, the dismantling of Israel-backed armed militias, and progress toward Palestinian self-determination and an independent Palestinian state.
* **Drop Site obtains roadmap documents on Gaza governance, weapons:** Drop Site [obtained](https://substack.com/redirect/84942f2b-9096-4e7a-b812-b04f6c9662a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a document outlining the framework Hamas and other Palestinian factions' agreed to for Gaza's governance and the handling of resistance weapons.
* Heavy weapons, military production sites, weapons depots, and tunnels would be inventoried and stored only after Israel halts attacks, withdraws from Gaza, and allows the entry of life essentials.
* The process would proceed alongside a phased Israeli withdrawal and a decommissioning of Israel-backed armed militias. No weapons would be handed over to Israel or any non-Palestinian party, and the National Committee would ultimately become the sole Palestinian body responsible for storing and controlling weapons in Gaza.
* The document says the framework is intended to support "a credible path toward realizing Palestinian self-determination and the establishment of the Palestinian state."
* On governance, the document states the National Committee would assume responsibility for Gaza's civil administration, ensure the continuity of public institutions and services, and restore the rights of public employees who were dismissed or forced into retirement in accordance with Palestinian law.
* The Committee would also conduct a comprehensive financial and administrative audit of Gaza, work to protect and recover public assets, and gradually repay up to $400 million in debts owed to suppliers and contractors over three years.
* **Israel has yet to officially agree to the deal:** Israel has not publicly agreed to the proposal and has made no official comment yet. * Around 100 soldiers from the battalion walked out of the Sde Teiman base without authorization on Thursday--leaving behind their military equipment and weapons--after their commander ordered battalion signs to be removed and destroyed.
* Sde Teiman is the notorious military detention and torture site where Israel has held Palestinians seized en masse from Gaza without charge or access to lawyers. There is extensive documentation of severe beatings, systematic rape and sexual abuse, and other forms of torture there.
* The soldiers did not walk off the base in protest of the torture of Palestinians at Sde Teiman or of combat duty in the genocide in Gaza but rather because they argued the signs that were ordered taken down--which portrayed or related to hazing practices inflicted by older troops on younger ones--represented a long-standing battalion tradition.

* **Israeli demolitions in southern Lebanon generate seismic waves the equivalent of a 3.8-magnitude earthquake, despite "ceasefire": **Israel carried out a series of large-scale demolitions, shelling attacks, and artillery strikes across southern Lebanon late Thursday and Friday, despite the U.S.-brokered ceasefire, Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported.
* Shortly after midnight, Israeli forces [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/67429efb-38b8-4008-8d7b-55d294821794?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) massive explosions in the Nabatieh district around Yahmar al-Shaqif, Arnoun, and Kfartebnit. * Israeli forces [demolished](https://substack.com/redirect/6ad5af07-047b-43d4-8f31-54d820231aa7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) caves and homes around Al-Mansouri and Majdal Zoun in the Tyre (Sour) district on Friday. * Aoun, who faces domestic opposition to the deal from Hezbollah and Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri, told Turkey's Anadolu Agency that implementation depends on "a complete Israeli withdrawal simultaneous with the deployment of the Lebanese army" and an international mechanism to verify compliance from both sides.

* **Mandela Barnes drops out of Wisconsin Democratic governor 's race: **Former Wisconsin Lt. Gov. **Mandela Barnes** announced that he is exiting the Democratic primary for governor. The state's primary is August 11.
* Democratic socialist and state Rep.**Francesca Hong** now faces Milwaukee County Executive **David Crowley** , who re-entered the race earlier this month with the endorsement of outgoing Democratic Gov. **Tony Evers.**
* A Marquette University Law School poll released on Wednesday showed that Hong had the support of 38% of Democratic primary voters, and Crowley had only 7%, with 34% of voters remaining undecided and 16% preferring the now-withdrawn Barnes.

* The poll found democratic socialists tend to be younger, more likely to be extremely motivated to vote, and are also much more likely to be critical of Israel, with 48% saying they'd be enthusiastic about a candidate who wants to cut U.S. support to Israel, compared with 20% of non-democratic socialists.

* Exxon chief financial officer **Neil Hansen** said further price increases are possible if the Strait of Hormuz is closed to tanker traffic.
* Hansen told the FT that the "pain point" regarding oil prices was not with crude, which he said is trading within its historical ranges, but with products such as petrol and diesel, which have seen their prices surge as production capacity diminished.
* **New York sues Kalshi, alleging prediction market platform runs "illegal gambling operation"**: New York state [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/612c7c89-83f9-41ee-a0d4-f234cab65935?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a lawsuit against the prediction market platform Kalshi on Friday, with Attorney General **Letitia James** alleging the company is operating illegally by accepting wagers without registering with the New York State Gaming Commission.
* The lawsuit seeks a permanent injunction, restitution to users, and financial penalties against the company, which is based in New York City.
* **WSJ reports on Trump 's fundraising focus, nightly calls for multimillion dollar donations:** President Donald Trump has personally directed a fundraising operation that has taken in more than $800 million since he returned to office, according to a Wall Street Journal report published on Thursday, with the president nightly calling his fundraiser **Meredith O 'Rourke** to press companies for donations ranging from $5 million to $50 million toward projects including his presidential library, a White House ballroom, and political committees.
* Companies including SoftBank, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta Platforms have made multimillion-dollar contributions, and executives told the Journal that donations appear linked to access and favorable regulatory treatment.

* **60,000 cross from Morocco into Ceuta after border breach:** At least 41 people have [died](https://substack.com/redirect/c03bbbf4-6ae9-427e-9b4a-e594ef4ed618?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) trying to reach the Spanish territory of Ceuta after breaching the border from Morocco with some 60,000 migrants entering the enclave in the past 24 hours.
* Ceuta, along with Melilla--another autonomous Spanish city in North Africa--represents the European Union's only land border with Africa. Migrants cross into Ceuta by land and sea, with people often swimming from the Moroccan town of Fnideq three miles away. Many of those who died drowned, while others were killed in a stampede to cross the border fence.
* Moroccan security forces clashed with thousands of people on the Moroccan side of the border as they tried to cross, using water cannons and firing warning shots into the air.
* Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez travelled to Ceuta on Friday and called the crossings "a violation of Spain's territorial integrity." Spain's Ministry of Interior said some 25,000 people were returned from Ceuta to Morocco so far on Friday.
* According to the AP, authorities in both Ceuta and Madrid, linked the mass influx of migrants to a recent decision by Spain's Supreme Court that ruled migrants arriving by sea could not be summarily deported, unlike those who cross by land or climb the border fence. Sanchez said migrant smugglers misinterpreted the ruling, triggering the surge.
* **Russia 's Africa Corps killed eight civilians in Mali air strike, HRW reports: **Africa Corps, the Russian paramilitary group that has largely replaced the Wagner Group in Africa, [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/1d51b643-568c-42e4-af79-d05777436306?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) eight civilians, including three children, in a June 15 air strike on the village of Kyrnia in Mali's central Mopti region, Human Rights Watch said Friday.

Drop Site Daily: July 31, 2026 | | | Jul 31 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Hundreds of migrants have attempted to swim from Morocco to the Spanish city of Ceuta in North Africa, Spain on July 30, 2026. Photo by Marcos Moreno/Anadolu via Getty Images. Friday, July 31, 2026 - U.S. resumes strikes on Iran. Iran hits U.S. bases in Jordan, Kuwait, and Bahrain. Over 4,000 children killed or injured in Iran war. Pakistan trying to broker more negotiations, Foreign Ministry says. Egypt, Iran respond to Wednesday attack on Egyptian port. Iraqi government denies it approved U.S.-Saudi strikes. U.S. tags more Iranian firms with sanctions. Tanker traffic through Hormuz is increasing, Bloomberg reports. Britain arrests British-Azerbaijani man on suspicion of spying for Iran in Cyprus. Report: Saudi Arabia prepares offensive against Ansarallah. Fourteen countries back Saudi-led Red Sea naval coalition. Chinese-linked ships transit Bab Al-Mandab openly as most vessels go dark. Lloyd's underwriters restrict war-risk cover for Saudi-linked ships. Israel kills six in Gaza. Hamas agrees to second phase of Gaza ceasefire, says implementation hinges on Israel. Drop Site obtains roadmap documents on Gaza governance, weapons. Israel continues its attacks in the occupied West Bank. Palestinian says he was tortured while in Israeli custody. Israeli demolitions in southern Lebanon generate seismic waves the equivalent of a 3.8-magnitude earthquake, despite "ceasefire." Lebanon's Aoun seeks Turkish backing for U.S.-brokered framework with Israel. Mandela Barnes drops out of Wisconsin Democratic governor's race. A third of Democrats now identify as democratic socialists, CNN poll finds. ExxonMobil and Chevron post combined $26.5 billion in second-quarter profits amid Iran war oil surge. New York sues Kalshi, alleging prediction market platform runs "illegal gambling operation." 60,000 cross from Morocco into Ceuta after border breach. Russia's Africa Corps killed eight civilians in Mali air strike, HRW reports. Attack on police checkpoint kills 11 officers in northwest Pakistan. Cuba details plans to open state economy to private industry. Milei signs decree allowing Argentina to expel foreigners who "spread hate" about the country. Brazilian Supreme Court authorizes probe into President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's son. Sudanese air force launches heavy strikes on RSF positions across Kordofan. Ukrainian drone sets Wildberries warehouse ablaze. Nepal's Prime Minister calls for calm after Hindu-Muslim clashes leave three dead. At least 32 miners killed in Balochistan coal mine explosion. British police arrest 77 at rally in support of Palestine Action. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran U.S. resumes strikes on Iran: The U.S. restarted its campaign of strikes against Iran Thursday following an Iranian missile attack on a U.S. base in Jordan on Wednesday, with strikes reported across Iran's south and southwest. U.S. strikes on Qeshm Island on Thursday killed a taxi driver, his wife, and their 2-year-old child, Iranian media reported. Three members of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps were killed in U.S. strikes on Thursday, the group announced. Footage circulating online appeared to show missiles being from Kuwait, despite the insistence of the government to the Wall Street Journal earlier this week that it had not allowed missiles to be launched from its territory. Separately, CENTCOM on Thursday evening that U.S. forces had redirected 24 commercial vessels, disabled two, and boarded two, as part of their naval blockade on Iranian ports that began mid-July. Iran hits U.S. bases in Jordan, Kuwait: Iran responded by attacking bases in Jordan, Kuwait, and Bahrain, with Friday attacks reportedly aircraft shelters, satellite communication systems, and equipment storage facilities at the Ahmed Al-Jaber base in Kuwait and the Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain. Kuwait's Defense Ministry it detected and destroyed Iranian drones in Kuwaiti airspace. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps a missile strike on the Al-Azraq air base in Jordan on Thursday "completely destroyed" three U.S. F-35 fighter jets and badly damaged three others, according to a statement carried by Iranian state media. The IRGC also that its strikes on Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait destroyed two drone hangars and a fuel depot for military aircraft and helicopters, according to Tasnim. U.S. CENTCOM this, though satellite imagery appeared to show damage to a hangar. The Chinese embassy in Kuwait that a vehicle working for a Chinese company was struck during Iran's Thursday strikes on the country, killing its Nepalese driver, though it did not identify Iran as the party responsible for the strike in its statement. In the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said Friday it targeted two oil tankers attempting to pass with U.S. military "air support." The IRGC claimed the two tankers were "targeted and stopped," while four other oil tankers quickly changed course and turned back. Over 4,000 children killed or injured in Iran war: More than 4,000 children have been killed or injured across six countries since the Iran war began five months ago, according to UNICEF. In Iran, 386 children have reportedly been killed and 2,117 children injured. "As war reverberates in Iran and neighboring countries, children continue to be killed and maimed in the places where they should be safest - their homes, schools and communities," Abdul Fofana, UNICEF Acting Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa, said in a . "Parties to the conflict should not normalize the suffering of children, who remain at the sharpest end of conflicts they did not start and have no power to stop." Pakistan trying to broker more negotiations, FM says: Tahir Andrabi, a spokesman for Pakistan's Foreign Ministry, reporters Pakistan is making "every effort to bring all parties back to the Islamabad memorandum," and has urged them to fully honor their commitment to hold technical talks under the deal, according to BBC Persian. Egypt, Iran respond to Wednesday attack on Egyptian port: Egypt's government confirmed that a U.S.-owned Floating Storage Regasification Unit, the Energos Winter, sustained significant damage from a drone attack at Egypt's Damietta port on Wednesday. Fire also engulfed a separate vessel, the Gaslog Salem. The government its security committee was assessing the situation and reviewing potential responses. The Winter is a floating terminal that receives super-chilled liquefied natural gas from transport tankers and converts it back into its gaseous form to feed national energy grids. FSRUs like the Winter play a critical role in supplementing Egypt's national power grid and managing domestic energy demand. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi to Wednesday's drone attack by warning that it may be an Israeli "false flag" operation. Iraqi government denies it approved U.S.-Saudi strikes: Iraqi government spokesperson Haider al-Aboudi on Thursday that Baghdad had no prior knowledge of the joint U.S.-Saudi attacks on Iraqi territory, directly contradicting President Donald Trump's earlier claim. The strikes killed at least 20 members of the Iran-backed Popular Mobilization Forces. Prime Minister Mohammed al-Zaidi subsequently a planned trip to Saudi Arabia. Iran thanks Jordan for "cooperation" after public letter calling for U.S. to leave: An open letter demanding the immediate withdrawal of U.S. forces was signed by more than 200 prominent Jordanians. The letter said the roughly 4,000 U.S. troops in Jordan expose the country to "security, political, and economic risks that serve no national interest," according to the New York Times. Iran's armed forces publicly "the people of Jordan" on Thursday for their "cooperation" and for providing useful information from inside U.S. bases on Jordanian soil. Iran has previously claimed that it has operational support within Jordan. U.S. tags more Iranian firms with sanctions: The U.S. Treasury Department on Thursday that it would be sanctioning Mahan Air, one of Iran's largest airlines, along with individuals and companies in China, India, Russia, and Iran accused of keeping the carrier flying. The Treasury accused Mahan of "enabling" the IRGC while "presenting itself as a civilian carrier," and alleged that it facilitated the movement of drones and weapons for the group. Tanker traffic through Hormuz is increasing, Bloomberg reports: A Thursday report from Bloomberg that oil-tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is picking up again after slowing earlier this month, despite this week's intensification of strikes. The report outlines a "transfer system" involving smaller or regional vessels, often sailing with transponders off, which work to move crude out of the Persian Gulf and which bring that crude to larger ships for international transport. Over the past seven days, the maritime tracking firm Kpler 18 tankers exiting the Strait of Hormuz, five of which were linked to Iran, carrying an average 1.86 million barrels per day. Britain arrests British-Azerbaijani man on suspicion of spying for Iran in Cyprus: Rashad Sultanov, a 44-year-old dual British-Azerbaijani national from Islington, north London, was in Cyprus on July 17 on suspicion of surveilling Britain's RAF Akrotiri base and passing information to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, London's Metropolitan Police announced. The IRGC threatened earlier this month to strike British bases used by U.S. forces against Iran, and an Iranian-type Shahed drone caused slight damage at Akrotiri on March 2, after which Britain excluded the base from its defensive agreement with Washington. Yemen Report: Saudi Arabia prepares offensive against Ansarallah: Saudi Arabia is reportedly for a major military offensive against Yemen's Ansarallah by sea and possibly by land, in an effort to break their pressure on Saudi oil exports through the southern Red Sea, according to The Guardian. Saudi forces have reportedly begun withdrawing from eastern Yemen and concentrating troops for a possible assault on Ansarallah-controlled Al-Bayda governorate in central Yemen. Fourteen countries back Saudi-led Red Sea naval coalition: Fourteen countries, including Egypt, Turkey, and Pakistan, a Saudi-led maritime coalition aimed at countering Ansarallah's blockade of regional shipping routes. Saudi Arabia's Defense Ministry said the coalition would expand military coordination across the Bab Al-Mandab Strait, Red Sea, and Gulf of Aden. The United States, whose participation analysts call essential, is not among them. Chinese-linked ships transit Bab Al-Mandab openly as most vessels go dark: Two Chinese-linked cargo vessels through Bab Al-Mandab on July 30 without evasive maneuvers, GPS manipulation, or disabling their AIS signals, according to maritime intelligence firm Windward. Windward said the movements support reports of a case-by-case safe-passage arrangement between China and Ansarallah, with Iran informed. Twelve vessels traveled "dark" during the same period amid Ansarallah threats to target Saudi-linked tankers and export infrastructure. Lloyd 's underwriters restrict war-risk cover for Saudi-linked ships: Leading Lloyd's underwriters, including Ascot and Navium, brokers they would cancel or restrict war-risk and cargo coverage for vessels with Saudi links, following Ansarallah's July 20 maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia, the Financial Times reported. The squeeze leaves Saudi Arabia caught between disruption in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea embargo, with Yanbu, currently its main outlet for crude exports. Palestine Israel kills six in Gaza: Israeli strikes on Gaza Thursday six Palestinians, including two children, and wounded several others. An Israeli strike on Gaza City Thursday morning two Palestinians and wounded at least 10 others, WAFA reported. A separate drone strike in Jabaliya, north of Gaza, killed another Palestinian and wounded several more. Israeli warplanes a tent sheltering displaced people in the Al-Mawasi area west of Khan Younis, killing two Palestinians, including a child. An Israeli missile a residential apartment in central Gaza, killing a child and injuring several others. Hamas agrees to second phase of Gaza ceasefire, says implementation hinges on Israel: The Board of Peace and mediator countries announced Thursday that Hamas had agreed to a detailed roadmap for implementing the next phases of the Gaza ceasefire. The mediators said Hamas had, "for the first time," formally committed to "an actionable plan for relinquishing all its weapons," followed by an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza. In a Truth Social post, President Donald Trump hailed what he called a "HISTORIC agreement for the COMPLETE DISARMAMENT of Hamas." Hamas said Friday that it and other Palestinian factions had engaged "responsibly and positively" with mediators' proposals for the second phase of the ceasefire but stressed that implementation cannot proceed unless Israel fulfills all of its obligations under the first phase of the October 2025 agreement. The group said discussions over its heavy weapons are conditional on a permanent end to Israeli attacks, a full Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, early recovery and reconstruction, the entry of the National Committee and international forces, the dismantling of Israel-backed armed militias, and progress toward Palestinian self-determination and an independent Palestinian state. Drop Site obtains roadmap documents on Gaza governance, weapons: Drop Site a document outlining the framework Hamas and other Palestinian factions' agreed to for Gaza's governance and the handling of resistance weapons. Heavy weapons, military production sites, weapons depots, and tunnels would be inventoried and stored only after Israel halts attacks, withdraws from Gaza, and allows the entry of life essentials. The process would proceed alongside a phased Israeli withdrawal and a decommissioning of Israel-backed armed militias. No weapons would be handed over to Israel or any non-Palestinian party, and the National Committee would ultimately become the sole Palestinian body responsible for storing and controlling weapons in Gaza. The document says the framework is intended to support "a credible path toward realizing Palestinian self-determination and the establishment of the Palestinian state." On governance, the document states the National Committee would assume responsibility for Gaza's civil administration, ensure the continuity of public institutions and services, and restore the rights of public employees who were dismissed or forced into retirement in accordance with Palestinian law. The Committee would also conduct a comprehensive financial and administrative audit of Gaza, work to protect and recover public assets, and gradually repay up to $400 million in debts owed to suppliers and contractors over three years. Israel has yet to officially agree to the deal: Israel has not publicly agreed to the proposal and has made no official comment yet. An Israeli official told Reuters on condition of anonymity: "Israel demands the complete disarmament of Hamas, including the removal of weapons from Gaza and the complete demilitarization of the strip as a precondition for any process." National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir in Hebrew on X: "The draft agreement published by the 'Peace Council' is not acceptable to Israel....The targeted killings in Gaza must continue, encouraging emigration must happen, Israel must win." Israel continues its attacks in the occupied West Bank: Nablus: A Palestinian man was in the neck by Israeli soldiers on Thursday, following an attack on his vehicle. Israeli forces a Palestinian man in the abdomen in Al-Juneid on Friday. Forces tear-gassed several Palestinians, including children. The Israeli military was accompanying settlers who had initiated an attack in the area. In the village of Burin, Israeli settlers to agricultural land and burned down several olive trees. Bethlehem: Israeli forces the Solomon's Pools tourist area on Friday, declaring the site to be a "closed military zone" and forcing visitors to leave the site at gunpoint, WAFA reported. Earlier, an Israeli military convoy stormed into the city, raided a house, and detained a Palestinian man. Ramallah : Israeli forces the Qaddura refugee camp, ransacking the headquarters of the camp's Popular Committee and releasing tear gas, and detaining one of the camp's residents. Palestinian says he was tortured while in Israeli custody: Rizq Shakarneh, 47, from Nahhalin west of Bethlehem, WAFA he suffered fractures and multiple injuries from torture during his eight days in Israeli detention, after being arrested following the demolition of homes and structures in his town. He said Israeli forces starved and denied him necessary medical treatment despite pre-existing health problems, and CT scans conducted after his release Wednesday evening reportedly revealed rib fractures, bruises and head injuries. Drop Site interviews family of Palestinian man detained and mocked by Israeli soldiers in viral photos: Drop Site's Mohamed Ahmed with the parents of 22-year-old Mahmoud Al-Drimli, who identified him as the blindfolded Palestinian man in a viral photograph showing two female Israeli soldiers smiling as they pose beside him. Mahmoud disappeared on November 2, 2024. His family said they had received no information about him until recognizing him in the image. "The moment I saw the picture, my heart was at peace, and I was happy. But at the same time, when I saw him in that state, my heart broke," his mother said through tears. Watch the full interviews with Mahmoud 's parents . Israeli soldiers walk off Sde Teiman base in protest of order to remove battalion signs glorifying hazing: Fourteen soldiers of the Givati Brigade's Tzabar Battalion who took part in a mass desertion on Thursday have been sentenced to 30 days in military jail and permanently dismissed from combat duty, according to the Israeli military. Around 100 soldiers from the battalion walked out of the Sde Teiman base without authorization on Thursday--leaving behind their military equipment and weapons--after their commander ordered battalion signs to be removed and destroyed. Sde Teiman is the notorious military detention and torture site where Israel has held Palestinians seized en masse from Gaza without charge or access to lawyers. There is extensive documentation of severe beatings, systematic rape and sexual abuse, and other forms of torture there. The soldiers did not walk off the base in protest of the torture of Palestinians at Sde Teiman or of combat duty in the genocide in Gaza but rather because they argued the signs that were ordered taken down--which portrayed or related to hazing practices inflicted by older troops on younger ones--represented a long-standing battalion tradition. Lebanon Israeli demolitions in southern Lebanon generate seismic waves the equivalent of a 3.8-magnitude earthquake, despite "ceasefire": Israel carried out a series of large-scale demolitions, shelling attacks, and artillery strikes across southern Lebanon late Thursday and Friday, despite the U.S.-brokered ceasefire, Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported. Shortly after midnight, Israeli forces massive explosions in the Nabatieh district around Yahmar al-Shaqif, Arnoun, and Kfartebnit. The explosions, centered near Beaufort Castle, shattered windows and damaged homes in Qlayaa, while Lebanon's National Center for Geophysics said the blast generated seismic waves equivalent to a 3.8-magnitude earthquake. Israeli forces caves and homes around Al-Mansouri and Majdal Zoun in the Tyre (Sour) district on Friday. Forces also shelled Talousa in the Marjayoun district. Israeli troops illuminating shells at Ali Al-Taher hill on the outskirts of Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, "deliberately igniting" fires in the area, according to the NNA. Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri condemned the attacks, saying the 700 tons of explosives that generated tremors equivalent to an earthquake should "awaken national and human conscience" to Israel's "machinery of destruction." Lebanon 's Aoun seeks Turkish backing for U.S.-brokered framework with Israel: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun to Ankara on Thursday to meet Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, seeking Turkey's support for a U.S.-brokered framework agreement Lebanon signed with Israel in Washington on June 26. Aoun, who faces domestic opposition to the deal from Hezbollah and Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri, told Turkey's Anadolu Agency that implementation depends on "a complete Israeli withdrawal simultaneous with the deployment of the Lebanese army" and an international mechanism to verify compliance from both sides. U.S. News Mandela Barnes drops out of Wisconsin Democratic governor 's race: Former Wisconsin Lt. Gov. Mandela Barnes announced that he is exiting the Democratic primary for governor. The state's primary is August 11. Democratic socialist and state Rep.Francesca Hong now faces Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley , who re-entered the race earlier this month with the endorsement of outgoing Democratic Gov. Tony Evers. A Marquette University Law School poll released on Wednesday showed that Hong had the support of 38% of Democratic primary voters, and Crowley had only 7%, with 34% of voters remaining undecided and 16% preferring the now-withdrawn Barnes. A third of Democrats now identify as democratic socialists, CNN poll finds : About a third of Democrats and Democratic-leaning adults as democratic socialists, according to a CNN poll conducted by SSRS. The poll found democratic socialists tend to be younger, more likely to be extremely motivated to vote, and are also much more likely to be critical of Israel, with 48% saying they'd be enthusiastic about a candidate who wants to cut U.S. support to Israel, compared with 20% of non-democratic socialists. ExxonMobil and Chevron post combined $26.5 billion in second-quarter profits amid Iran war oil surge : ExxonMobil and Chevron combined second-quarter earnings of $26.5 billion, with Chevron posting record net income of $12.2 billion and ExxonMobil reporting $14.5 billion, as crude and petrol prices surged following the U.S. and Israeli attack on Iran in February. Exxon chief financial officer Neil Hansen said further price increases are possible if the Strait of Hormuz is closed to tanker traffic. Hansen told the FT that the "pain point" regarding oil prices was not with crude, which he said is trading within its historical ranges, but with products such as petrol and diesel, which have seen their prices surge as production capacity diminished. New York sues Kalshi, alleging prediction market platform runs "illegal gambling operation": New York state a lawsuit against the prediction market platform Kalshi on Friday, with Attorney General Letitia James alleging the company is operating illegally by accepting wagers without registering with the New York State Gaming Commission. The lawsuit seeks a permanent injunction, restitution to users, and financial penalties against the company, which is based in New York City. WSJ reports on Trump 's fundraising focus, nightly calls for multimillion dollar donations: President Donald Trump has personally directed a fundraising operation that has taken in more than $800 million since he returned to office, according to a Wall Street Journal report published on Thursday, with the president nightly calling his fundraiser Meredith O 'Rourke to press companies for donations ranging from $5 million to $50 million toward projects including his presidential library, a White House ballroom, and political committees. Companies including SoftBank, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta Platforms have made multimillion-dollar contributions, and executives told the Journal that donations appear linked to access and favorable regulatory treatment. "What can I do to help you?" Trump has told donors at multiple events, according to attendees. "What do you need?" he reportedly asked a group of CEOs at an event he hosted in Florida. The full report from the WSJ is available . 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News 60,000 cross from Morocco into Ceuta after border breach: At least 41 people have trying to reach the Spanish territory of Ceuta after breaching the border from Morocco with some 60,000 migrants entering the enclave in the past 24 hours. Ceuta, along with Melilla--another autonomous Spanish city in North Africa--represents the European Union's only land border with Africa. Migrants cross into Ceuta by land and sea, with people often swimming from the Moroccan town of Fnideq three miles away. Many of those who died drowned, while others were killed in a stampede to cross the border fence. Moroccan security forces clashed with thousands of people on the Moroccan side of the border as they tried to cross, using water cannons and firing warning shots into the air. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez travelled to Ceuta on Friday and called the crossings "a violation of Spain's territorial integrity." Spain's Ministry of Interior said some 25,000 people were returned from Ceuta to Morocco so far on Friday. According to the AP, authorities in both Ceuta and Madrid, linked the mass influx of migrants to a recent decision by Spain's Supreme Court that ruled migrants arriving by sea could not be summarily deported, unlike those who cross by land or climb the border fence. Sanchez said migrant smugglers misinterpreted the ruling, triggering the surge. Russia 's Africa Corps killed eight civilians in Mali air strike, HRW reports: Africa Corps, the Russian paramilitary group that has largely replaced the Wagner Group in Africa, eight civilians, including three children, in a June 15 air strike on the village of Kyrnia in Mali's central Mopti region, Human Rights Watch said Friday. The rights group noted no fighters from the al-Qaeda-linked group Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal Muslimin were believed to be killed in the strike despite the group controlling the village. Russian mercenaries have backed the Malian government's fight against JNIM and the Azawad Liberation Front, a Tuareg separatist group. The two rebel groups joined forces to launch nationwide, coordinated attacks on government installations starting in April. Attack on police checkpoint kills 11 officers in northwest Pakistan: An ambush on a police checkpoint in the Hangu district of Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province at least 11 police officers and injured 28 others late Wednesday. The attackers reportedly used explosive-laden quadcopters before storming the post near the Afghan border. Security forces said they killed 15 of the attackers in a subsequent hours-long gun battle. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, though it follows a suicide bombing claimed by the Pakistan Taliban that killed 27 people in nearby Tank district last week. Cuba details plans to open state economy to private industry: Cuba new details of its plans to privatize key sections of its economy, including easing land-use restrictions, letting businesses import fuel and medications, and authorizing private tourism companies to operate on the island, following a two-day National Assembly. Cuba has been subject to a fuel blockade and a stifling regime of sanctions since January, part of an explicit plan by the Trump administration to topple its government. President Miguel Diaz-Canel said the changes were not meant to appease Washington and insisted healthcare, science, culture and other strategic sectors would not be privatized. Milei signs decree allowing Argentina to expel foreigners who "spread hate" about the country: Argentine President Javier Milei an emergency decree empowering the government to bar, deport, or revoke the visas of foreigners who express "hate" toward Argentina or tarnish its national symbols following Argentina's second-place finish at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. FIFA opened a disciplinary probe into the Argentinian Football Association over behavior in a number of matches, investigating "team misconduct" and "discrimination and racist abuse." Milei has claimed without evidence that the criticism stems from a coordinated "anti-Argentina campaign" funded by leftists in Brazil, Mexico, and the U.S. Democratic Party, an accusation that prompted Brazil to recall its ambassador last weekend. Brazilian Supreme Court authorizes probe into Lula 's son: Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Andre Mendonca federal police to investigate Fabio Luis Lula da Silva, over suspicions he improperly helped businessman Antonio Carlos Camilo Antunes gain access to health ministry officials over a cannabidiol-based medication contract, Reuters reported on Thursday. Sudanese air force launches heavy strikes on RSF positions across Kordofan: Sudan's air force a wave of airstrikes on Rapid Support Forces positions across North and West Kordofan states, targeting locations including Um Badr, Sodari, Al-Khuwei and Al-Nuhud, according to Sudan Tribune. The strike wave followed a Sudanese army ground offensive over the weekend that secured a crucial road linking North Kordofan to Khartoum. Ukrainian drone sets Wildberries warehouse ablaze: A Ukrainian drone an energy facility and a warehouse in Russia's Volgograd region on Friday, the province's governor reported, injuring five. Wildberries, the Russian ecommerce giant which Ukraine's military has increasingly targeted in recent weeks, reported that one of its facilities caught fire as a result of the strike. Nepal 's PM calls for calm after Hindu-Muslim clashes leave three dead: Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah for calm after clashes between Hindu and Muslim groups in Nepal's Sunsari district, near the Indian border, left three people dead. The violence began Sunday over a dispute involving loud music and religious flags during a Hindu procession, and police killed two men while dispersing the crowd, a police spokesperson said. At least 32 miners killed in Balochistan coal mine explosion: At least 32 miners were , and three more remained trapped, after a methane gas explosion tore through a coal mine in Sorange, near Quetta in Pakistan's southwestern Balochistan province on Friday. British police arrest 77 at rally in support of Palestine Action: British police 77 people Thursday at a rally outside the Westminster Magistrates' Court, coinciding with hearings against those tried as terrorists for expressing support for Palestine Action, a group proscribed as a terrorist organization in the UK. It marked the first such demonstration since Andy Burnham became prime minister earlier this month. Separately Thursday, the UK's Supreme Court agreed to hear a new appeal against the group's"terrorist" designation. Mexico continues to buy Israeli weapons, despite Sheinbaum 's condemnations: Mexico more guns from Israel than from any other country last year, according to data included in Mexico's report to the UN Arms Trade Treaty and analysis by Stop U.S. Arms to Mexico. Mexico bought nearly 18,000 assault rifles, light machine guns, and pistols from Israel, 37% of its total firearm imports. | Letter from the Chair
---
One Vote Away from the Abyss: How Our Institutions Have Turned Socialistic and Propagandized
Fellow Republicans,
Look around. The institutions that once safeguarded liberty, truth, and the American way of life are no longer neutral referees. They have been steadily captured by democrat socialistic impulses and relentless propaganda. The evidence is daily, undeniable, and accelerating. And the hard truth is this: we are one vote--one election, one Senate seat, one Supreme Court appointment--away from descending even further into a system that prioritizes control over freedom, ideology over parents, and open borders over citizens.
The Media's Propaganda Machine
We observe it every single day. Mainstream media no longer reports news; it curates narratives. Anthony Fauci's recent congressional testimony and the admissions buried in his own government journals were largely ignored--except when outlets rushed to defend him. The same blackout greeted the recently released Biden tapes. When inconvenient facts threaten the preferred storyline, they simply vanish from the front page. This is not journalism. It is institutional propaganda designed to shield progressive orthodoxy and keep the public in the dark.
Nationalized Healthcare's Broken Promise
Socialism's track record on healthcare is on full display for anyone willing to look. During the recent FIFA matches, Canadians appeared in clips explaining why they crossed into the United States for care. They spoke of crushing waits and rationing back home, contrasted with the efficiency of American treatment--"get in and get out." These are not anecdotes from the distant past. They are live warnings of what government-run medicine delivers: delayed care, higher ultimate costs, and the quiet erosion of individual choice. Expanding that model here would not be compassion. It would be surrender.
Open Borders and the Erosion of Sovereignty
Just days ago, we watched masses of illegal immigrants come ashore off the coast of Spain, flooding towns and entering homes. The scenes were familiar because our own southern border towns lived them not long ago. Open borders are not humanitarian policy; they are the deliberate abandonment of national sovereignty. When institutions treat illegal entry as a right rather than a crime, they import instability, strain public resources, and signal that the rules no longer apply to those who follow them. A nation that cannot control its borders will not long control its destiny.
The Suppression of Faith
Remember the grandmothers. Under the Biden administration, elderly women praying peacefully outside abortion facilities were prosecuted and locked up. Biden's DOJ issued a memorandum listing Catholic churches as a threat and surveilled them.
The message was clear: certain forms of religious expression, especially those that challenge progressive sacred cows, will be treated as threats. When the state weaponizes law against quiet prayer, it is not defending rights--it is suppressing the moral foundations that once undergirded our culture. Faith is not optional window dressing in a free society. It is a bulwark against the soft tyranny of the administrative state.
The Assault on the Family and the Next Generation
Perhaps the most insidious advance of this socialistic mindset is the systematic undermining of the family. Schools increasingly indoctrinate rather than educate. Parental influence is treated as an obstacle. Christianity is scrubbed from classrooms while gender confusion is elevated as settled truth. The results speak for themselves: dismal proficiency scores, confused children, and a generation taught to distrust the very parents who love them. When institutions replace the family as the primary authority over children, they are not advancing progress--they are engineering dependency and division.
These are not isolated failures. They form a pattern: media that propagandizes, healthcare that nationalizes, borders that dissolve, faith that is punished, and families that are sidelined. Each step moves us closer to a society in which the individual serves the collective, and dissent is pathologized.
The conclusion is inescapable. We are one vote away from locking these trends into permanent power. The remedy is not despair or resignation. It is clarity, courage, and action at the ballot box and beyond. Support Republican candidates who will restore institutional neutrality, secure the border, defend parental rights, protect religious liberty, and reject the siren song of socialism. Speak the truth without apology. Demand accountability from every media outlet, school board, and agency that has forgotten its proper role.
America's institutions can still be reclaimed. But only if we refuse to look away--and only if we vote as if the future of the republic depends on it. Because it does.
Together, We Win!
In Liberty and in Truth,
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

It is institutional propaganda designed to shield progressive orthodoxy and keep the public in the dark. Nationalized Healthcare's Broken Promise Socialism's track record on healthcare is on full display for anyone willing to look. During the recent FIFA matches, Canadians appeared in clips explaining why they crossed into the United States for care. They spoke of crushing waits and rationing back home, contrasted with the efficiency of American treatment--"get in and get out." These are not anecdotes from the distant past. They are live warnings of what government-run medicine delivers: delayed care, higher ultimate costs, and the quiet erosion of individual choice. Expanding that model here would not be compassion. It would be surrender. Open Borders and the Erosion of Sovereignty Just days ago, we watched masses of illegal immigrants come ashore off the coast of Spain, flooding towns and entering homes. The scenes were familiar because our own southern border towns lived them not long ago. Open borders are not humanitarian policy; they are the deliberate abandonment of national sovereignty. When institutions treat illegal entry as a right rather than a crime, they import instability, strain public resources, and signal that the rules no longer apply to those who follow them. A nation that cannot control its borders will not long control its destiny. The Suppression of Faith Remember the grandmothers. Under the Biden administration, elderly women praying peacefully outside abortion facilities were prosecuted and locked up. Biden's DOJ issued a memorandum listing Catholic churches as a threat and surveilled them. The message was clear: certain forms of religious expression, especially those that challenge progressive sacred cows, will be treated as threats. When the state weaponizes law against quiet prayer, it is not defending rights--it is suppressing the moral foundations that once undergirded our culture. Faith is not optional window dressing in a free society. It is a bulwark against the soft tyranny of the administrative state. The Assault on the Family and the Next Generation Perhaps the most insidious advance of this socialistic mindset is the systematic undermining of the family. Schools increasingly indoctrinate rather than educate. Parental influence is treated as an obstacle. Christianity is scrubbed from classrooms while gender confusion is elevated as settled truth. The results speak for themselves: dismal proficiency scores, confused children, and a generation taught to distrust the very parents who love them. When institutions replace the family as the primary authority over children, they are not advancing progress--they are engineering dependency and division. These are not isolated failures. They form a pattern: media that propagandizes, healthcare that nationalizes, borders that dissolve, faith that is punished, and families that are sidelined. Each step moves us closer to a society in which the individual serves the collective, and dissent is pathologized. The conclusion is inescapable. We are one vote away from locking these trends into permanent power. The remedy is not despair or resignation. It is clarity, courage, and action at the ballot box and beyond. Support Republican candidates who will restore institutional neutrality, secure the border, defend parental rights, protect religious liberty, and reject the siren song of socialism. Speak the truth without apology. Demand accountability from every media outlet, school board, and agency that has forgotten its proper role. America's institutions can still be reclaimed. But only if we refuse to look away--and only if we vote as if the future of the republic depends on it. Because it does. Together, We Win! President Trump encouraged me to consider running in the Special Election by saying, "Run, Darline, Run!" Now, with the President's "Complete and Total Endorsement," I'm running to represent South Carolina for a full term in the United States Senate. I've spent a lot of time talking and praying with my family. This was not a decision I made lightly. I know it will be difficult, but I am ready. I know what Lindsey cared about, and we shared the same conservative values. He cared deeply about the people of South Carolina. With what I learned from Lindsey and my nearly 30 years of helping people of the state find dignity through work, I am ready to take on this next challenge. It's time for me to step up for South Carolina, just like Lindsey stepped up for me when our parents died. I've learned God often calls on ordinary people to do extraordinary things in the most challenging of times. I am not Lindsey. I have my own way of doing things. But we were raised with the same values: work hard each day, trust in the Lord, remember your roots, and never forget who you work for. I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot. Hey folks,
This was one of the more unexpected conversations we've had in a long time.
I sat down with [Clavicular](https://open.substack.com/users/533415121-clavicular?utm_source=mentions) --the internet's most infamous 20-year-old--to try to understand the person behind the headlines. We talked about 'looksmaxxing', the male loneliness epidemic, masculinity, social media, politics, self-improvement, and what it actually means to build a life worth living. We agreed on more than I expected, disagreed where it mattered, and by the end, I think we got somewhere real.
This one isn't about scoring points. It's about asking better questions. Don't miss it.
* **00:01:07** -- We jump right into the biggest question: why someone so closely associated with MAGA personalities insists he's completely apolitical--and whether that's actually possible.
* **00:10:33** -- The conversation turns to the male loneliness epidemic, dating, and why Clavicular believes "looksmaxxing" has become such a powerful movement among young men.
* **00:17:03** -- We debate what really makes someone attractive: appearance, personality, purpose, career, confidence, or some combination of all of them.
* **00:28:59** -- We dig into the pressure of internet fame, streaming culture, viral moments, and the responsibility that comes with influencing millions of young people.
* **00:44:00** -- The conversation ends on a surprisingly thoughtful note about values, growth, Maslow's hierarchy of needs, and what it means to become a well-rounded person instead of just chasing attention.

At its core, this conversation is about something much bigger than social media. It's about the pressures facing young men, the search for identity, and whether self-improvement is enough if it only focuses on the outside. Even where we disagreed, I appreciated the willingness to stay in the conversation. If you're trying to understand why these movements resonate--and what we're missing in the broader conversation--this is a must-watch. If you value honest conversations like this, help me keep them going.

# [No Scrubs](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=209160362&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA5MTYwMzYyLCJpYXQiOjE3ODU1MTM4NzAsImV4cCI6MTc4ODEwNTg3MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.4ce0tgEVHKDxEUXg6lA3DCc2yay8q_nOhe9i_kfrmrI)
### How my first car is inspiring this campaign as we speed to the final end-of-month deadline of the primary
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Jul 31
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/no-scrubs?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-restack-comment&action=restack-comment&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA5MTYwMzYyLCJpYXQiOjE3ODU1MTM4NzAsImV4cCI6MTc4ODEwNTg3MCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.4ce0tgEVHKDxEUXg6lA3DCc2yay8q_nOhe9i_kfrmrI&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/no-scrubs?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

My first car was a used Oldsmobile Cutlass Supreme.
I loved that car and I was so dang proud to drive it. I remember driving to school with the windows rolled down, grinning from ear to ear with my CD player blasting TLC's "No Scrubs."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6ba2c540-9bba-479c-a21f-5d118b92c19c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I couldn't wait to drive that car around Michigan. It meant I owned a small piece of my state.
An Oldsmobile: a car designed in Michigan by a Michigan company - somebody's dad, somebody's mom, somebody's neighbor, somebody in my state who literally clocked in and created the thing I was driving. Incredible.
You don't forget that feeling.**Driving around your own state in something your own people made possible.** That's a specific kind of pride, and I don't know if folks in other states quite have that feeling.
My friend Debbie Stabenow says something I think about a lot: In Michigan, we make things and we grow things.
That's special.
The Cutlass Supreme seats were plush. Big, soft, cushy bench seats, like taking your grandma's den for a drive down I-96. And the engine was relentless - from cold Michigan winter mornings or zipping up a hill. Tough as nails.
**That 's Michigan right there. Tough, with a big heart. Made of grit and kindness.** Michiganders work hard, get covered in grime - and then at the end of the day we clean up and bring a casserole to the neighbor who's having a rough week.
I've been thinking about that Oldsmobile a lot lately. Because that engine could take a beating - and right now, a whole lot of folks in this state are taking one.
I was knocking on doors in Detroit on a hot afternoon, standing on a porch while a mom told me about her insurance premium going up again and again. I was in a grocery store watching folks put hamburger meat back on the shelf because the price was just too darn high.
I've been in union halls and diners and on picket lines, drinking coffee with folks and doing a lot of listening because here's my honest belief about this job: Listening and learning come first. **You cannot fix a problem you don 't truly understand.**
And I understand things are hard right now. Washington is a mess. Michiganders have been paying the price of Trump's affordability crisis every single day - at the pump, at the register, at the pharmacy counter. And instead of giving relief to Michigan families, Republicans want to hand Trump tens of billions of your tax dollars for a reckless war in Iran.
It's unacceptable.
Some people just want to yell about it. I'm fighting to fix it.
That's the whole reason I'm in this race. **Slogans and celebrity don 't win elections. They sure as heck don't lower anybody's grocery bill.**
I'm running to be the relentless engine for Michigan. Somebody who gets the job done.
That's what I'm trying to do right now in this race. But we're speeding toward the finish line, and I need your help to fill the tank. The primary is Tuesday, and tonight at midnight is our final end-of-month deadline.
Right now, it's all about having the resources to fund our get-out-the-vote push. The next four days are the whole ball game. The polls show I'm the best Democrat to defeat Mike Rogers, but that doesn't mean anything if we don't reach critical voters.
Our organizers are heading into the busiest weekend of this entire campaign so far - phones, doors, texts, and a whole lot of reminding folks that Tuesday is the big day. It's unglamorous work. But those good folks do it with clipboards and sore feet because they believe in sending somebody who was made in Michigan and ready to get stuff done to the U.S. Senate.
That grit and doggedness is how close primaries get won - not with likes on an Instagram account, just Michiganders talking to our neighbors.
**If you 're able, will you chip in before midnight tonight to power that final push and help us hit our last end-of-month deadline before the primary?** No pressure, and I'm not asking for a fortune; 20 or 30 bucks would help support our team's work more than you know.
[DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/6ba2c540-9bba-479c-a21f-5d118b92c19c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
That Cutlass is gone, but I'm still the girl who loves Michigan, still so proud to be a Michigander, and ready to keep fighting for the people I love.
Tough as nails, big hearts, full speed ahead.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/6ba2c540-9bba-479c-a21f-5d118b92c19c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Elon Musk wants me out of Congress — and he's prepared to spend a fortune to do it.
Yesterday, the Times reported that Musk — the richest man on the planet — has authorized his super PAC to spend at least $100 million to help Republicans take back the House this fall. It's a paid, boots-on-the-ground operation. It starts next month. Washington is on his target list, which means he’s coming for this district.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/mgpvf-dsg-email?]
Sit with what that means. One man. More money, by himself, than entire political party committees have in the bank. And he's decided that a mechanic from Southwest Washington who won't take corporate PAC money is a problem worth spending millions to erase.
And he isn't even the whole story — he's the newest piece of it. Donald Trump is sitting on a $400 million war chest he hasn't opened yet, with his team promising it starts "very soon." Dear Friend, This week's email is about disguises. In Wyoming, a group with "Prosperity" in its name is spending big to take out the most conservative legislature in America.In West Virginia, a surveillance dragnet is being sold as "public safety." The good news? Our folks in the states are ripping the masks off, and now the whole country is watching them do it.
---
|
---
**WYOMING** You've probably heard of Americans for Prosperity. It's an organization that markets itself as conservative, but is endorsing the most LIBERAL candidates in Wyoming's August 18 Republican primaries...against the **Wyoming Freedom Caucus** , the most conservative lawmakers in the state. Don't take my word for it. Our friends at the Institute for Legislative Analysis ran the numbers using their GOP Platform scorecard, which rates lawmakers from 0 to 100 based on how their votes stack up against the Republican platform.Every AFP endorsee with a voting record lands in Democrat territory: Ogden Driskill at 47%. Evie Brennan at 50%. Julie Jarvis at 32%. Tony Niemiec at 27%! The conservatives they want gone score between 87% and 97%. AFP's other six picks have no legislative record at all. The chart below tells the whole story. And look who's in the crosshairs: our friend **Rep. John Bear** (97%), the same John Bear who helped deliver the monster property tax cut featured in this week's Radio Clip. So who's running this operation? Tyler Lindholm, AFP's Wyoming state director. A little history is in order. Lindholm was a state representative until August 18, 2020, when **Wyoming Freedom Caucus member Chip Neiman** beat him in the Republican primary. Chip is now Speaker of the Wyoming House and one of the strongest conservative leaders in the country. Six years later, Lindholm's organization is bankrolling the effort to stop Chip's state Senate bid, endorsing 47% Ogden Driskill. Lindholm told Cowboy State Daily that his endorsed candidates' "votes speak for themselves." On that point, we agree completely. The votes say 27%, 32%, 47%, and 50%. PRO-TIP to Wyoming voters: when a group with "Prosperity" in the name endorses candidates who vote like Democrats, trust the scorecard, not the brochure. The full ratings are at [GOPScorecard.com](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTjmY2AIel-2BnWqkMPNGZPnZyXyL-2FJeb5ou-2Fau1v-2BJi-2FhxWrbXcfiyJsADgnw0SYADnjqOLAA2hbN6q285C31eq2c0-3DMUnE_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHer6IBXnguCro5DorXtcI6ns4pgj-2FAy2gLshU016ePpZn-2BQzbNihEwuaiUEzd-2Bez8sq6VdSrKULDCEPkpnVJy98oL5sUgxPI6qm58AlW0kbi7UTVFBhvYOo9Uzc5YZ-2BY9HFPHVk6TGm1Pp02TxU2MU9mO0w9mRYGx-2B9K9j56wcgZs71dSTlu7bAk6IKjhVINMm6pUzupNBOAZzPOp2kjyagSW1f79-2BmOin22bFUWd007sA-3D).

**WEST VIRGINIA** Last week we told you about your **West Virginia Freedom Caucus** and their fight to rip out the Flock surveillance cameras tracking law-abiding citizens across their state. This week, Fox News picked up the story, and the whole country is now watching Charleston. Here's the fight. Flock cameras are AI-powered license plate readers that photograph every passing vehicle and build a database of where innocent West Virginians drive, worship, work, and see their doctors. West Virginia Freedom Caucus chairman, **Delegate Chris Anders** , gave Fox the line of the week: "George Orwell's 1984 was intended as a warning, not an instruction manual. We should be striving for more 1776, not more 1984." The caucus has the solution ready to go. The Fourth Amendment Restoration Act would prohibit warrantless use of license plate readers, facial recognition, and surveillance drones. Police can still investigate crimes. They just need a warrant based on probable cause, exactly what the Constitution has required for 230 years.So why isn't it law? Ask the Charleston Swamp. The bill has been introduced two years running, and two years running, Republican House leadership buried it without a debate or a vote. Speaker Roger Hanshaw and Judiciary Chairman JB Akers own that decision. Meanwhile, the surveillance state keeps growing: Huntington's mayor and city council just approved a $2.1 MILLION Flock contract covering the city in AI cameras, gunshot detectors, and automatically dispatched drones. More than 50 citizens showed up to oppose it. Even the ACLU is suing to stop it. When the Freedom Caucus and the ACLU end up on the same side, the government has REALLY overstepped. Your WVFC isn't waiting around. The caucus has pledged to use every procedural tool in both chambers to force an up-or-down vote on the Fourth Amendment Restoration Act.Buckle up, Charleston.

**RADIO CLIP OF THE WEEK** **Wyoming Freedom Caucus member State Rep. John Bear** joined the show to talk about a number every homeowner in his state can see on their tax bill: 25%. That's the property tax cut Wyoming homeowners received this year on the first $1 million of their home's value.Not a one-time rebate. Not a temporary gimmick. PERMANENT. John calls it the largest tax relief in Wyoming history, and he's clear about why it happened: your **Wyoming Freedom Caucus** runs the House, and they made it happen. name: R. Cooper
subject: A few things that might convince you
body:
Our end-of-month fundraising deadline is at midnight, and we’re not where we need to be to hit our goal.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk860&source=&t=1&akid=2396%2E124072%2EZOKi5L)
| | | |

| | Peter, we don’t have much time. **Our end-of-month fundraising deadline is at midnight, and we’re not where we need to be to hit our goal.** I’m hoping there’s something I can say to convince you to [**_make your first $7 donation to my U.S. Senate campaign right now to help me out._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk860&amount=7&t=8&akid=2396%2E124072%2EZOKi5L)

---
| | **Republicans are going all in to defeat me, because if we lose in North Carolina, Democrats will lose our chance to take back the Senate. That’s what is at stake in this race – and that’s why I’m asking:**
---
| | [**_Will you chip in your first $7 now to help us reach our crucial end-of-month goal so we can fight back against GOP attacks, protect our slim polling lead and flip North Carolina blue? I need you, Peter._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk860&amount=7&t=9&akid=2396%2E124072%2EZOKi5L)

Roy Cooper

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136373518/637236038/2134884402?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_EOM10_260731_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNDE4MzMxMS1mZDhjLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Lu654LZsY3R63aLcIdOVLDTqDytCMy9gcc-fi3N2m8k=) Thank you, Derek.

This is one of the most challenging times I have ever seen over the course of my time in public service.

This president has launched us into a war-of-choice overseas without a clear strategy, is kicking millions of Americans off their health insurance while giving tax breaks to those at the very top – and is still obsessed with conspiracy theories about an election he lost six years ago.

**And maybe worst of all, I have been deeply disappointed to see far too many of my Republican colleagues bend to Trump’s demands – no matter how dangerous or just downright stupid they are.**

Derek, during times like these, it would be easy to get discouraged. But as I travel the Commonwealth and talk to voters about the issues that matter the most to them, I see folks who are fired up to flip Congress blue and finally put some guardrails on this administration run amok.

**The support and enthusiasm for this campaign is humbling – and I am so grateful for grassroots supporters like you who have stepped up time and time again at critical moments.**

Now, we’re facing another pivotal deadline – and I need to ask for your help yet again. This is one of our final end-of-month fundraising pushes of the election. The support we receive before midnight helps us buy more time on the airwaves, hire more staff, knock on more doors, and host more events all across Virginia in the coming months.

# [Apple beats estimates while AI memory costs crush tech cash](https://substack.com/redirect/120ab821-1c08-4c03-8edc-09eb68490176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Apple exceeded third-quarter expectations with $109.4 billion in revenue and strong iPhone sales of $54.2 billion, but shares fell as Services and China missed **[while memory constraints from the AI boom darkened guidance.](https://substack.com/redirect/10f0da6e-94b1-4ab8-a79b-788db673fa1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/120ab821-1c08-4c03-8edc-09eb68490176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **iPhone sales drive beat** : iPhone revenue climbed to $54.2 billion from $44.5 billion a year earlier, topping the $53.5 billion estimate and helping overall revenue reach $109.4 billion against $108.8 billion expected.
* **Services China miss targets** : Services generated $30.7 billion, **[below the $31.3 billion forecast,](https://substack.com/redirect/b79723bf-a08a-4223-8990-5545b84285fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** while Greater China contributed $18.8 billion versus the $19.5 billion analysts anticipated for the quarter.
* **Memory prices force hikes** : Soaring memory costs from AI demand led Apple to raise Mac and iPad prices with iPhone hikes expected, as Tim Cook warned of rises beyond September before stepping down.
* **Hyperscalers face cash strain** : Amazon, Alphabet and Tesla reported negative cash flow while Meta's generation plunged 91%, with AI spending projected at $765 billion this year and Amazon lifting capex to $220 billion.

# [$45B AI fund crashes to $10B in brutal fire sale](https://substack.com/redirect/120ab821-1c08-4c03-8edc-09eb68490176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner's Situational Awareness hedge fund **[plunged from a $45 billion peak to around $10 billion](https://substack.com/redirect/bbe8879e-f837-4e5a-81e8-69b1cf96f4ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after leverage-driven margin calls forced a fire sale of all public stock positions to Citadel.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/120ab821-1c08-4c03-8edc-09eb68490176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Leverage triggers forced sale** : **[Reported leverage of up to 400% amid tumbling semiconductor stocks](https://substack.com/redirect/0cf73889-de8c-4264-bba5-7f9c93c5fe8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** forced the fund to sell all leveraged public equity bets including SK Hynix and CoreWeave.
* **Citadel buys at discount** : Ken Griffin's Citadel acquired the positions at a discount as prime brokers including Bank of America, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan managed the margin calls.
* **AI stocks drive losses** : Portfolio holdings such as Nebius, Sandisk, Micron and CoreWeave fell more than 35% this month while short positions in software like Adobe moved against it.
* **Gains reverse amid wedding** : The fund had posted more than 1,000% returns since its 2024 launch before the crash, which coincides with Aschenbrenner's wedding this weekend.

# [Chip stocks explode higher as Lam Research and memory names surge](https://substack.com/redirect/120ab821-1c08-4c03-8edc-09eb68490176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Semiconductor shares rocketed higher after strong earnings from Microsoft and Lam Research, **[with Lam climbing 18% for its best day since 1999](https://substack.com/redirect/115de057-9cb9-4eb3-8ea8-1ccc7f63964e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and memory stocks surging on Samsung's warning of a prolonged crunch into 2028.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/120ab821-1c08-4c03-8edc-09eb68490176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Lam Research posts big gain** : Lam Research shares climbed 18% after reporting strong earnings and guidance driven by artificial intelligence demand, marking the company's best day since 1999.
* **Memory stocks rebound hard** : Micron rose 18% and Sandisk jumped 26% after Samsung warned the memory crunch could last into 2028, reversing recent underwhelming SK Hynix results.
* **Broader chip rally spreads** : Advanced Micro Devices gained 13%, Applied Materials 15%, Intel 11%, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF rose 8% as AI infrastructure demand fueled the rebound.
* **Arm sees strong demand** : Arm Holdings advanced 7% after CEO Rene Haas said demand for its first in-house AGI CPU has surpassed $2 billion across fiscal 2027 and 2028.

# [Novo Nordisk shares crash after heart drug trial fails](https://substack.com/redirect/120ab821-1c08-4c03-8edc-09eb68490176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Novo Nordisk shares **[fell as much as 10% after its experimental heart medicine Ziltivekimab](https://substack.com/redirect/2d8d6f4d-a96f-443e-80df-2cbe6b748448?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** failed to show a statistically meaningful reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events in a late-stage trial of more than 6,300 patients.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/120ab821-1c08-4c03-8edc-09eb68490176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Trial misses key endpoint** : Ziltivekimab did not achieve a statistically meaningful reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events versus placebo in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease.
* **Biological effect falls short** : The medicine showed some biological effect by blocking the IL-6 pathway but that did not translate into clinical benefit on cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack or stroke.
* **Company remains committed** : Chief scientific officer Martin Holst Lange said the result does not change Novo Nordisk's strategic commitment to cardiovascular disease despite the disappointment.
* **Pipeline faces fresh pressure** : The miss is the latest blow as the company races to restore investor confidence amid intense competition from Eli Lilly and prior setbacks in its obesity pipeline.

# [Wider losses hammer Coinbase, shares tumble on revenue miss](https://substack.com/redirect/120ab821-1c08-4c03-8edc-09eb68490176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Coinbase shares **[dropped more than 7% after the crypto exchange posted a wider-than-expected second-quarter loss](https://substack.com/redirect/3b6c6485-afa4-4e5f-8b8f-8e88ca387d56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of $1.36 per share and revenue of $1.2 billion that missed Wall Street estimates amid ongoing crypto market weakness.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/120ab821-1c08-4c03-8edc-09eb68490176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Loss widens beyond forecasts** : Coinbase reported a loss of $359.5 million or $1.36 per share against expectations of a 17 cent loss, compared with a $1.43 billion profit a year earlier.
* **Revenue declines year over year** : Second-quarter revenue fell to $1.2 billion from $1.5 billion a year ago and missed the $1.3 billion forecast, marking the third straight quarterly miss.
* **Subscriptions offer bright spot** : Subscription revenue reached $555 million while transaction revenue was $599 million, though both missed expectations and declined from the prior year.
* **CEO highlights market share** : Brian Armstrong said Coinbase reached an all-time high in crypto trading market share and is no longer just a bet on the price of bitcoin.

* * *
* * *
# [Amazon stock surges as AWS growth smashes every estimate](https://substack.com/redirect/120ab821-1c08-4c03-8edc-09eb68490176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Amazon shares **[jumped more than 13% after second-quarter results showed AWS revenue climbing 36.7%](https://substack.com/redirect/35167cd0-2924-49dc-ba14-6033ff6e9fa7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to $42.2 billion, with AI and custom chip businesses each topping a $25 billion annualized run rate and capital spending raised to $220 billion.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/120ab821-1c08-4c03-8edc-09eb68490176?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **AWS delivers record growth** : AWS generated $42.2 billion in second-quarter revenue, up 36.7% year over year, after adding $4.6 billion quarter over quarter -- about 80% more than its largest prior increase.
* **AI chips hit milestones** : Amazon said its AI services and custom chip businesses have each surpassed a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate amid surging demand for inference and cloud capacity.
* **Capex guidance rises higher** : The company raised its capital expenditures forecast to approximately $220 billion from prior guidance of around $200 billion to support AI infrastructure already booked into 2028.
* **Analysts call it home run** : CFRA Research described the quarter as a home run, noting AWS now runs at about a $170 billion annual revenue rate, more than four times its 2019 level.
