name: Ben Blom
subject: The old-growth forests of the future
body:
Dear Peter,

We measure the lives of redwoods in centuries, not years. To heal these forests takes time, expertise, and a long-term commitment to see the job through.

Taking on these kinds of ambitious projects—and seeing them through—is what Save the Redwoods has done for more than 100 years. Now, with our Redwoods Rising initiative, we are seeking to restore more than 70,000 acres of forests once damaged by industrial logging.

If we can give these young, damaged forests a second chance, they will grow into the old-growth forests of the future. But to do that, we need people like you with us.

We have a funding deadline coming up tonight at midnight. Your gift will help us keep this season’s restoration projects moving forward and put damaged forests on a path to healing. [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising?sourceid=1170310&ms=RR_EM14&utm_campaign=K2D-1170310&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email]

SUPPORT REDWOODS RISING [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising?sourceid=1170310&ms=RR_EM14&utm_campaign=K2D-1170310&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email]

This work doesn’t happen overnight. But we can already see the fruits of our labor: streams flowing free and clear, fish returning to restored habitats, and young redwoods growing strong.

If that’s what we’ve been able to achieve in just a short time, can you imagine how these forests will look in another 20 or 30 years?

If you've been considering a gift, I hope you'll make one before midnight tonight. Your support will make that healthy, thriving future possible for these forests. [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising?sourceid=1170310&ms=RR_EM14&utm_campaign=K2D-1170310&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email]

Sincerely,
Ben Blom
Director of Stewardship and Restoration

P.S. Redwoods Rising is one of the most ambitious restoration efforts in the history of the redwood range. Please make your gift before tonight's deadline and help keep this work moving forward. [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/redwoodsrising?sourceid=1170310&ms=RR_EM14&utm_campaign=K2D-1170310&utm_source=ea-fundraising&utm_medium=email]

Taking on these kinds of ambitious projects—and seeing them through—is what Save the Redwoods has done for more than 100 years. Now, with our Redwoods Rising initiative, we are seeking to restore more than 70,000 acres of forests once damaged by industrial logging. If we can give these young, damaged forests a second chance, they will grow into the old-growth forests of the future. But to do that, we need people like you with us. We have a funding deadline coming up tonight at midnight. Your gift will help us keep this season’s restoration projects moving forward and put damaged forests on a path to healing. [] SUPPORT REDWOODS RISING [] This work doesn’t happen overnight. But we can already see the fruits of our labor: streams flowing free and clear, fish returning to restored habitats, and young redwoods growing strong. If that’s what we’ve been able to achieve in just a short time, can you imagine how these forests will look in another 20 or 30 years? If you've been considering a gift, I hope you'll make one before midnight tonight. Your support will make that healthy, thriving future possible for these forests. [] Sincerely, Ben Blom Director of Stewardship and Restoration P.S. Redwoods Rising is one of the most ambitious restoration efforts in the history of the redwood range. **This fight is what democracy actually looks like,** not some PAC check or a curated press release timed to a news cycle. My slogan is **HOMETOWNS OVER HEADLINES** , and it reads that way for a reason.
I am Mike Cortese and I have been in rooms like this one all across Tennessee's 4th District for the past year and a half. I have heard from seniors who are rationing prescriptions and parents who can't afford their kids' healthcare since Scott DesJarlais voted to gut Medicaid. My run for Congress is rooted in working people who do everything right and still feel like Washington has forgotten they exist, and **[I need help to keep our fight up. I came to Nashville 24 years ago. My wife and I survived things most politicians wouldn't survive publicly. We fought for our family against impossible odds and came out the other side with the absolute conviction that this district deserves better than 15 years of silence from a man who has delivered nothing.

# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136374965/637237339/-664395954?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS84OTkxNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMTE0YjNhNS1mZThjLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sz22I7DWsdDMRVqYzrgODu9pMOtSCVHNqrQ-Nqrh_yc=)
Hi friend – Chelsey Wininger here, DASS Executive Director. When people ask me what drives the work at DASS, I always come back to the same answer: it's about stopping extremists from taking over the offices that run our elections. With less than 100 days until Election Day, election deniers are on the ballot for Secretary of State in state after state. Candidates who've flirted with fake elector schemes. Candidates who have said -- on the record -- that they'll only certify results they personally agree with. Let me repeat that. People running right now to oversee elections in their states have told voters, plainly, that they'll decide which results count, or don’t. **And in November, there are 26 Secretary of State races on the ballot across the country -- including in swing states like Nevada, Arizona, and Michigan.** Those aren't just battleground states for 2026. body:
Meet Jim Risch's Achilles Heel

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
###
### Peter —
This week, the disruption in Idaho’s Senate race opened up a new viable path for our independent to win. The Democratic nominee dropped out of the race, narrowing the field and leaving it a one-on-one race between Todd Achilles, an independent Army veteran, and Jim Risch, the 83-year-old Republican incumbent. In a state President Trump won by 36 points, this is a real opportunity to compete in a deep-red state, and most notably, Achilles has been consistently polling ahead with voters informed about him. Until this week, the conventional wisdom said that no matter how strong an independent candidate might be, a Democrat on the ballot in a deep-red state would split the non-Republican vote and hand the incumbent an easy win. That math just changed. David Roth, the Democratic nominee, had raised less than $10,000 before stepping aside. Achilles has raised almost 100 times more than that! Todd Achilles served his country as an Army officer and tank commander and then came home and built a career as a telecom executive, college professor, and state legislator. He ran for Senate as an independent because he saw the dissatisfaction happening in Idaho that stemmed from Washington leaders. Farmers being hit with tariffs and veterans exhausted from partisan dysfunction are growing more and more disenchanted by the day in Idaho--all while their incumbent, Jim Risch, has **not held a town hall in 18 years.** This ballot change matters not just for Idaho but for the entire country and for everything the Forward Party has been building toward.
* * *
The strategy at play here is something we have pushed for years. The Senate today operates with margins so narrow that a small number of members not beholden to either party could determine the balance of power on every vote. They would not be a majority but a bloc that neither party could control or ignore. This is where we have a game of numbers. **You don't need 51 independent senators to change the Senate. You only need 3 or 4.** In a chamber that regularly deadlocks on party lines, 3 or 4 members who answer only to their constituents would be the most powerful voting bloc in Washington. This is a golden opportunity to show that we can improve American politics from outside the two-party system rather than waiting for the system to fix itself. No one in American politics thought that Idaho’s Senate seat would be contested, but here we are. That is what we are trying to build. And as of Tuesday, the map just became more realistic than it has ever been. That map includes polls now showing Independent [Seth Bodnar](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=W3VAJIDBoH9PlhvL-POstDOPdnZt0CWRKj8nu_hf-EY&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_110&n=1) ahead of the Republican in Montana if it’s one-on-one and Independent [Brian Bengs](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=AOXa9YXuTRM2xxte2I3Ke1GDXXw3bCn9OSm_Ql1nxPN6L4MP7d39e_ip-9ibHlfO&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_110&n=2) ahead of the Republican in South Dakota. Each of them has raised 4 times more than the Democrat in the race. The map could spread further than anyone had imagined. |
## **The Lineup for Change in the Senate**
### **Idaho**
**Todd Achilles - U.S. Senate** One-on-one as of Tuesday. Democrat dropped out. Achilles leads Risch in polling on informed ballot.
### **Montana**
**Seth Bodnar - U.S. Senate** Polling ahead of the Republican one-on-one. Raised 4x more than the Democrat in the race. Approximately 30,000 petition signatures submitted across 52 of 56 counties. We are watching for a similar development in Idaho.
### **South Dakota**
**Brian Bengs - U.S. Senate** Polling ahead of the Republican one-on-one. Raised 4x more than the Democrat. A Navy and Air Force veteran and law professor. The Democrat remains on the ballot, but the race has a similar dynamic to Montana.
### **Colorado**
**Bob Chew \- U.S. Senate** Running on the Forward Party ballot line against Sen. Hickenlooper. A large ad buy is running statewide. He has over $1m cash on hand to compete with.
---
**The Forward Party has been building the infrastructure for this moment.** The results are starting to show up where it counts: on the ballot, in the polls, and now in a one-on-one race that nobody thought was possible six months ago.

I am in, President Trump! | Fellow Patriot, With less than two weeks to go, The legacy my brother, Lindsey, built can never be replicated, but I can honor him by working as hard as he did, every single day, for the people of South Carolina. President Trump encouraged me to run in the upcoming Senate Special Election by saying: "Run, Darline, Run!" That endorsement isn't just an honor. It's a call to action. The President knows South Carolina needs a fighter who will finish what my brother started, and he's counting on us to deliver. I intend to earn every vote because that's what this job demands, and that's what South Carolina deserves. But here's the truth: My opponents are self-funding millionaires or have spent years stockpiling campaign cash. I'm new to this. The Special Election Primary is August 11th - just 11 days away. Every dollar raised between now and then determines whether we can compete on the airwaves, get out the vote, and win. There is no "catching up later." This is the moment. > ****Hi Peter,
>
> There are a lot of political events every year.
>
> **There is only one Fancy Farm.**
>
> Every August, candidates, elected officials from both sides of the aisle, reporters, and thousands of Kentuckians gather in a Western Kentucky church parish for one of our most beloved political traditions. There’s a raffle. There’s a LOT of barbecue. There’s community, faith, and service.
>
> And yes, there are more than a few good-natured jokes, jabs, and jeers in the day’s speeches. My team and I are hard at work getting ready for me to take the stage this Saturday.
>

> | | **What issues do you think I should make sure to cover at Fancy Farm?** Your concerns and challenges, your dreams, the issues you’re talking about around your kitchen table — _those_ are the things that drive my work. **[So I want to make sure I’m speaking to what’s on your mind.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136377168/637243566/-56925754?refcode=20260731_RA_EN_FANCYFARM_2&refcode2=7cff0089-018d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MjEwMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3Y2ZmMDA4OS0wMThkLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=73VvJ9WfISgQmz-xR9Jn9lJxlQUkmcD_3kH9pvAXx3Q=&emci=264949b7-2c8c-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=7cff0089-018d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=7807262)**

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: A hair’s breadth
body:
Taking back Texas this year is in our sights.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter —
I need you to sit with this number for a second: **one point.**
That's it. That's the entire gap between me and Greg Abbott right now, according to a brand-new Fox News poll — yes, Fox News.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260731_2_onepoint.dNGRt7&refcode=em20260731-1710&t=1&akid=1710%2E299639%2EjArb3d)
In nearly twelve years as governor, through three elections, Greg Abbott has never faced a poll this close. _Not once._ His campaign has already spent over $54 million this cycle just to hang on to power. This poll says people aren’t buying what he’s selling anymore.
Here's why it's happening: Texans are falling behind financially, and they know exactly who's been in charge while it happened. Nearly 4 in 10 Texans say inflation is the top issue on their minds — **and after 12 years of Greg Abbott, they're done waiting around for things to get better.**
I'm not surprised. I've been hearing it at every stop — from Brownsville to Austin to Amarillo. Families are tired of watching their grocery bills and insurance premiums climb while Abbott hands billions to his donors.
**This 1-point poll shows that a new chapter for Texas is finally in reach.** But it’s not guaranteed. Turnout will decide this election. And Abbott's team knows it — they're going to spend the next 95 days doing everything they can to make sure Texans who are ready for change don't show up to the polls to vote. They will do anything to keep Texans from turning the page on his failed administration.
I can't outspend Greg Abbott, and I don’t need to. Our campaign can out-organize him, but that takes people like you stepping up right now to raise the resources we need to win this race.
**[Can you chip in $15 today to help us keep closing this gap and — finally — take back Texas?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1374?c0=em_ms_gh_20260731_2_onepoint.M74SQ6&refcode=em20260731-1710&t=2&akid=1710%2E299639%2EjArb3d)**

We've never been this close. Let's make sure we don't waste this opportunity.
Gina

I've never believed this office should be about advancing a political career or personal agenda. It should be about showing up, doing the work, and fighting for the people who sent me to Washington, DC in the first place.

And that's what I've strived to do every day. Whether it's protecting access to health care, lowering costs for families, standing up to powerful special interests, supporting farmers and small businesses, or working to pass bills that make a real difference, my focus has always been on delivering results for you and your family.

body:

| | | | | [|

**PRESS RELEASE**

**Dan Green’s “Two Minutes” Remark Raises Questions About His Commitment to Florida’s Entire 9th District**

Green’s comment leaves voters asking: Are families in Belle Isle, Lake Nona, Kissimmee, St. Cloud, Frostproof, Avon Park, Sebring, Moore Haven, and everywhere in between worthy of his time?
---
|
---
| | July 31, 2026Contact: [Justin@VoteJustinStory.com](mailto:justin@votejustinstory.com?subject=&body=)
---
| | **ST. CLOUD, FL** — Republican congressional candidate Justin Story’s campaign today raised serious questions about whether opponent Dan Green is prepared to serve every community in Florida’s expansive 9th Congressional District after Green stated in a recently recorded video: “You should drive two minutes to see your representative, not two hours in another city.”
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/13Y3rnW0Jsl?e=90ad5fc3c5&c2id=d60c3f7cebee07fc4dcb3011da999329)
| |
“Florida’s 9th District is not one neighborhood or one city,” Story said. “It stretches across portions of Orange, Osceola, Polk, Indian River, Okeechobee, Highlands, and Glades counties — from Belle Isle and Lake Nona to Kissimmee and St. Cloud, down through Frostproof, Avon Park, and Sebring to Moore Haven. The next member of Congress must be willing to show up for every constituent, whether that person lives two minutes away or two hours away.”
Green, who lists a Vero Beach address on his candidate filing, made the remark while discussing access to representation. Serving in Congress, however, requires representing numerous communities, towns, and cities, not only the voters who live closest to a candidate.
“Our citizens are already not represented in Washington,” Story said. “The last thing we need is someone who has already decided some of us aren’t worth the drive. If Dan Green considers traveling two hours to meet voters an unacceptable burden, how will he approach constituent service after the election? Campaigning for Congress is a job interview. The people deserve a candidate willing to put in the work before Election Day and continue doing so afterward.”
Story pledged that, when elected, he will continue traveling throughout the district to listen to voters and will work to establish accessible district offices serving its different regions.
“The people of Florida’s 9th District deserve a representative who shows up,” Story said. “They deserve no shortcuts and no excuses. They deserve strong, determined, principled conservative leadership for every community in the district.”
**About Justin Story** Justin Story is a sixth-generation Central Floridian who grew up in St. Cloud. A retired Marine Corps officer and former F/A-18 combat fighter pilot, he is running for Congress to serve the people, not to build a political career. He and his wife Maria, who fled the communist regime in Venezuela, are raising their family in St. Cloud.
For more information or to get involved, visit [http://votejustinstory.com ](https://us.list-manage.com/LmOjwBO_8dJ?e=90ad5fc3c5&c2id=d60c3f7cebee07fc4dcb3011da999329)or [email Justin.](mailto:justin@votejustinstory.com?subject=I%20want%20to%20get%20involved!&body=)

| | | This [Disability Pride Month](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136379695/637252184/482427939?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzUvMS84MDk5NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ODAyMTYwMi0wNjhkLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ECsJbOf9mHGLah4FHeGUTzoP5B-ujaa4-lAZMy0h9Zw=&emci=82ffdcfb-5c8c-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=58021602-068d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=560478), we recognize and celebrate the leadership, advocacy, and contributions of people with disabilities in California and across the country. In 1990, disability rights activists organized the [Capitol Crawl](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136379696/637252185/-2087198248?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzUvMS84MDk5NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ODAyMTYwMi0wNjhkLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ECsJbOf9mHGLah4FHeGUTzoP5B-ujaa4-lAZMy0h9Zw=&emci=82ffdcfb-5c8c-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=58021602-068d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=560478) to demand passage of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Their organizing efforts helped shine a light on the barriers disabled Americans were facing and built support for one of the most important civil rights laws in our nation’s history. This month, we celebrated 36 years of the [Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136379697/637252186/-165807577?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzUvMS84MDk5NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ODAyMTYwMi0wNjhkLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ECsJbOf9mHGLah4FHeGUTzoP5B-ujaa4-lAZMy0h9Zw=&emci=82ffdcfb-5c8c-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=58021602-068d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=560478), the landmark legislation that prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in all areas of public life, removing barriers to employment, transportation, public services and other critical areas. The ADA expanded access, opportunity, and inclusion for millions of Americans with disabilities – and its legacy reminds us that meaningful progress is built over time, and that the fight for disability rights continues today. We invite you to [check out this important conversation](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136379698/637252187/1356075402?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzUvMS84MDk5NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ODAyMTYwMi0wNjhkLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ECsJbOf9mHGLah4FHeGUTzoP5B-ujaa4-lAZMy0h9Zw=&emci=82ffdcfb-5c8c-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=58021602-068d-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=560478) about disability rights and activism with CADEM Executive Director Melanie V. clean_body: | | | | | | | This , we recognize and celebrate the leadership, advocacy, and contributions of people with disabilities in California and across the country. In 1990, disability rights activists organized the to demand passage of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Their organizing efforts helped shine a light on the barriers disabled Americans were facing and built support for one of the most important civil rights laws in our nation’s history. This month, we celebrated 36 years of the , the landmark legislation that prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in all areas of public life, removing barriers to employment, transportation, public services and other critical areas. The ADA expanded access, opportunity, and inclusion for millions of Americans with disabilities – and its legacy reminds us that meaningful progress is built over time, and that the fight for disability rights continues today. We invite you to about disability rights and activism with CADEM Executive Director Melanie V. Peter,

You may have heard me quote one of my mentors, the late Senator Paul Wellstone, who said “Politics is about the improvement of people’s lives.”

**I truly believe that.** That’s why, throughout my career, I’ve focused on getting results.

In the U.S. Senate, I was ranked number one for bipartisan bills and number three out of one hundred for getting bills passed into law -- from transportation projects across the state, to help for our farmers and rural areas, to lower prescription drug costs for our seniors.

**Now, I’m running for governor of Minnesota to stand up for what’s right and fix what’s wrong.**

I couldn’t be prouder of Minnesota. We have been the center of America's heartbreak, but we've also been the center of America's hope and courage. Through it all, the people of our state continue to show up with compassion and resolve.

I am running for governor for every Minnesotan who wants to buy their first home, for every parent who wants a better world for their kids and for everyone who wants more affordable healthcare. I'm running for every student, farmer, dreamer and builder.

These times call for leaders who can stand up and not be rubber stamps of this administration, but who are also willing to find common ground and fix things in our state. I’ve never shied away from taking on the powerful, and I will do my job without fear or favor.

name: Roy Cooper
subject: This is easier said than done
body:
This race is too consequential to sit out. The stakes are too high.
[](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260731-1.4v_gSs&refcode=em-20260731-1&t=1&akid=1686%2E1086043%2Ebm03xm)
Peter, deciding to run for this U.S. Senate seat wasn’t easy.
I had planned on serving North Carolina from here at home. That’s why I was so humbled when North Carolinians twice elected me to be their Governor.
**But this Senate race is too consequential to sit out. The stakes are simply too high.**
I entered this race to fight for people like you, who’ve put your trust in me -- and I have full faith that together, we can win. But tonight, we’re facing the biggest test yet of our grassroots movement’s strength: **[With time running out to reach our ambitious $1.5 million goal, I’m personally asking you to help out by pitching in a $5 donation split between our campaign and Wes Moore, right now.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260731-1.4v_gSs&refcode=em-20260731-1&t=2&akid=1686%2E1086043%2Ebm03xm)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260731-1.4v_gSs&amount=5&refcode=em-20260731-1&t=3&akid=1686%2E1086043%2Ebm03xm)**
I’m running because our nation cannot afford two more years of unchecked Republican power in Washington. The attacks on health care, on democratic values and even on Americans -- **they have to stop.**
Our leaders should be focusing on strengthening our communities by investing in public schools, securing health care access and prioritizing hardworking folks over the wealthiest few. That’s what I strove to do in North Carolina – and by the end of my time in office, we added thousands of jobs by expanding the clean energy economy, gave public school teachers statewide a much-needed raise, expanded Medicaid and more.
**This is the work I’m ready to continue as the next Senator from North Carolina. But that means we have to flip this seat from red to blue for the first time in a generation and take back the Senate for the people who elect us, which is easier said than done.**
I’ve never lost a race, but this one will be the most competitive of my career. It’s the best pick-up opportunity for Democrats this cycle, and our ability to flip the Senate hinges on us succeeding.
**A recent poll shows our lead narrowing to just four points -- and as GOP dark money floods our race, we can expect that margin to grow even tighter.**
That’s why far-right groups are already spending nearly $100 million so far to attack me -- and experts expect this to be the most expensive Senate race ever, so they will spare no expense to help President Trump’s hand-picked candidate buy his way to victory.
So if they see us missing goals like the one we set for tonight, they _will_ use this as an opportunity to strike. They _will_ flood the airwaves with millions more in attack ads to smear me, knowing that their investments are working as intended, because we _will not_ have enough funds to fight back.
**[Chipping in $5, $25 or whatever amount is right for you, split between our campaign and Wes Moore before the end of the day won’t just help us close the gap in time; it’ll prove to everyone that momentum is on our side. So if you’re with us, Peter, please make it clear by making a donation right away.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260731-1.4v_gSs&refcode=em-20260731-1&t=4&akid=1686%2E1086043%2Ebm03xm)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260731-1.4v_gSs&amount=5&refcode=em-20260731-1&t=23&akid=1686%2E1086043%2Ebm03xm)**
If you made it this far, thank you so much for reading -- and for all you do to help me flip this battleground seat blue.
Roy Cooper

name: With Honor Action
subject: 70% of Americans Report High Confidence in Military Veterans 📊
body:
Plus, Rye Barcott on "I Serve", and the House passage on the FY27 NDAA

| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/8SizkEPykVP?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720)
| | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/Fr6b0MbbT5c?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720)
| | Hi Peter,
According to a new poll released this week by [**With Honor and Gallup**](https://us.list-manage.com/o_PML119w7U?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720) , 7 in 10 U.S. adults say they have a great deal or quite a lot of confidence in military veterans, with 77% saying they would trust a person with military experience a great deal or a fair amount to perform well as an elected official.
This trust in leaders with military experience extends across party groups, with majorities of Democrats (70%), Independents (73%), and Republicans (91%) expressing this view.
The findings come as With Honor Action reports that[ 752 veterans across the political spectrum](https://us.list-manage.com/uqfnr1YmzDt?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720) have run or are running for Congress in the 2026 cycle—a 47% increase from 2024 and the highest number the organization has tracked since it began monitoring veteran candidates in 2018.
Read more from [Military.com](https://us.list-manage.com/BcI8cC4lQqC?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720)’s Deputy Editor Nick Mordowanec [here](https://us.list-manage.com/ucXuTcPtGWA?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720).
---
|
---
| |

# **Rye Barcott on** _**I Serve:**_**Iraq, With Honor, and the meaning of courage**
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/14rd5rFHRdc?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720)
| | With Honor Co-Founder and CEO Rye Barcott’s episode of _I Serve_ was released on Tuesday, completing the first season of a new eight-episode podcast from Foreign Policy and With Honor.
Rye traces his path to service back to his father, a Marine officer and Vietnam veteran. The episode follows Rye through tours in Bosnia, the Horn of Africa, and Fallujah, and into why he co-founded With Honor: to help elect veterans who put the common good above party lines.
The series also features With Honor Advisory Board members General Nadja West: "The Surgeon General," Elliot Ackerman: "The Special Operator," and General H.R. McMaster: "The Historian,” as well as British MP Alistair Carns: “The Minister,” recounting his remarkable 24 years as a Royal Marine—including covertly boarding suspected sanctions-busting vessels in the Persian Gulf and nearly being pulled into a ship’s propeller.
---
| [Listen Now](https://us.list-manage.com/et0CmEUYJHp?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720)
---
|
---
| |

# **With Honor Action Joins Letter on Including the MOLD Act in the FY27 NDAA**
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/nfGqmg9MEXW?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720)
| | On Wednesday, With Honor Action, along with partner organizations, sent a letter to the House and Senate Armed Services Committees urging the inclusion of the Military Occupancy Living Defense (MOLD) Act, [**H.R. 7188**](https://us.list-manage.com/Uqd67ZzcfDB?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720)**/**[**S. 3654**](https://us.list-manage.com/hvWKYDd103h?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720) , in the final version of the Fiscal Year 2027 NDAA.
Led by Founding For Country Caucus Co-Chair Rep. Jimmy Panetta alongside Sen. Richard Blumenthal and With Honor Action allies Sens. Joni Ernst and Tim Sheehy, the MOLD Act would implement new, comprehensive standards for privately-contracted military housing across the Department of Defense (DoD).
Read the letter [here](https://us.list-manage.com/8NMnSCGeAsb?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720).
---
| [Tell Congress to Pass the MOLD Act](https://us.list-manage.com/xATxJGxvKtO?e=33f53a5b1a&c2id=cb2f151404272f38c482059c4a3ef720)

My team tells me we still need to raise around $2,000 before midnight to hit our monthly goal. And with my primary only 11 days away, this is not a goal we can afford to miss. They are willing to spend whatever it takes and say whatever they need to say to mislead voters and drown out the truth. But you know me, I am not going to let them scare me into silence. **I am going to keep taking on corporate greed, fighting back every time the Trump administration abuses its power, and working to lower costs for families who are doing everything right and still getting squeezed.** _And if I am going to keep showing up for these fights, I need you standing with me._ **I do not have billionaires waiting in the wings to cut a million-dollar check without thinking twice. Before I won my first election, not a lot of people looked at me and thought: _That’s a future Congresswoman._
I was raised by a single mom who spent 20 years serving her country in the Army. She didn’t just teach me the value of hard work or responsibility — she lived it, every single day.
I carried with me the lessons my mom taught me when I worked multiple jobs to get through school. I carried them into my work in economic and community development on Native American reservations. And I carried them with me when I launched a campaign to unseat a four-term incumbent in Congress.

Peter, it’s nice to meet you.
I’m Sam Skardon, and I’m so deeply honored that Jermaine has asked me to join him on the ticket as our nominee for Lieutenant Governor.
In just a minute, I’m going to ask you to make a donation to our campaign. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jermaine-july26?refcode=073126_1] But first, I want to tell you about the four years that shaped everything I believe about public service.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jermaine-july26?refcode=073126_1 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jermaine-july26?refcode=073126_1]
I was blessed to serve on the staff of Congressman John Lewis. More times than I can count, I had the honor of hearing him tell his life story, and every so often, I had the privilege of telling it too. Mr. Lewis and his colleagues truly built a New America through their sweat and blood.
From the sit-ins, to the Freedom Rides, to the march across the Edmund Pettus Bridge, let me tell you - his story has become a lifelong source of inspiration. It’s why my twin sons are named Lewis, after the Congressman, and Lawson, after Reverend Jim Lawson who taught Congressman Lewis and a generation of young organizers the discipline of non-violent resistance. I think about both of those men every day as I'm raising my boys in Charleston.
Now I'm running for Lieutenant Governor because Jermaine’s vision for a New South Carolina is one I’m willing to fight for too. Will you stand with us in this fight by chipping in any amount you can ahead of tonight’s end of month fundraising deadline? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jermaine-july26?refcode=073126_1]

The lesson I carried back home to South Carolina was to fight for the people who’ve been told to sit down and wait their turn. I’ve spent the past seven years in the city where I was raised, building and growing community loan funds to invest capital in small local businesses, clean energy projects, and affordable housing. And, of course, to make as much Good Trouble as possible.
Our opponent, Alan Wilson, and his family have spent 58 years in elected office, and they’ve done nothing but tell people to sit down and wait longer. He’s brought lawsuits to end patient protections from insurance companies, overturn elections, and interfered with corruption investigations. Jermaine and I are fighting for a New South Carolina that works for everyone - not just the sons of Congressmen.
Peter, we can get it done - but only if people like you stand beside us every step of the way. If you’re able, please make a donation today to help us build a winning campaign. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jermaine-july26?refcode=073126_1]
Thanks so much, Peter. Let’s make some Good Trouble.
Talk soon,
Sam

In the Navy's Nuclear Power Program, evidence is everything. You don't guess. You test, you observe, you measure, and you act on what the data tells you. So let me tell you what July's data shows. __**The Hypothesis:**_
A grassroots campaign in VA-02 with the right resources, the right message, and the right candidate can flip this seat blue and, with it, the House of Representatives._ __**The Evidence:**__
* Cook Political Report rates VA-02 a dead-even Toss-Up.
* The most recent polls have me tied 47-47 with Trump-endorsed Jen Kiggans.
* Grassroots donors raised more than $50k in support of my campaign this month.
* TV ad launched across Coastal Virginia, reaching persuadable voters before Republican attacks begin.
* Thousands of doors knocked, calls made, voters contacted across the district.

Hypothesis confirmed. _This campaign has what it takes._ In science, you control the variables. Folks, it’s James Carville.
I’ve spent nearly half a century helping Democrats win elections, and I’m gonna tell you something plainly:
For too long, we have waited until the house was already on fire before deciding to buy a hose.
We wait until a race becomes a crisis.
We wait until a great candidate is getting buried in attack ads.
We wait until Republicans have already built the infrastructure, raised the money, and defined the battlefield.
Then everybody starts running around asking what happened.
Well, Raja Krishnamoorthi has gone and done something about it.
He founded Equal Opportunity Now [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email] to find and support bold leaders and important causes before it’s too late — leaders who will stand up to Donald Trump and the MAGA movement, fight for working families, and actually deliver results.
And all I can say is:
FINALLY.
Finally, an organization that understands we cannot defeat MAGA with timid candidates, stale talking points, and a last-minute panic.
But Raja cannot build this by himself.
Will you contribute $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help Equal Opportunity Now find, fund, and support the leaders Democrats need to start winning again? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
SUPPORT EQUAL OPPORTUNITY NOW! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Now, I know Raja.
He is smart. He is tough. And he knows firsthand what opportunity can mean.
His family came to this country with very little. They relied on public housing and food stamps. He worked his way from Peoria all the way to Congress.
And instead of pulling the ladder up behind him, Raja has spent his career fighting to make sure the next family gets the same shot.
That means standing up for workers.
Holding powerful corporations and corrupt politicians accountable.
Defending immigrants, voting rights, and every American targeted by Trump’s politics of division.
And now he is putting that experience toward building the next generation of Democratic leadership.
Here’s the truth: The leaders we need are already out there.
They are running for city council, state legislature, Congress, and offices most national donors are not paying attention to yet.
They have the courage.
They have the ideas.
What they do not always have is the money, infrastructure, and early support necessary to compete.
That is where Equal Opportunity Now comes in.
Please chip in $25, $50, or whatever you can today to help Raja build the organization Democrats should have built years ago. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
HELP DEMOCRATS WIN: DONATE TODAY! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
We’ve got a good battle plan, now, let’s help Raja build this damn thing.
-- James Carville

I grew up in a working-class family in Allagash.
We didn’t always have heat or running water. Sometimes, we relied on food assistance to make ends meet.
My dad was a logger out in the woods, and one day he and his fellow loggers had to stand up to a wealthy landowner who was threatening their wages. They weren’t even asking for more money, they just wanted to be paid fairly.
“Take the pay cut or go home,” they were told.
I’ll never forget that day. I was only 11 years old, and watched my dad fight for something bigger than all of us — a basic fairness every worker should be entitled to, the ability to make ends meet, the ability to put food on the table for their family.
I know what it’s like to worry about paying the bills on time. I know what it’s like to fight, not just for your own future, but for the future of everyone around you, too.
And it’s that fight I’ll bring to the United States Senate. For too long, our voices have been ignored and crushed by powerful corporations and special interests who make backroom deals with greedy politicians.
Now’s our chance to change that. NAME, we have less than 100 days to build a campaign big enough to defeat Susan Collins. But with your help today, I know we can do it. I promise you I’ll spend every day in the Senate fighting for you and your families.
So that’s why I have to ask: Can you chip in a donation of any amount split between my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to defeat Collins and take back our Democratic majority? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson]
DONATE TO DEFEAT SUSAN COLLINS AND FLIP THE SENATE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-jackson]
I appreciate your support always,
Troy

class champions who know the struggles their communities face firsthand,

Dear Friends,Please help before the July 31st deadline. I’m $4865 from reaching my July fundraising goal!This campaign is built on one simple principle: local government should provide **opportunity for all.** Today, families across our city are feeling the squeeze of rising housing, healthcare, and grocery costs. Young families wonder if they can afford to stay, and seniors worry about being priced out. Working people deserve a City Hall focused on making life more affordable while protecting the unique quality of life that makes Daly City so special.As a lifelong resident and the proud son of working-class Filipino immigrants, these challenges are personal. My family has called Daly City home since 1977, when my parents bought our home at the Top of the Hill. I attended our local schools and learned the values of hard work, service, and looking out for your neighbors.My career has been dedicated to serving this community. For the past ten years, I’ve served as Chief of Staff to San Mateo County Supervisor David J. Canepa. As Vice Chair of Daly City's Personnel Board, I’ve also gained firsthand experience in making local government more responsive and accountable. I know how to navigate government, build partnerships, and bring resources home because I’ve spent my career doing exactly that.If elected, I will focus on delivering real results that provides opportunity for all:
* [**Affordability:** Improving housing affordability, expanding healthcare access, and helping families keep up with the cost of living.](https://us.list-manage.com/pi3S211k5iZ?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)
* [**Public Safety & Infrastructure:** Investing in first responders, fixing flooding challenges, repairing potholes, and strengthening transit options.](https://us.list-manage.com/UFh8zK97I3D?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)
* [**Family Support:** Advocating for a childcare center at Daly City Hall to support working parents and make city services more accessible.](https://us.list-manage.com/AnSPgPN2Yhi?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)
* [**Senior Care:** Protecting and expanding programs that help seniors age safely and independently in their homes.](https://us.list-manage.com/17Ks_UufdaR?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)

**I’m ready to step into a leadership role myself in every way but I can’t do it without you. As I know from helping to run Supervisor Canepa’s campaigns and you probably do too, campaigns are not cheap.**[**Can you be one of my founding donors?**](https://us.list-manage.com/sttB3EZXuow?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)**Nothing is more important to a campaign than early money, as it helps us get off to a fast start and build a winning campaign from the get-go.**
[**Could you donate today in any amount up to $5,900? $1,000, $500, $100 or even $25 will make a huge difference to my campaign at this early stage.**](https://us.list-manage.com/19ppc_yonHL?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)
Our city has always been defined by hardworking families, diverse neighborhoods, and neighbors who care about one another. Together, we can build a Daly City that is more affordable, safer, better prepared for the future, and continues to be a place where families of every generation can thrive – a Daly City that truly provides opportunity for all.I would be honored to earn your support, your ideas, and your vote.In friendship,
Tony BayudanCandidate for Daly City Council**P.S. Anything you can donate today at**[**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/tony-bayudan-1**](https://us.list-manage.com/1A7aXkNaPgx?e=a77f0ac4a9&c2id=f2f0b537fa844d5b5a30cd2c82e303f0)**will be so valuable – even if it’s just $5!**

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

On August 7th, 2025, President Trump signed **Executive Order #14330** — _"Democratizing Access to Alternative Assets for 401(k) Investors."_

At the time, most retirees brushed it off. "Just another order. We'll see if anything happens."

Well, something happened.

On **March 30th, 2026** , the Department of Labor quietly filed a proposed rule operationalizing that order. (Release ebsa20260330, if you want to look it up.)

And in the same window, Congressman Troy Downing introduced the **Retirement Investment Choice Act** — a bill designed to establish Trump's executive order directly into federal law.

Put simply: **physical gold inside 401(k) plans is no longer a "maybe someday."** It's moving through the regulatory pipeline right now.

Here's why this matters for your retirement:

Once **$9 trillion of 401(k) assets** become eligible to allocate to physical gold, even a small percentage shift could create a tsunami-sized wave of demand the gold market has never seen.

With gold already trading **near $4,500 per ounce** , J.P. Morgan is projecting it to average over **$5,000 by the end of 2026**. Bank of America has called for **$6,000 per ounce**. And Goldman Sachs even sees nearly **$5,000 by December**.

These aren't fringe forecasts. These are the same banks managing the retirement money in question.

But here's the part most Americans miss:

**You don't have to wait for the rulemaking to finish.** There's already an **IRS-approved process** that lets you move a portion of your existing 401(k), IRA, or TSP into physical gold — _tax-deferred and penalty-free when done correctly_.

The smart movers are positioning right now, before the rule formalizes and the demand wave hits.

He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. But you deserve to hear the truth
| I debated sending you these 3 quick updates, but you deserve to hear the truth:
FIRST: We promised to protect and expand our pro-Trump Majority to save President Trump from impeachment. We worked so hard to win the House and the Senate and send President Trump back to the White House just to give up on him now.
THEN: Last month was a fundraising disaster. We fell short of our end-of-month goal just as a Democrat Super PAC dropped $272 MILLION in attack ads across the country to target 35 Conservatives in vital swing seats. We're stretched too thin to defend each one, and Democrats only need to flip a couple to destroy our Pro-Trump Majority.
NOW: We're pacing $500,000 behind our End-of-Month Goal, so we can't fall short on our promise to deliver President Trump a Conservative House Majority this year. But if every Patriot reading this gave just $5 right now, we'll be in striking distance of our goal and able to rush immediate resources to all 35 races.

NOW: We're pacing $500,000 behind our End-of-Month Goal, so we can't fall short on our promise to deliver President Trump a Conservative House Majority this year. But if every Patriot reading this gave just $5 right now, we'll be in striking distance of our goal and able to rush immediate resources to all 35 races. Donald Trump has been sued
more than 750 times since he took office.

750 times.

And in more than 450 of those cases, judges have let Trump's policies stay
in effect — while the lawsuits are still being fought.^1

For years, Trump and his allies have stacked the courts — from district
benches all the way to the Supreme Court — with loyalist judges who'd
rubber-stamp whatever he wanted, whenever he wanted it.

And look at just some of the chaos it’s allowed to ensue:

* Trump attempted to end birthright citizenship
* He froze federal funding to entire states
* He tried to fire a sitting Federal Reserve governor over accusations
she was never even charged with
* He fired the watchdogs whose job is to hold him accountable
* He punished a law firm for refusing to do free legal work for his
agenda
* He's using a wartime law from the 1700s to deport people without due
process.

This is the system Trump built: push unconstitutional, self-serving
policies. Get sued. Fall back on the cronies he installed on the bench to
keep it running long enough to do the damage. Cash in while the courts
slow-walk justice.

Demand Justice PAC exists to fight exactly this — to expose judicial
corruption and Trump’s court takeover scheme, and demand accountability
from the courts Trump has his grip on.

| | It's wildfire season in Oregon and places across the country, and I'm doing all I can to make sure that our communities have the resources they need. Right now, I'm pushing this administration to increase the amount of money dedicated to firefighting efforts so that we can avoid "fire borrowing," a practice that can pull money from other important programs to help pay for firefighting costs. That's just the start. Last week, I introduced three bills to get ahead of this crisis before it starts:
* Making it easier to use prescribed fire, one of our best tools for reducing the fuel that turns a spark into a firestorm

* Fixing biomass and Renewable Fuel Standard policy so we're clearing dangerous fuel loads instead of leaving them to burn

* Taking on the home insurance mess that's leaving Oregon families in fire-prone areas unable to afford coverage, or unable to get it at all

And on the Interior Appropriations Subcommittee, I've used my seat at the table to fight for real funding increases for wildfire prevention and response, not just bigger checks after the disaster, but real investment before it. This is the type of fierce advocacy I've always believed in and championed. [**Please help me continue doing that work. | | Welcome back to Fact Friday. **Today I want to answer a question I hear often: What's the difference between immigration law, executive action, and border enforcement?** If you've recently turned on the news or listened to a political debate, you've probably heard these terms used as if they mean the same thing. _But they don't._ They represent three distinct parts of our government, each with a different role and level of authority. Living in a border community like ours, we see the impact of these decisions every single day. Knowing who actually holds the power to make these choices makes it a lot easier to cut through the noise. Here's how it breaks down:
1. **Immigration Law (Written by Congress)**

Only Congress has the power to write or permanently change federal immigration law. That includes determining who can legally immigrate, how visas and green cards work, who qualifies for asylum, and how someone becomes a U.S. citizen. When people talk about "fixing our broken immigration system," lasting reform requires Congress to act. A president or federal agencies cannot pass a law.
2. **Executive Action (Directed by the President)**

While the President can't rewrite the law, they do decide how federal agencies implement and prioritize existing laws. Through executive orders and other policy directives, the White House can adjust enforcement priorities, shift agency resources, or change how existing laws are administered. These actions can have a significant impact. But because they aren't written into law, a future president can often reverse them.
3. **Border Enforcement (Carried out by Agencies)**

Border enforcement is the day-to-day work of carrying out the laws Congress passes under the enforcement priorities set by the administration. Federal agencies like U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) handle the ground-level work: inspecting trade and travel, processing migrants, and enforcing existing statutes. They carry out their work within the authorities and funding Congress provides them. **For communities like El Paso, these distinctions shape our daily lives and explain why lasting immigration reform cannot happen through executive action alone.** For decades, leaders across the political spectrum have acknowledged that our immigration system is incredibly outdated. Until Congress passes comprehensive immigration reform that reflects both our security needs and our values, presidents will continue to use temporary executive fixes to manage a system that desperately needs a permanent solution. **As your representative, my focus is on the one part of this equation that creates lasting change: writing and passing legislation.** That's why I've worked with both Democrats and Republicans on common-sense, comprehensive solutions and created the bipartisan Dignity Act — legislation that modernizes border security, protects Dreamers, and creates legal pathways to make our immigration system more orderly, secure, and functional for communities like El Paso. While the Dignity Act has not yet become law, it reflects the kind of bipartisan legislative solution that only Congress can enact, and I'm proud to have authored it. If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. Staying informed is power. Let's use it, El Paso. clean_body: | | | | Welcome back to Fact Friday. Today I want to answer a question I hear often: What's the difference between immigration law, executive action, and border enforcement? If you've recently turned on the news or listened to a political debate, you've probably heard these terms used as if they mean the same thing. But they don't. They represent three distinct parts of our government, each with a different role and level of authority. Living in a border community like ours, we see the impact of these decisions every single day. Knowing who actually holds the power to make these choices makes it a lot easier to cut through the noise. Here's how it breaks down: 1. Immigration Law (Written by Congress) Only Congress has the power to write or permanently change federal immigration law. That includes determining who can legally immigrate, how visas and green cards work, who qualifies for asylum, and how someone becomes a U.S. citizen. When people talk about "fixing our broken immigration system," lasting reform requires Congress to act. A president or federal agencies cannot pass a law. 2. Executive Action (Directed by the President) While the President can't rewrite the law, they do decide how federal agencies implement and prioritize existing laws. Through executive orders and other policy directives, the White House can adjust enforcement priorities, shift agency resources, or change how existing laws are administered. These actions can have a significant impact. But because they aren't written into law, a future president can often reverse them. 3. Border Enforcement (Carried out by Agencies) Border enforcement is the day-to-day work of carrying out the laws Congress passes under the enforcement priorities set by the administration. Federal agencies like U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) handle the ground-level work: inspecting trade and travel, processing migrants, and enforcing existing statutes. They carry out their work within the authorities and funding Congress provides them. For communities like El Paso, these distinctions shape our daily lives and explain why lasting immigration reform cannot happen through executive action alone. For decades, leaders across the political spectrum have acknowledged that our immigration system is incredibly outdated. Until Congress passes comprehensive immigration reform that reflects both our security needs and our values, presidents will continue to use temporary executive fixes to manage a system that desperately needs a permanent solution. As your representative, my focus is on the one part of this equation that creates lasting change: writing and passing legislation. That's why I've worked with both Democrats and Republicans on common-sense, comprehensive solutions and created the bipartisan Dignity Act — legislation that modernizes border security, protects Dreamers, and creates legal pathways to make our immigration system more orderly, secure, and functional for communities like El Paso. While the Dignity Act has not yet become law, it reflects the kind of bipartisan legislative solution that only Congress can enact, and I'm proud to have authored it. If you want to keep getting clear, fact-based breakdowns of the issues affecting our community, make sure you stay connected and share this with someone who should be paying attention, too. Staying informed is power. Let's use it, El Paso. **[Convention of States has a Colorado bill ready for 2027. It still has no sponsor.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Convention of States Action (COSA) says more than 62,000 Coloradans have signed its petitions calling for a constitutional convention to impose fiscal restraints on the federal government, limit its power, and set term limits for Congress.
The organization has a draft bill ready for the 2027 legislative session. Its representatives have met with senior policy staff in the Governor’s Office.
According to Michael Forbis, a 20-year Army veteran and Colorado Springs resident who volunteers on COSA Colorado’s Legislative Liaison Team, House Republican staff distributed an earlier version of the proposal to the caucus’s 22 members.
What it does not have is a single Colorado legislator willing to sponsor it.

**[History, when convenient: Colorado media’s selective celebration of representation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY C. J. GARBO, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_A historic all-Hispanic gubernatorial ticket barely registers in Colorado coverage — raising pointed questions about whose "firsts" the press chooses to celebrate._
* **A historic ticket, mostly ignored:** Unaffiliated candidates Greg Lopez and Taralyn Romero qualified for Colorado's November gubernatorial ballot with nearly 12,000 signatures, forming what appears to be the state's first all-Hispanic gubernatorial ticket — yet outlets like The Colorado Sun led with Lopez alone, largely erasing Romero and the ticket's historic significance.
* **A double standard in coverage of "firsts":** C.J. Garbo contrasts this muted treatment with the extensive, repeated coverage given to Jared Polis's historic election as the nation's first openly gay governor and Yadira Caraveo's milestone as Colorado's first Latina in Congress — both Democrats.
* **A majority of voters left uncovered as a movement:** With unaffiliated voters now making up over 50 percent of Colorado's active electorate — more than Democrats and Republicans combined — Garbo argues the press continues treating independent candidates as mere "spoilers" rather than covering the two-party system's declining grip as its own major story.

____________________________________
I grew up the only boy with four sisters.
Four. Sisters. Lol and I absolutely loved it!
I grew up in a house full of women. Four sisters and a mother. A bathroom that was never mine. That wasn't stressful, it wasn't weird, it was normal. I learned early that women's lives, their values, their beliefs, their essence wasn't a burden because they were different than mine. They're mine to protect because they mattered to me.
That doesn't leave you as you get older. It shapes you. Watching then and still watching now, how they moved through the world. Watching what they still have to put up with that I never did. Watching what it costs to be a woman in America every single day. You absorb all of that, even when you don't realize it's happening.
Now I'm a dad. I have a daughter named Daphne. And everything I watched growing up, everything I came to understand about what women navigate just to get through their day, it all lands differently when you're looking at your daughter and thinking about the world she's going to inherit.
Wednesday this week, I went to the press conference in support of the Epstein survivors. Not because someone asked me to show up. Not for a photo. Because you don't grow up in a house full of women, you don't raise a daughter, and then look away when survivors are standing up and asking to be seen, to be heard, for JUSTICE!!! You just go. Because that's what you do when you truly want to be an ally and be supportive. You just show up!
Being there with them, supporting those women and man, Sky Roberts who is advocating for his late sister Virginia Roberts Giuffre, listening to them tell the truth about what was done to them and the powerful men who got away with it for so long, that meant something to me. As a dad. As a brother. As a son. As a man who was raised to understand that "If you are neutral in situations of injustice, you have chosen the side of the oppressor." That great quote is attributed to Bishop Desmond Tutu.
After I left, I got some dms and comments left for me. I'll let this one speak for itself.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3a4da57b-1c16-4376-b398-69ad0d1d6f1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Charming. Real charming.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..52nK9_SQxDiR-GyW44a0vxt7SjPfkqzOWAZ6suxjAuw?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=209288161)
Here's what I want to say directly to the men reading this, especially the ones who look like me: being an ally isn't a performance. It's not a checklist. It's not complicated. It's what you already know is right if you were raised right, or if you've done the work to get there. Sometimes it's just showing up. Literally walking into a room and saying, I see you, I believe you, I'm not going anywhere.
We have a lot of loud voices right now telling men that caring about women is weakness. Joe Rogan. Andrew Tate. Pete Hegseth. Some of them have built entire platforms out of making men feel like empathy is something to be embarrassed about and manliness is how much you can bench press. Like protecting the people you love is soft. Like calling out misogyny makes you less of a man.
I grew up with four sisters. I have a daughter named Daphne. My Mother who I love and cherish. And I promise you, there is nothing soft about any of it. Misogyny isn't abstract to me. It never was. I know what it looks like because I grew up watching the people I love deal with it. And I have never once looked at any of them and thought, caring about you is making me less of a man.
Those guys and their followers have it exactly backwards.
Show up. Listen. Support. That's it. That's the whole thing.
Happy Friday.
-Harry

Before tonight's end-of-month fundraising deadline, I'm asking you to make a donation to my Senate campaign in North Carolina. If that's all you need to hear, you can use this button to chip in:

By chipping in $5, you'll join the hundreds of thousands of people who have pitched in to claim a stake in our grassroots movement.
By chipping in $5, you'll be saying that you refuse to let the GOP buy this seat for President Trump's handpicked candidate - and that you're ready to fight back against the nearly $100 million in attack ad spending that Republicans have poured into this race so far.
By chipping in $5, you'll help us reach our $1.5 million end-of-month goal.

Thank you,
Roy Cooper

| | Hey Patriot,
---
Look – I’m not gonna sugarcoat this one.
**We _cannot_ run out of money** to fund and train ballot chasers at the worst possible time in this election cycle.
You’re one of Turning Point’s most dedicated supporters. When the rest of the list goes quiet, folks like you step up. That’s why I’m reaching out to you directly here.
Charlie Kirk built this movement from the ground up. He **_believed_** in the power of everyday patriots showing up, knocking on doors, and changing the direction of this country one conversation at a time.
We lost him, but we are **_still_** carrying his torch.
We need to train at least **[500 new ballot chasers next month](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12633130/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfanUtZW9tLWJjX2JyXzIwMjYwNzMx/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA3MzE/LbmNsb29NU2xaNg/qP3V0bV90ZXJtPTIzMzc2X3dyMSZhbW91bnQ9MTAw/gamz2ZQ/savd979c6dd)** and put them in key districts across the country.
If we hit that number, we have a real fighting chance at winning the midterms. We can keep “**democratic socialists** ” _AKA_ **_communists_** OUT of Congress.
But if we fail... we lose the majority. President Trump becomes a lame duck president. We get more of the same disastrous Biden-era policies. And for all practical purposes, the fight is over.
This is NOT theoretical. This is the crossroads.
We need patriots on the pavement right now. We need the funding to train them, equip them, and send them out before early voting begins.
**Help us keep Charlie’s mission alive.**
**[Every dollar makes a difference in training ballot chasers.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12633130/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfanUtZW9tLWJjX2JyXzIwMjYwNzMx/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA3MzE/LbmNsb29NU2xaNg/qP3V0bV90ZXJtPTIzMzc2X3dyMSZhbW91bnQ9MTAw/gamz2ZQ/savd979c6dd)**

[KEEP THE TORCH BURNING](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12633130/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfanUtZW9tLWJjX2JyXzIwMjYwNzMx/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA3MzE/LbmNsb29NU2xaNg/qP3V0bV90ZXJtPTIzMzc2X3dyMSZhbW91bnQ9MTAw/gamz2ZQ/savd979c6dd)

We are running out of time to get the resources we urgently need to scale this operation. The only thing standing between us and a radical socialist takeover is the ground game Charlie so deeply believed in – **[and the patriots willing to fund it.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e12633130/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuYW5lZG90LmNvbS90cHBhYy90cHBhY19kb25fc2Jfc2ZfanUtZW9tLWJjX2JyXzIwMjYwNzMx/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjA3MzE/LbmNsb29NU2xaNg/qP3V0bV90ZXJtPTIzMzc2X3dyMSZhbW91bnQ9MTAw/gamz2ZQ/savd979c6dd)**
Please please please don’t sit this one out.
For Charlie. For Our Country. For the America we still believe in.

Tyler Bowyer
Executive Director, Turning Point PAC

As permitted by law, TPPAC, Inc. maintains a non-contribution account for the purpose of influencing federal, state, and local elections. Federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the name, address, occupation, and employer of individuals whose contribution exceeds $200 in an election cycle. For contributions from federal committees, corporations, and labor unions - regardless of contribution amount - federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the committee’s name and address. Contributions to this account may be used to influence federal elections by making independent expenditures in support of or in opposition to federal candidates. Individuals, federal committees, corporations, and labor unions may contribute to TPPAC, Inc.’s non-contribution account without limit. Contributions by national banks, foreign nationals (without lawful permanent resident status), and other foreign entities (e.g., foreign corporations) are prohibited. Contributions to TPPAC, Inc.’s non-contribution account are not tax-deductible for federal income tax purposes.
