subject: I hate sending this email — but here’s the reality, Peter
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Heartland Patriots (LucasKunce
body:
My team and I are sitting down right now to make tough calls about this campaign that could decide whether we win or lose.
[](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/106509?refcode=em20260731-10741&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10741%2E614464%2EkJS88y)
Hi, it’s Dan Osborn, the Independent candidate running to defeat Republican Billionaire Pete Ricketts for U.S. Senate in Nebraska.
I’m going to level with you.
My team and I are sitting down right now to make tough calls about this campaign that could decide whether we win or lose.
→ How many people can we afford to put on the ground?
→ How many doors can we knock?
→ How loud can we make our message when we’re up against someone with unlimited money?
Because here’s what I’m up against: **_My opponent is a billionaire. I’m not._**
I don’t have a pile of cash to fall back on. I don’t have corporate PACs waiting in line to bail me out. What I’ve got is a campaign built the hard way — by regular people chipping in what they can.
**_And right now, we’ve got gaps to close. If we don’t start raising more money, we’ll have to make tough decisions about which outreach programs to keep and which to cut._**
**So I’m asking straight up:[Can you pitch in $10 or whatever you can right now to Heartland Patriots and my campaign so we can keep building this campaign?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/106509?refcode=em20260731-10741&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10741%2E614464%2EkJS88y)**
**[DONATE](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/106509?refcode=em20260731-10741&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=10741%2E614464%2EkJS88y)**
Every dollar we raise goes directly into reaching more people — more conversations, more momentum, more chances to prove that this race doesn’t belong to the highest bidder.
I won’t pretend this part is fun. Asking for money never is.
But I believe in what we’re building here. And I believe that if enough regular folks step up, we can beat someone who thinks this seat can be bought.
**So I’ll ask one more time:[Will you chip in today to me and Heartland Patriots to help us close the gap and keep this campaign moving?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/106509?refcode=em20260731-10741&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=10741%2E614464%2EkJS88y)**

This only works if we all show up.
— Dan Osborn

Hi friends — this is an end-of-month fundraising email. I wanted to tell you right off the bat so you can delete it if you’d prefer! I understand it may not be possible to give right now (or you may just be sick of being asked).
So no hard feelings if this is the last sentence you read before clicking that trash icon.
If you’ve stuck around, I’m impressed — and thankful, because this is so important to talk about:
Right now, the stakes of everything feel so high. I remember in 2016, working on Hillary Clinton’s campaign, some people said our fears about a Donald Trump presidency were unfounded. That we were “overreacting.”
A decade later, we watch videos of innocent children being detained, families being ripped apart, and Americans being murdered — over and over again — by masked ICE and Border Patrol agents in our communities.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]
We read story after story about women who are needlessly dying because of Trump’s abortion bans.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]
We see states trying to criminalize people seeking health care — even suggesting the *death penalty* should be used as punishment for having an abortion.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]
We walk by military troops deployed in our cities, patrolling our streets.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]
All of that barely scratches the surface of this administration’s corruption and cruelty — and we’re only a year in.
We all know that we have to keep taking action to defend our democracy, but it’s daunting.
So here’s my promise to you: I will do every single thing in my power to fight for you and your rights. I will use every legislative tool, partner with our allies in the judicial system and out in the community, and push hard to protect our values and our freedoms.
But I’ll also tell you this — we’ll be a lot more successful in that work if we can claw back the GOP trifecta in Washington, and in less than 100 days, we have our chance.
My team and I are mapping out our plans for the next three months: winning re-election in CA-51, supporting my House colleagues in tough races, and boosting strong Democratic challengers in key battleground districts.
Will you help? We’re trying to raise $2,300 more online before tonight to keep our plans on track — anything you can give towards that goal will make a difference.
Click here or on the buttons below to contribute before we close the books on our July fundraising. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]

Thank you so much. I know we can do this — and I’m deeply grateful for your partnership!
—Sara

| Tonight is our first end-of-month fundraising deadline since we won the primary, and it feels a little different.
We've proven what this movement can do when thousands of people show up together, and now we're working to carry that same energy into November.
But this month, we also learned that a third-party challenger is entering our race, so we need to make sure we're staying on our game and not assuming the work is finished.
What we raise right now will determine whether we can organize at full strength across Denver, turn out every voter we can, elect progressive candidates, and pass ballot initiatives that will help our communities up and down the ballot.
I want November to send a message far beyond our district: Working people are ready for a new generation of leadership, and we are bringing everyone with us.
[If you can, chip in $15, or whatever feels right, before midnight tonight.](https://cefuo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001E8iSwtvLJmrNVERrZZgMfR532JtQAcRv27nlLFo9XUfsDjbRdR49gGMf3vp0KmCdzywm_3_zbBnMPdRUHnEArdZqWwfNmym9JL_5sYtji3as0hSJ8stEVP3ZLtdlwSBM2wW3QTgZL-ajvIr0_qnCGohGwmdwhemTI1-Ii-rgdsR28HyyHH7UUfLTZkE7dZ09TxYPAYH4wCOt0cawat48jrjyQS6xIw20AfckOQlDw2Xv-NmBytRu4g==&c=08KMQhmaKfucdc_bHFeosDbKm99sSbPJdMklx3FowBBVqCsfjSVN0Q==&ch=1R5WU2TBr5MZ_PjWhKDH9VJvgLPUitTSTMMwAtiTsB74oWc0UFVLrQ==)

name: Dan Ahlers
subject: Peter, I have the change we need.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY DAN AHLERS FOR GOVERNOR
body:
|

| |

---
| | | [VOLUNTEER](https://us.list-manage.com/f98AAiMh5sa?e=cee7b49c04&c2id=3adc23449cf80dcda430cceaf3c4b05d)
---
| | | |
---
| |
---
Burke Stampede Rodeo

How could I miss the legendary Burke Stampede Rodeo? This event is a part of a long list of traditions that capture the impressive talent and grit that thrives in South Dakota.

The rodeo is a prime display of the grit and impressive talent that thrives in South Dakota. By celebrating these traditions that make us South Dakotan, we draw attention to what is important to us and what we should invest in. We lose too many South Dakotans to opportunities outside of the state.

Beyond the the roping, wrestling, and racing, I learned a lot from ranchers about managing livestock and the issues that they face in the industry. In these events and small communities, I see opportunity to build back rural South Dakota. Repeatedly, ranchers and farmers are heard, but not truly listened to. My policy and decision making will be informed by the ranchers I shake hands with. I will keep South Dakotans with me every step of the way.

As governor, I will continue my commitment to collaborating with communities like Burke to learn how I can help. I appreciate the organizers of the Burke Rodeo for putting together such a well run event that celebrates the traditions that make South Dakota special.

| | |
---
| |
---
Yankton Meet & Greet

In Yankton we had great conversations about the importance of investing in South Dakota and our public schools. While past governor’s have prioritized selling South Dakota to stakeholders outside of the state. The most important stakeholders have been left behind: the South Dakotans who already live here. The current governor invested South Dakotans money on an out of state company despite the talent that exists right here at home, such as a Wakonda farmer that could’ve built hemp farms all over South Dakota, but chose to do so in a nearby state instead. This business could’ve directly contributed to small rural communities and our largest cities. By investing right here in South Dakota, we bring resources to support schools, affordability, hospitals, and essential services that are disappearing across the state.

With my time as a substitute teacher, I understand the importance of education for building a brighter South Dakota. If we are to improve the condition of our schools, we need to start believing in them. Actions speak louder than words, and educators deserve a positive attitude that commits to state funding for our schools without hesitation, and nothing less.

| | | |
---
| |
---
Conversations at Lower Brule and Enemy Swim, SD

This week I had the opportunity to visit with community members in Lower Brule and Enemy Swim. I want to thank everyone who took the time to share their experiences, concerns, and hopes for the future. These conversations reinforced something I’ve said throughout this campaign: South Dakota is strongest when we work together. Building a better relationship with our tribal nations begins with honoring and respecting tribal sovereignty and treating tribes as true partners, not as an afterthought. Together, we can address the challenges that affect so many families, including access to healthcare, the shortage of medical professionals, affordable housing, safer roads, and stronger educational opportunities. I’ll work collaboratively with tribal leaders and local communities to build trust, find practical solutions, and ensure everyone in South Dakota has the opportunity to succeed.

On the Campaign Trail

| |
---
Here’s the latest from across the campaign trail—key updates, major milestones, and where we’re headed next.

| | | |
---
| |
---
The Importance of Conservation

Conservation isn’t a partisan issue, it’s a South Dakota issue. Access to clean water, healthy soil, and the outdoors that define our way of life matter to every one of us. Farmers depend on reliable water and productive land. Native communities have long been stewards of our natural resources and understand their importance for future generations. Sportsmen and women know that healthy habitats supports the hunting, fishing, and recreation that are part of our heritage. Republicans, Democrats, and Independents all have a stake in protecting South Dakota’s land and water for future generations.

We don’t have to choose between a strong agricultural economy and strong conservation--we can and must have both. By encouraging voluntary conservation practices like riparian buffer strips, cover crops, wetland restoration, rotational grazing, and improved nutrient management, we can reduce runoff, improve water quality, strengthen wildlife habitat, and keep our farms productive for generations to come. Good stewardship and good agriculture go hand in hand. As governor, I’ll work with farmers, ranchers, tribal nations, conservation organizations, sportsmen and women, and local communities to find practical, science-based solutions that protect our natural resoruces while respecting private property rights and supporting South Dakota’s economy.

| |
---
What’s Next

We will be in parades in Moody County, Aurora, and Arlington this week. I will also be at the Sioux Empire Fair for Ag Appreciation Day, the community center in Woonsocket, and a town hall in Union County. In the coming weeks, we will begin distributing Dan Ahlers for Governor signs. If you would like to request a sign, email [info@danahlers.com](mailto:info@danahlers.com), or fill out the volunteer form at [danahlers.com](https://us.list-manage.com/nZgb4pxNKHR?e=cee7b49c04&c2id=3adc23449cf80dcda430cceaf3c4b05d). November is quickly approaching, but with the momentum we are experiencing so far, we will hit the ground running.

Four more years of Republican rule will get South Dakota nowhere.

I have the change we need.

Colorado turns 150 tomorrow, and we're celebrating with one of the state's sweetest food legends on the _[Feel Good Table](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuwyAUANDT4C0W_t8YMjBUqtwpnSp1RAQ-Ni02EflJlNtX7RV6gTe8z5M7-Vzyvrz7jWxakuNU3U6PayFmao6J9pITLTff4kqt8qOu5CM5kDAdpD7g4KLP5enGLtpEBIQd2UEbpcDgoLrVejwrNBMYMpPxoOTxmPQ0jNHAlMaAXba_mtQ4gJRqgB4MRYQQMWAMqJQYJcXMtfVfNe-8UirPeqfWh7p1xa7Ml6vAFwGzgPlZb3zrzyRgdnD_SE2_beFb4MwCX2HUXbPx8sil5OukxSiXzefyJ_G_C-4WfgIAAP__HY5vgQ)_. [Tune in here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFuwyAUANDT4C0W_t8YMjBUqtwpnSp1RAQ-Ni02EflJlNtX7RV6gTe8z5M7-Vzyvrz7jWxakuNU3U6PayFmao6J9pITLTff4kqt8qOu5CM5kDAdpD7g4KLP5enGLtpEBIQd2UEbpcDgoLrVejwrNBMYMpPxoOTxmPQ0jNHAlMaAXba_mtQ4gJRqgB4MRYQQMWAMqJQYJcXMtfVfNe-8UirPeqfWh7p1xa7Ml6vAFwGzgPlZb3zrzyRgdnD_SE2_beFb4MwCX2HUXbPx8sil5OukxSiXzefyJ_G_C-4WfgIAAP__HY5vgQ)!

subject: MAGA “obsessed” with winning sleepy KS referendum Tuesday
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY DEFEND OUR COURTS, NOT AUTHORIZED BY ANY CANDIDATE
body:
Whenever judges rule against core MAGA objectives they attack the courts.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=00195tOm8tKJeJah1l3ZigpzF2pU8F4QhPiT_5Ki4qgBxRV9deSl1QOWQfHYMyCRt5Un-0K6BM4atXzUUSiV5htNxCeHMwvDcz_XuZHvt2jZrDNZG77IONXKmLxnF9cyaSqGQydg2jVU9y1qVvALOwTICI0hl_niQPixEM8qN5lh2Bn9nc5fjLZm5wr33OFGkS0yg4WCG0AmlJSZSTprE0hi8kJ892UgS6as_dRRYjiuLY=&c=yVinJVBwrj0NnhMyISsTXbvP9ycWPFFokY2KnKSwAa4EgpFD5JT34A==&ch=g9lptTI-23U-DPCD_xLOHDL4N98RbCO-ExV7REhlZtELvLIwMWCdmw==)
---
|
Peter,
The entire universe of MAGA usual suspects are laser-focused on a sleepy Kansas ballot referendum vote on Tuesday.
The ballot measure would change the way state supreme court justices are selected, moving from a merit-based nominating commission system to direct election at the discretion of the state's GOP majority.
Here's why MAGA is obsessed with winning this ballot measure on Tuesday:

1. Abortion is actually on the ballot. In 2022, Kansas voters shot down a GOP constitutional amendment to say there was no right to an abortion in the state. A state Supreme Court stacked with MAGA appointees could undo that right.
2. MAGA is losing in front of KS courts including the KS Supreme Court. The justices currently on the KS Supreme Court were selected through a merit-based nominating commission system.

If MAGA wins the referendum on Tuesday, they would be able to gain control over the KS Supreme Court and turn it into another arm of the Republican Party.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=00195tOm8tKJeJah1l3ZigpzF2pU8F4QhPiT_5Ki4qgBxRV9deSl1QOWQfHYMyCRt5Un-0K6BM4atXzUUSiV5htNxCeHMwvDcz_XuZHvt2jZrDNZG77IONXKmLxnF9cyaSqGQydg2jVU9y1qVvALOwTICI0hl_niQPixEM8qN5lh2Bn9nc5fjLZm5wr33OFGkS0yg4WCG0AmlJSZSTprE0hixT50PL_dvh4gvc1p_VGGdU=&c=yVinJVBwrj0NnhMyISsTXbvP9ycWPFFokY2KnKSwAa4EgpFD5JT34A==&ch=g9lptTI-23U-DPCD_xLOHDL4N98RbCO-ExV7REhlZtELvLIwMWCdmw==)
---
| Whenever judges rule against MAGA and thwart their ambitions for ultimate power, they attack the courts. That's what is happening now in Kansas, and in judicial races across the country this year.
When that happens, organizations like Defend Our Courts are there to stop them.
We not only fight to safeguard fair courts and impartial judges by protecting merit-based selection systems like the one in Kansas; we wade into the rat's nest of judicial elections and thoroughly research and vet each judicial candidate we support.
Defend Our Courts is also leading a cutting edge campaign to reform the US Supreme Court, our Unpack Our Courts agenda.
In order for Democrats in Congress to be able to take any action to fix the broken Supreme Court, we need to win a majority in the US Senate. Our team is preparing a critical last minute campaign to help elect Dems in key swing state Senate elections this midterm.

Trust me, I know all the constant emails and texts can weigh on you. It wears on me too. Some days I wonder if it's worth it. But then I remember why I'm here. Peter,
I wanted to reach out with a quick update before our deadline at midnight.
**With the Washington state primary election next Tuesday, this is an important moment for our campaign and our movement.**
And with so much at stake, every fundraising deadline gives us a chance to show the strength of this grassroots community and make sure Pramila has the resources she needs to keep fighting.
Right now, Pramila is standing up against an administration that is threatening our democracy, attacking our communities, and putting the interests of the powerful ahead of working people.

That’s why I’m reaching out today.
With the clock ticking, we’re asking this grassroots community to come together and help us finish strong.

Hey Peter,
On the campaign trail, I’m able to talk to a lot of folks, from a lot of different walks of life. It is eye-opening how many of their struggles and concerns about our government are shared, regardless of their background.
When people open up to me, at an event, out canvassing, or in line at the grocery store, they know that I’m listening to them, because when I get to Washington, I’m going to do everything I can to fix these issues for them. That means introducing and uplifting legislation that helps our communities back home, rather than voting with party leaders and corporate interests that want legislation that uplifts the ultra-wealthy and harms our neighbors.
Our Congress has taken advantage of their position and become comfortable with the imbalance in regulations on their jobs. We need leaders ready to step up and serve their communities, not pad their stock portfolios and connect with wealthy corporate investors.
I’m running to represent you. I spend my time in our community because it’s my home too, and I want the best for it. Our current representative, Brad Knott, is backed by the extremist current administration, corporate PACs, and bankrolled by wealthy family members. I am running this campaign on the support of grassroots donations, because I answer to you, our community.
Will you donate to help me beat Brad Knott this November, and bring more common sense back to Washington? The Trump administration has been a disaster for our nation, and Republicans in Congress have just sat back and supported Trump’s every whim. This includes his call to pass a dangerous, massive anti-voter bill that will make it more difficult for millions of eligible voters to make their voices heard.

Derek, we’ll be upfront about it: This is a fundraising email. When we’re done, we’re going to ask you to [**chip in before our End-of-Month fundraising deadline tonight at midnight.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136391833/637287155/-2014140140?refcode=email_073126_mythfact&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDYvMS84NTY5MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyNmQyYzZhZC0yMThkLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=EoN97T2i2zxSA_Mo8L156B8pmI1kgg6mkaoHovFQxcc=) But before we do that, we want to set the record straight about this campaign — so if there’s a reason why you might be hesitant to pitch in today, we want to dispel a few myths you may have heard about our election. **Myth #1: “The polls show Josh Shapiro ahead, so clearly he’s going to win.”** Derek, if there’s anything we’ve learned from the past few elections, it’s that you can _never_ trust what the polls say — especially in Pennsylvania. | | Hi Peter,

Today is a special day for my family.

**My parents, Keith and Nancy, are celebrating their 56th wedding anniversary.**

Growing up, I was blessed to watch two people who built a life together rooted in _faith, hard work, and love_ for one another.

They taught me that the strongest foundations are built on commitment, sacrifice, and putting family first.

**To me, their story is an Arkansas love story.**

Everything I do is shaped by the lessons they taught me around the kitchen table and by the example they've set over the past 56 years.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/10KdPVXW3qs?e=624a44d946&c2id=f3183fbb44b13f86f374b3da2b3069f5)
---
| _Keith and Nancy on their wedding day._
Fifty-six years later, they're still the same couple who believed in each other, believed in God, and believed in the promise of Arkansas.
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/lSER4e8I2R8?e=624a44d946&c2id=f3183fbb44b13f86f374b3da2b3069f5)
---
| _Celebrating 56 wonderful years together._
**To celebrate their anniversary, I'm asking 56 supporters to make a[$56 contribution in honor of their 56 years of marriage](https://us.list-manage.com/ujjVpVCVFNk?e=624a44d946&c2id=f3183fbb44b13f86f374b3da2b3069f5).**

It would mean so much to me to celebrate this milestone by continuing the work they inspired me to do.
---
| [>>> GIVE $56 FOR 56 YEARS ](https://us.list-manage.com/NGQkTujaQOm?e=624a44d946&c2id=f3183fbb44b13f86f374b3da2b3069f5 ">>> GIVE $56 FOR 56 YEARS ")

| Thank you for celebrating this special day with my family. I hope you'll join me in wishing my parents a happy anniversary.

\- Leslie

name: Wes Moore
subject: This team does not back down from a fight
body:
Let me be crystal clear.
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1687%2E1086043%2E2wBm6L)
Hi Peter — it’s Wes.
I wanted to reach out to you one final time before our end-of-month deadline tonight.
**[Before midnight, will you pitch in $5 to our campaign? Every donation helps fight back against our MAGA opponent’s attacks.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260731-2.hm6uTl&refcode=em-20260731-2&t=2&akid=1687%2E1086043%2E2wBm6L)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260731-2.hm6uTl&amount=5&refcode=em-20260731-2&t=21&akid=1687%2E1086043%2E2wBm6L)**
Let me be crystal clear, Peter: Dan Cox, Donald Trump, and national Republicans would love to make me a one-term Governor.
They’re afraid of the results we’ve delivered for Maryland. From making our communities safer to investing in public education, Republicans are trying to roll it all back.
But here’s what else I know, Peter: **This team does not back down from a fight. If they want to tear down our accomplishments, let them try.**
These last few hours are critical. It’s our last shot to bring in the resources we need to stay competitive. There’s no catching up, and no re-do. Your $10 or $25 today has a huge impact — because with less than 100 days to go, we have to keep up the pace every day.
**[If you want to defend this seat this fall, I’m asking you to chip in $10 or $25 right now. Every dollar we raise now will help us fight whatever Republicans throw at us the next few weeks.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260731-2.hm6uTl&refcode=em-20260731-2&t=22&akid=1687%2E1086043%2E2wBm6L)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260731-2.hm6uTl&amount=5&refcode=em-20260731-2&t=23&akid=1687%2E1086043%2E2wBm6L)**
Let’s run through the tape, Peter. The finish line is just a few hours away.
Elevate,
Wes
[ ](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260731-2.hm6uTl&refcode=em-20260731-2&t=24&akid=1687%2E1086043%2E2wBm6L)

* * *
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wes-em-footer?refcode=em-20260731-2&t=25&refcode2=1687_1086043_2wBm6L&akid=1687%2E1086043%2E2wBm6L)**
**[Volunteer »](https://support.wesmoore.com/a/volunteer?source=em-20260731-2)**
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a critical way we communicate with grassroots supporters like you. However, if you would like to change your subscription preferences, here are some options:
* [Receive Fewer Emails](https://act.wesmoore.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails/?t=26&akid=1687%2E1086043%2E2wBm6L)
* [Update Your Information](https://act.wesmoore.com/signup/update-your-information/)
* [Unsubscribe](https://act.wesmoore.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?t=27&akid=1687%2E1086043%2E2wBm6L)

Email us: [info@wesmoore.com](mailto:info@wesmoore.com)
BY AUTHORITY: WES MOORE FOR MARYLAND, MARY TYDINGS, TREASURER

Hi team,
We have a lot of empty wall space at our new office, and we want your help to decorate it.
**[If you chip in before our end-of-month deadline at midnight, we 'll put your name on the wall at campaign HQ.](https://substack.com/redirect/34be14f5-f561-427a-9d4a-3de9b94889bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[PUT YOUR NAME ON THE WALL](https://substack.com/redirect/34be14f5-f561-427a-9d4a-3de9b94889bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The _Republican Herald_ described our office as "honest, no frills" and "a true reflection of grassroots politics." That's exactly right.
Our office is the home of our campaign. There's no better way to decorate it than with a show of appreciation for the people who make it possible.
We're not hosting flashy Mar-a-Lago fundraisers or sucking up to billionaire donors like Dan Meuser. This campaign is built by people like you. Because you're who I'm fighting for.
**And I 'm really counting on your support today. Hitting our end-of-month goal means we can keep organizing, keep reaching voters, and keep showing up in every corner of our part of PA.**
**[Will you chip in before midnight and let us put your name on the grassroots donor wall at campaign HQ?](https://substack.com/redirect/34be14f5-f561-427a-9d4a-3de9b94889bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ CHIP IN NOW](https://substack.com/redirect/34be14f5-f561-427a-9d4a-3de9b94889bf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Every time I walk into our office, I think about all of the people who believe our part of PA deserves better and step up to fight for it. This wall will be another reminder of who our campaign is all about.
- Rachel Wallace

Team, Republicans officially nominated Warren Petersen to run against me for Attorney General. I want to be direct with you about who he is and why he's dangerous. Warren Petersen spent years spreading lies about the 2020 election. He was a driving force behind the sham "audit" of Maricopa County's ballots — the one that dragged on for months, humiliated our state, and still confirmed the results. He knows there was no fraud. He has known it for years. And he has never stopped lying about it. Just this year, he handed Arizona's 2020 election records over to the Trump administration's so-called election "probe" — a weaponization of federal law enforcement in service of crackpots and conspiracy theories. Now think about what's coming: in 2028, Arizona will once again help decide the presidency. The Attorney General stands alongside the Governor and Secretary of State when our state certifies its results — and it's the Attorney General's office that defends Arizona's elections in court when they come under attack. Warren Petersen wants to be in that seat, holding that power, when the 2028 results come in. That should terrify every Arizonan who believes voters — not politicians — decide our elections. [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=8052%2E582294%2EdBF24h ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=8052%2E582294%2EdBF24h ]Chris Pappas for Senate

If there’s one thing Republicans can’t stand, it’s an election they can’t
buy.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260731_3.CgSHqc&refcode=em20260731-3&t=1003&akid=8052%2E582294%2EdBF24h ]FIGHT BACK: CHIP IN NOW »

Their strategy is clear: pour as much cash into New
Hampshire as they possibly can to flip our state red.

And it’s working.

The GOP is dumping over $25 million onto the airwaves, and now their
investments are starting to pay off. Polls are showing me tied with John
Sununu.

We have to change the tide of this race, and I’m relying on grassroots
support from people like you: the people who believe the Granite State is
not for sale.

I don’t accept a cent of corporate PAC money, because they don’t represent
New Hampshire values. We might not match them dollar-for-dollar, but we
can turn this trend around if we fight back together.

If you’ve been waiting for your chance to step up
for the first time,
now’s your chance. [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260731_3.CgSHqc&refcode=em20260731-3&t=1004&akid=8052%2E582294%2EdBF24h ]Please, make a donation of

I’m humbly asking you, before my primary election, can you rush a gift of any amount to give my campaign the resources it needs to get over the finish line? The next few days will decide everything. This race is too important to leave anything on the table. We’ve fought too hard to risk coming up short because we didn’t have the resources when it mattered most. Politics is about more than one speech, one endorsement, or one day at a convention. It's about earning trust over time.
When the Republican convention concluded, there were strong feelings on every side. James "Jamie" Millington gave the nomination speech for my opponent, and it was clear we had different views about the direction of this race.
But something important happened after the convention.
Jamie watched.
He watched me show up at Republican town committees, community events, and local gatherings across the Fourth District. He watched me answer difficult questions, engage directly with voters, and remain accessible on social media. He watched me continue to work every day--not because it was easy, but because Connecticut deserves a representative who will never stop fighting.
Most importantly, he saw persistence.
Persistence is often missing from congressional campaigns. Elections cannot be won by showing up only at election time. They are won by earning trust, being present, listening, and demonstrating that you're willing to put in the work every single day.
That is why Jamie's endorsement means so much to me.
It represents something larger than one individual supporting one candidate. It reflects the idea that Republicans can unite after a primary and focus on what really matters: winning in November and delivering results for Connecticut.
My motivation for running has never changed.
As both a physician and an attorney, I want to bring decades of real-world experience to Washington. At the same time, I intend to use this campaign as a platform to give Connecticut a stronger voice in Washington.
That is exactly what we've already begun doing.
We've been reaching out to federal officials, including EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin and Energy Secretary Chris Wright, to advocate for policies that will lower energy costs, improve affordability, and create economic opportunity for Connecticut. Our outreach on energy policy didn't begin yesterday--it has been an ongoing effort because I believe our state's affordability crisis requires leadership at the federal level.
Our campaign has always been built around one simple idea:
**Federal solutions to local problems.**
Whether it's healthcare, energy, affordability, workforce development, or protecting Long Island Sound, Connecticut deserves someone who is willing to engage directly with federal decision-makers instead of simply talking about problems.
It is even more powerful when local Republican leaders unite behind that mission.
Jamie's endorsement is not just a personal honor--it is another sign that our party is coming together.
Now it's time to build on that momentum.
**Early voting begins Monday, August 3, and continues through August 9. Republican Primary Day is Tuesday, August 11.**
Let's show Connecticut--and show our opponents--that while they remain divided, Republicans are united, energized, and ready to compete all the way through November.
I am fighting for Connecticut.
I am fighting for this country.
And, most importantly, **I am fighting for you.**
**Dr. Michael Goldstein**
Republican-Endorsed Candidate for Congress
Connecticut's 4th District

It's about earning trust over time. When the Republican convention concluded, there were strong feelings on every side. James "Jamie" Millington gave the nomination speech for my opponent, and it was clear we had different views about the direction of this race. But something important happened after the convention. Jamie watched. He watched me show up at Republican town committees, community events, and local gatherings across the Fourth District. He watched me answer difficult questions, engage directly with voters, and remain accessible on social media. He watched me continue to work every day--not because it was easy, but because Connecticut deserves a representative who will never stop fighting. Most importantly, he saw persistence. Persistence is often missing from congressional campaigns. Elections cannot be won by showing up only at election time. They are won by earning trust, being present, listening, and demonstrating that you're willing to put in the work every single day. That is why Jamie's endorsement means so much to me. It represents something larger than one individual supporting one candidate. It reflects the idea that Republicans can unite after a primary and focus on what really matters: winning in November and delivering results for Connecticut. My motivation for running has never changed. As both a physician and an attorney, I want to bring decades of real-world experience to Washington. At the same time, I intend to use this campaign as a platform to give Connecticut a stronger voice in Washington. That is exactly what we've already begun doing. We've been reaching out to federal officials, including EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin and Energy Secretary Chris Wright, to advocate for policies that will lower energy costs, improve affordability, and create economic opportunity for Connecticut. Our outreach on energy policy didn't begin yesterday--it has been an ongoing effort because I believe our state's affordability crisis requires leadership at the federal level. Our campaign has always been built around one simple idea: Federal solutions to local problems. Whether it's healthcare, energy, affordability, workforce development, or protecting Long Island Sound, Connecticut deserves someone who is willing to engage directly with federal decision-makers instead of simply talking about problems. It is even more powerful when local Republican leaders unite behind that mission. Jamie's endorsement is not just a personal honor--it is another sign that our party is coming together. Now it's time to build on that momentum. Early voting begins Monday, August 3, and continues through August 9. Republican Primary Day is Tuesday, August 11. Let's show Connecticut--and show our opponents--that while they remain divided, Republicans are united, energized, and ready to compete all the way through November. I am fighting for Connecticut. I am fighting for this country. And, most importantly, I am fighting for you. ## Amy Acton and a Primary Process That Failed Ohio Democrats
Erin In The Morning
[Dem. Ohio Gov Candidate Amy Acton Scheduled a Meeting With LGBTQ+ Advocates, Didn't Show Up, And Kicked Out Trans People Who Did](https://substack.com/redirect/73732567-86ff-4e85-8f58-46fe8a58d365?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

[Read more](https://substack.com/redirect/73732567-86ff-4e85-8f58-46fe8a58d365?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
a day ago * 564 likes * 66 comments * Erin Reed
The first story is Amy Acton and the growing conflict between her campaign and Ohio's LGBTQIA+ community. What interests me most about this controversy is what it reveals about our broken political process.
I have been ranting about this for a long time: Democrats do not seem to like democracy nearly as much as they claim.
Amy Acton became the Democratic nominee for governor without having to survive a real primary. Other people considered running. Potential candidates were pushed aside. Party leaders, donors, elected officials, and political organizations put their thumbs on the scale because they decided Acton should be the nominee.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/93b4606e-7d06-470a-b460-69a6258e49ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That meant Democratic voters never got a meaningful campaign in which candidates were forced to explain their ideas, defend their records, show their character, and tell Ohioans what they would actually do as governor.
Now, fewer than 100 days before the general election, we are still learning basic things about both candidates.
Vivek Ramaswamy flying around in a private jet, spending substantial time outside Ohio, saying crazy things, and blaming ordinary people for their failures while he lives as a multi-billionaire is ridiculous. But Ramaswamy being ridiculous does not take responsibility from Amy Acton.
Acton's short, pithy plans and lack of detailed policy have already frustrated some voters and members of the media. Her recent comments about transgender athletes have now created a much deeper problem.
Acton endorsed restrictions on transgender participation in sports and referred to transgender girls as "boys." Members of Ohio's LGBTQIA+ community wanted an apology, a clarification, or some indication that she understood why they were angry. Her campaign scheduled what was presented as a listening session with LGBTQIA+ advocates.
**Acton did not attend.**
According to reporting by Erin Reed, the situation became worse from there. Arienne Childrey, vice chair of the Ohio Democratic Party Pride Caucus, a transgender candidate for the Ohio House, and Ohio's first openly transgender city council member, was reportedly barred from entering the Zoom meeting. Advocate Ciara Keeton was removed after asking why Childrey had been excluded. Kim McCarthy, chair of the Progressive Caucus, was reportedly left in the waiting room for the entire session.
Childrey said she was eventually able to speak only because Pride Caucus Chair Kyle Herman called her personal phone and put her on speakerphone inside the meeting.
The meeting opened with Equality Ohio rescinding Acton's "A" rating on its LGBTQIA+ candidate scorecard. When participants pressed campaign manager Philip Stein about why certain advocates had been excluded, he reportedly said the event was "mostly a space we want to listen to the folks that we picked here." At the end, the campaign offered no retraction, no specific next step, and no commitment that Acton would meet directly with the people who had been excluded.
**Here is the point: this may simply be what Amy Acton believes.**
People are demanding that she make amends or say something different, but she may genuinely believe transgender athletes should not compete in sports associated with their gender identity. I am not making a value judgment on that position in this article. I am saying Democratic voters should have learned about it during a competitive primary, when Acton could have been questioned, challenged, and compared with other candidates.
Instead, party leaders avoided that debate. Now the ideological disagreement is exploding fewer than 100 days before an election that Democrats describe as an existential fight for democracy.
Ideas should have been fleshed out. Candidates should have debated. Democratic voters should have been allowed to decide whether Amy Acton represented them before the party effectively handed her the nomination.
This should never have gotten this far.

## "Daddy's House Is Scary" and the Allegations Against Max Miller
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..s1fyNI9lWmJxWobObUkPHO8RhVeIhFvfKEifn8gepwk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=209282199)
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..s1fyNI9lWmJxWobObUkPHO8RhVeIhFvfKEifn8gepwk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=209282199)
The second story is the continuing implosion of Rep. Max Miller's personal life.
**[I want to be precise about this: these are allegations. Allegations are not proof, and repeating an accusation does not make it true.](https://substack.com/redirect/2f47215f-b43a-4f2c-8328-2a151a2e5818?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/60cff642-0258-46e9-9a5f-a5fc36a5da42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Congressman Max "hot water" Miller
As of Friday, July 31, the allegations involving Miller and his ex-wife, Emily Moreno Miller, had not been proven in court. Photographs reportedly showing red skin on her stomach do not, by themselves, prove her allegation that Miller threw boiling water on her. The involvement of child-services agencies or other authorities also does not establish that abuse occurred.
We should not pretend otherwise.
But we also should not ignore the pattern of accusations surrounding Miller. His ex-wife has alleged that he threw boiling water at her, assaulted and bruised her, held a gun to her head, pushed her against a wall, and slapped her. Their daughter reportedly suffered a broken collarbone and allegedly told her mother, "**Daddy 's house is scary."** Miller has denied allegations of abuse.
These are not the first accusations involving his behavior. Former White House press secretary Stephanie Grisham wrote that Miller slapped her during their relationship. A former college classmate accused him of assaulting her during what she described as one of the most traumatic nights of her life. Other allegations about aggressive behavior have followed him since he was young.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b3ef02c6-97f8-437f-9c55-157e7184233e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Again, none of that means every allegation is true. But when accusations involving similar behavior emerge from multiple people across more than a decade, voters are allowed to take the pattern seriously.
Maybe the correct response is for Max Miller to step away, deal with his personal life, and get his shit together while somebody else represents Ohio's 7th District in Congress.
The district's Republican lean does not require voters to give Miller a safe seat. Character still counts. Voters show their own character through the behavior they are willing to accept from the people they elect.
If the accusations are false and Miller is ultimately exonerated, he can make that case publicly and run again. But while allegations this serious remain unresolved, Ohioans are not obligated to act as if nothing happened.

## America Is Losing Its Greatest Minds
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..s1fyNI9lWmJxWobObUkPHO8RhVeIhFvfKEifn8gepwk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=209282199)
Another thing on my mind this week was a video from Neil deGrasse Tyson's _StarTalk_ about America losing some of its greatest minds.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/1490867c-380d-4476-99ba-29bbca09dc55?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The argument itself is not new. The United States has weakened the incentives for young people to enter science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and research. We have reduced funding, attacked the credibility of scientists, and forgotten how discoveries in one field can transform industries that appear completely unrelated.
Cuts to scientific and medical research do not remain isolated inside a university or government agency. Work supported through the National Institutes of Health, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, NASA, and other institutions feeds into medicine, manufacturing, national security, technology, communications, and the broader economy.
We often seem willing to invest in science only when the government wants to flex American power. We fund a race to the Moon, a military objective, or some high-profile national goal. What we have failed to maintain is the larger ecosystem that allows researchers to pursue ideas before anyone knows exactly where those ideas will lead.
**This is becoming more than a research problem. It is a cultural problem.**
The United States increasingly imports instead of creates. We manufacture abroad and import the goods. We weaken our own scientific pipeline and then rely on researchers and scientists trained in other countries to fill the gaps here.
Bringing talented people to the United States is not the problem. America has always benefited from attracting smart, ambitious people from around the world. The problem is that we are failing to cultivate enough of that talent ourselves.
If we keep moving in this direction, the only thing Americans will be expected to do is scroll, consume, and purchase while other countries innovate, research, create, and manufacture.
That is not an economy capable of leading the world.

## Chris Ronayne, Courtney Scheff, and an Obvious Conflict
Moving closer to home, a conflict has emerged in the Cuyahoga County Council District 5 race between Democrat Courtney Scheff and Republican incumbent Michael Gallagher.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f490e388-481d-4fa0-b39c-3575aadb9527?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
County Executive Chris Ronayne's campaign committee contributed $5,000 to Scheff's campaign. Ronayne is also hosting a fundraiser for her that could bring in thousands more.
None of this appears to be illegal. Elected officials routinely use campaign funds to support other candidates. But legality is not the only standard we should apply to political conduct.
I have written about this race multiple times and said many positive things about Courtney. She is intelligent, accomplished, and has an impressive background. I have spoken with her several times. I have also said positive things about Gallagher's role as a check on the county executive.
The Angry Ohioans
[Cuyahoga County Council District 5: Courtney Scheff vs. Michael Gallagher](https://substack.com/redirect/d75b529c-c3a9-4a36-91ee-3903d0048483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Edit: Mike Gallagher made a website a couple weeks after this article came out. You can find his and Courtney's websites linked by their names below...
[Read more](https://substack.com/redirect/d75b529c-c3a9-4a36-91ee-3903d0048483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
21 days ago * The Angry Democrat, Matt Diemer, and Laura Rodriguez-Carbone
That check is exactly what concerns me.
The county executive is helping finance the campaign of someone who, if elected, will sit on the council responsible for overseeing his administration. Ronayne may call it coalition building. I see an executive helping elect a potential rubber stamp.
If Ronayne's money and political network help Scheff win, how much meaningful pushback will she be willing to give him once she is on council? That does not mean she will vote with him on everything. It means voters have a legitimate reason to question the relationship.
I think Scheff is favored to win. Strongsville remains Gallagher's strongest Republican base, while Democratic turnout across the rest of the district could carry her comfortably.
But I am bothered by the conflict, and I am more bothered that so few people appear willing to acknowledge it. A county council member should provide oversight of the executive branch, not owe her election to it.

## [East Cleveland Will Not Tell the Public How Many Police Officers It Has](https://substack.com/redirect/7b372b5e-7f1d-4011-bbfd-53a9f1998a52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..s1fyNI9lWmJxWobObUkPHO8RhVeIhFvfKEifn8gepwk?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=209282199)
The final political story on my mind is East Cleveland.
Online reports claimed the city was down to four active patrol officers and one detective. East Cleveland officials denied those numbers, but then refused to tell the public how many officers the department actually employs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/59d0886a-86b1-406f-a981-bd4726e39bc2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[https://www.ideastream.org/law-justice/2026-07-29/east-cleveland-refuses-to-say-how-many-police-officers-it-employs](https://substack.com/redirect/7b372b5e-7f1d-4011-bbfd-53a9f1998a52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Mayor Sandra Morgan and Law Director Ken Myers said the city could not disclose "specific tactical staffing numbers" for security reasons. But according to the Ohio Attorney General's 2026 _Sunshine Laws Manual_ , public offices are required to maintain a public database or list containing the names of their officials and employees.
Officials cannot dismiss public reporting as false while refusing to provide the number they claim is correct.
Ideastream reported that News 5 Cleveland had identified six active-duty patrol officers, which would amount to roughly two officers per shift. Ideastream said one of its own sources had heard the same number. The Cuyahoga County Sheriff's Department is providing limited weekend support, but the county says its deputies are not the primary agency responding to 911 calls and do not replace East Cleveland's patrol function.
The mayor later reportedly said the department had 16 officers. Even if that number is accurate, two were reportedly on sick leave and another was involved in a legal matter, leaving approximately 13 available. That is still an alarmingly small force for a city that requires coverage 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
The administration's response has been deflection followed by non-transparency. First, officials said the online numbers were wrong. Then they refused to release the actual number. Then a larger number was offered without acknowledging that even this staffing level appears dangerously inadequate.
You can find the discussion in the below podcast by Cleveland dot com. Around the 31 minute mark.
[| Today in Ohio, July 31, 2026 Congressman Max Miller could face ethics investigation. Do voters care?cleveland.comEpisode
---|---](https://substack.com/redirect/fda16178-5690-46b2-acb1-be6d178f8cb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This comes after years of scandal inside the department. More than a dozen East Cleveland officers have been convicted of crimes including bribery, assault, and robbery during the past five years. Former Police Chief Kenneth Lundy is facing 31 criminal charges. The city's finances are under state control through receivership, and the state auditor previously cited East Cleveland's failure to produce records needed to complete audits.
This is not one isolated staffing shortage inherited by a new administration. It is a systemic collapse in governance, accountability, public safety, and trust.
When officials refuse to provide basic information, people will speculate. That is not the public's fault. It is the predictable result of a government that demands trust while refusing transparency.
**Shame on you, Mayor Morgan. Shame on you.**

## What I Watched This Week

As you know, I love movies. I try to watch two or three each week, although I usually watch them the way most people watch television. I stop after an hour, go to bed, and finish them over the next day or two.
The first movie this week was _Mortal Kombat II_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d40bf73c-732d-434e-9c78-0a9dba9baf81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As someone who grew up in the 1980s and 1990s, _Mortal Kombat_ is legendary. The video game is a classic, but we have still never received a truly great movie adaptation. The previous movie was decent and finally put some of our favorite characters on screen. The sequel gives us even more of that.
It is hokey. It is bad. But if you want to see the characters you remember from the games, it does a decent job.
**I give it a 5 out of 10 .... uuuhhhhgggg maybe 4.5/10. **
I also watched _Masters of the Universe_ , another piece of 1980s nostalgia.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/890d1006-46b2-400c-ae49-4e786962649e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Again, it was horrible.** The dialogue was bad. The action was bad. The jokes and the entire script was a script and formula we has seen 100 times already.
But it had the nostalgia. It included the characters, and from what I remember of the cartoon, many of them looked pretty good. I wish they had included Man-E-Faces, the character whose face rotates among different identities. He always reminded of the Face Dancers from _Dune_.
Jared Leto was also fun as Skeletor. He played him as a quirky, narcissistic egomaniac, which worked better than most of the movie around him.
**Still, I give it a 5 out of 10. Maybe less.**
Both movies sucked, but I powered through them. Took me about 2 days each.
Those are the stories and ideas that were on my mind this week. Leave your thoughts below and tell us what you believed was the most important story of the week.

Democrats Non-Primaries Abandon LGBTQIA+ Community, Max Miller's House is Scary, and East Cleveland's Police Crisis | | | Jul 31 | | | | | | | | | | | | Hey, Angry Patriots! Welcome to another week of The Angry Files , where we take the stories and ideas that have been on our minds throughout the week and put them together in one place. This feels like the first week when the midterm elections are actually beginning to ramp up. We are now fewer than 100 days from Election Day. I do not think the real crunch begins until the end of August or sometime in September, but the direction of these races is starting to become clearer. Here is what has been on my mind this week. | | ---|---|--- Amy Acton and a Primary Process That Failed Ohio Democrats Erin In The Morning a day ago 564 likes 66 comments Erin Reed The first story is Amy Acton and the growing conflict between her campaign and Ohio's LGBTQIA+ community. What interests me most about this controversy is what it reveals about our broken political process. I have been ranting about this for a long time: Democrats do not seem to like democracy nearly as much as they claim. Amy Acton became the Democratic nominee for governor without having to survive a real primary. Other people considered running. Potential candidates were pushed aside. Party leaders, donors, elected officials, and political organizations put their thumbs on the scale because they decided Acton should be the nominee. | | ---|---|--- That meant Democratic voters never got a meaningful campaign in which candidates were forced to explain their ideas, defend their records, show their character, and tell Ohioans what they would actually do as governor. Now, fewer than 100 days before the general election, we are still learning basic things about both candidates. Vivek Ramaswamy flying around in a private jet, spending substantial time outside Ohio, saying crazy things, and blaming ordinary people for their failures while he lives as a multi-billionaire is ridiculous. But Ramaswamy being ridiculous does not take responsibility from Amy Acton. Acton's short, pithy plans and lack of detailed policy have already frustrated some voters and members of the media. Her recent comments about transgender athletes have now created a much deeper problem. Acton endorsed restrictions on transgender participation in sports and referred to transgender girls as "boys." Members of Ohio's LGBTQIA+ community wanted an apology, a clarification, or some indication that she understood why they were angry. Her campaign scheduled what was presented as a listening session with LGBTQIA+ advocates. Acton did not attend. According to reporting by Erin Reed, the situation became worse from there. Arienne Childrey, vice chair of the Ohio Democratic Party Pride Caucus, a transgender candidate for the Ohio House, and Ohio's first openly transgender city council member, was reportedly barred from entering the Zoom meeting. Advocate Ciara Keeton was removed after asking why Childrey had been excluded. Kim McCarthy, chair of the Progressive Caucus, was reportedly left in the waiting room for the entire session. Childrey said she was eventually able to speak only because Pride Caucus Chair Kyle Herman called her personal phone and put her on speakerphone inside the meeting. The meeting opened with Equality Ohio rescinding Acton's "A" rating on its LGBTQIA+ candidate scorecard. When participants pressed campaign manager Philip Stein about why certain advocates had been excluded, he reportedly said the event was "mostly a space we want to listen to the folks that we picked here." At the end, the campaign offered no retraction, no specific next step, and no commitment that Acton would meet directly with the people who had been excluded. Here is the point: this may simply be what Amy Acton believes. People are demanding that she make amends or say something different, but she may genuinely believe transgender athletes should not compete in sports associated with their gender identity. I am not making a value judgment on that position in this article. I am saying Democratic voters should have learned about it during a competitive primary, when Acton could have been questioned, challenged, and compared with other candidates. Instead, party leaders avoided that debate. Now the ideological disagreement is exploding fewer than 100 days before an election that Democrats describe as an existential fight for democracy. Ideas should have been fleshed out. Candidates should have debated. Democratic voters should have been allowed to decide whether Amy Acton represented them before the party effectively handed her the nomination. This should never have gotten this far. "Daddy's House Is Scary" and the Allegations Against Max Miller The second story is the continuing implosion of Rep. Max Miller's personal life. | | ---|---|--- Congressman Max "hot water" Miller As of Friday, July 31, the allegations involving Miller and his ex-wife, Emily Moreno Miller, had not been proven in court. Photographs reportedly showing red skin on her stomach do not, by themselves, prove her allegation that Miller threw boiling water on her. The involvement of child-services agencies or other authorities also does not establish that abuse occurred. We should not pretend otherwise. But we also should not ignore the pattern of accusations surrounding Miller. His ex-wife has alleged that he threw boiling water at her, assaulted and bruised her, held a gun to her head, pushed her against a wall, and slapped her. Their daughter reportedly suffered a broken collarbone and allegedly told her mother, "Daddy 's house is scary." Miller has denied allegations of abuse. These are not the first accusations involving his behavior. Former White House press secretary Stephanie Grisham wrote that Miller slapped her during their relationship. A former college classmate accused him of assaulting her during what she described as one of the most traumatic nights of her life. Other allegations about aggressive behavior have followed him since he was young. Again, none of that means every allegation is true. But when accusations involving similar behavior emerge from multiple people across more than a decade, voters are allowed to take the pattern seriously. Maybe the correct response is for Max Miller to step away, deal with his personal life, and get his shit together while somebody else represents Ohio's 7th District in Congress. The district's Republican lean does not require voters to give Miller a safe seat. Character still counts. Voters show their own character through the behavior they are willing to accept from the people they elect. If the accusations are false and Miller is ultimately exonerated, he can make that case publicly and run again. But while allegations this serious remain unresolved, Ohioans are not obligated to act as if nothing happened. America Is Losing Its Greatest Minds Another thing on my mind this week was a video from Neil deGrasse Tyson's StarTalk about America losing some of its greatest minds. The argument itself is not new. The United States has weakened the incentives for young people to enter science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and research. We have reduced funding, attacked the credibility of scientists, and forgotten how discoveries in one field can transform industries that appear completely unrelated. Cuts to scientific and medical research do not remain isolated inside a university or government agency. Work supported through the National Institutes of Health, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, NASA, and other institutions feeds into medicine, manufacturing, national security, technology, communications, and the broader economy. We often seem willing to invest in science only when the government wants to flex American power. We fund a race to the Moon, a military objective, or some high-profile national goal. What we have failed to maintain is the larger ecosystem that allows researchers to pursue ideas before anyone knows exactly where those ideas will lead. This is becoming more than a research problem. It is a cultural problem. The United States increasingly imports instead of creates. We manufacture abroad and import the goods. We weaken our own scientific pipeline and then rely on researchers and scientists trained in other countries to fill the gaps here. Bringing talented people to the United States is not the problem. America has always benefited from attracting smart, ambitious people from around the world. The problem is that we are failing to cultivate enough of that talent ourselves. If we keep moving in this direction, the only thing Americans will be expected to do is scroll, consume, and purchase while other countries innovate, research, create, and manufacture. That is not an economy capable of leading the world. The DNC Is Mortgaging Its Future Laura Rodriguez-Carbone wrote this week about the Democratic National Committee mortgaging its headquarters while trying to pay for elections. Her article examines the growing financial gap between the DNC, the Republican National Committee, and Donald Trump's MAGA Inc. super PAC as we approach the midterms. The Whisper Campaign A few months ago, I wrote about widespread concerns within the DNC about fundraising and we are now getting a clearer look at how bad the party's financial picture actually is... 2 days ago 2 likes Laura Rodriguez-Carbone Democratic leaders continue to tell us this election is all or nothing. If Democrats lose, they warn, American democracy itself may not survive. If that is true, it seems strange that the Democratic Party is entering the fight millions of dollars in debt. But this is not new. Democratic organizations have repeatedly operated in the hole and managed their money poorly. We see versions of the same problem in county parties, state parties, and the DNC. Read Laura's full article for the details. But the basic question is simple: if party leaders genuinely believe democracy is on the line, why have they managed the institution responsible for defending it so badly? Chris Ronayne, Courtney Scheff, and an Obvious Conflict Moving closer to home, a conflict has emerged in the Cuyahoga County Council District 5 race between Democrat Courtney Scheff and Republican incumbent Michael Gallagher. | | ---|---|--- County Executive Chris Ronayne's campaign committee contributed $5,000 to Scheff's campaign. Ronayne is also hosting a fundraiser for her that could bring in thousands more. None of this appears to be illegal. Elected officials routinely use campaign funds to support other candidates. But legality is not the only standard we should apply to political conduct. I have written about this race multiple times and said many positive things about Courtney. She is intelligent, accomplished, and has an impressive background. I have spoken with her several times. I have also said positive things about Gallagher's role as a check on the county executive. The Angry Ohioans Edit: Mike Gallagher made a website a couple weeks after this article came out. You can find his and Courtney's websites linked by their names below... 21 days ago The Angry Democrat, Matt Diemer, and Laura Rodriguez-Carbone That check is exactly what concerns me. The county executive is helping finance the campaign of someone who, if elected, will sit on the council responsible for overseeing his administration. Ronayne may call it coalition building. I see an executive helping elect a potential rubber stamp. If Ronayne's money and political network help Scheff win, how much meaningful pushback will she be willing to give him once she is on council? That does not mean she will vote with him on everything. It means voters have a legitimate reason to question the relationship. I think Scheff is favored to win. Strongsville remains Gallagher's strongest Republican base, while Democratic turnout across the rest of the district could carry her comfortably. But I am bothered by the conflict, and I am more bothered that so few people appear willing to acknowledge it. A county council member should provide oversight of the executive branch, not owe her election to it. The final political story on my mind is East Cleveland. Online reports claimed the city was down to four active patrol officers and one detective. East Cleveland officials denied those numbers, but then refused to tell the public how many officers the department actually employs. | | ---|---|--- Mayor Sandra Morgan and Law Director Ken Myers said the city could not disclose "specific tactical staffing numbers" for security reasons. But according to the Ohio Attorney General's 2026 Sunshine Laws Manual , public offices are required to maintain a public database or list containing the names of their officials and employees. Officials cannot dismiss public reporting as false while refusing to provide the number they claim is correct. Ideastream reported that News 5 Cleveland had identified six active-duty patrol officers, which would amount to roughly two officers per shift. Ideastream said one of its own sources had heard the same number. The Cuyahoga County Sheriff's Department is providing limited weekend support, but the county says its deputies are not the primary agency responding to 911 calls and do not replace East Cleveland's patrol function. The mayor later reportedly said the department had 16 officers. Even if that number is accurate, two were reportedly on sick leave and another was involved in a legal matter, leaving approximately 13 available. That is still an alarmingly small force for a city that requires coverage 24 hours a day, seven days a week. The administration's response has been deflection followed by non-transparency. First, officials said the online numbers were wrong. Then they refused to release the actual number. Then a larger number was offered without acknowledging that even this staffing level appears dangerously inadequate. You can find the discussion in the below podcast by Cleveland dot com. Around the 31 minute mark. This comes after years of scandal inside the department. More than a dozen East Cleveland officers have been convicted of crimes including bribery, assault, and robbery during the past five years. Former Police Chief Kenneth Lundy is facing 31 criminal charges. The city's finances are under state control through receivership, and the state auditor previously cited East Cleveland's failure to produce records needed to complete audits. This is not one isolated staffing shortage inherited by a new administration. It is a systemic collapse in governance, accountability, public safety, and trust. When officials refuse to provide basic information, people will speculate. That is not the public's fault. It is the predictable result of a government that demands trust while refusing transparency. Shame on you, Mayor Morgan. Shame on you. What I Watched This Week As you know, I love movies. I try to watch two or three each week, although I usually watch them the way most people watch television. I stop after an hour, go to bed, and finish them over the next day or two. The first movie this week was Mortal Kombat II. | | ---|---|--- As someone who grew up in the 1980s and 1990s, Mortal Kombat is legendary. The video game is a classic, but we have still never received a truly great movie adaptation. The previous movie was decent and finally put some of our favorite characters on screen. The sequel gives us even more of that. It is hokey. It is bad. But if you want to see the characters you remember from the games, it does a decent job. I give it a 5 out of 10 .... uuuhhhhgggg maybe 4.5/10. I also watched Masters of the Universe , another piece of 1980s nostalgia. | | ---|---|--- Again, it was horrible. The dialogue was bad. The action was bad. The jokes and the entire script was a script and formula we has seen 100 times already. But it had the nostalgia. It included the characters, and from what I remember of the cartoon, many of them looked pretty good. I wish they had included Man-E-Faces, the character whose face rotates among different identities. He always reminded of the Face Dancers from Dune. Jared Leto was also fun as Skeletor. He played him as a quirky, narcissistic egomaniac, which worked better than most of the movie around him. Still, I give it a 5 out of 10. Maybe less. Both movies sucked, but I powered through them. Took me about 2 days each. Those are the stories and ideas that were on my mind this week. Leave your thoughts below and tell us what you believed was the most important story of the week. Stay Angry. Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS by supporting Matt's and Laura's work. Subscribe and Share! | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Matt Diemer Berea, Ohio ? ?

On Saturday, the president's media company starts selling early access to his Truth Social posts. Firms that pay will get Trump’s words before you do. That will enable the people who pay him to get information affecting stock prices before you do.
Because his words move markets, on tariffs, on the Fed, on individual stocks he names himself. Reporting puts the early access price at up to $100,000 a month.
_This week I demanded the SEC answer one question before Saturday: how is selling a head start on market-moving information not insider trading?_
We have a good idea how this ends, because we've been watching Trump cash in on the presidency since day one of his second term. When Trump launched his memecoin, more than 810,000 people bought it — most of them his own supporters — and they lost $2 billion while he made $635 million.
**Every one of them trusted him. Every one of them paid dearly for that trust.**
That is the arrangement now: Wall Street pays $100,000 a month for the head start, the president's company banks it whether the trade works or not, whether ordinary consumers or investors in the market get screwed or not.
Yet another way to rig the system against people not wealthy enough to pay off the President.
It's obscene, and it is the whole government now, from the Qatari jet to the ballroom to the contracts going to donors instead of to the best bidder.
None of it stops until there is a Senate willing to stop it. I introduced bills this week to attack conflicts of interest and to tighten our laws against bribery — but not one becomes law unless we win the majority.
